170.s:
brahmovāca
cakṣustīrtham iti khyātaṃ rūpasaubhāgyadāyakam
yatra yogeśvaro devo gautamyā dakṣiṇe taṭe //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
चक्षुस्तीर्थम् इति ख्यातं रूपसौभाग्यदायकम्
यत्र योगेश्वरो देवो गौतम्या दक्षिणे तटे ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
There is a place famous as Cakṣustīrtha, bestowing beauty and good fortune,
where the god Yogeśvara resides on the southern bank of the Gautamī.

170.s:
puraṃ bhauvanam ākhyātaṃ girimūrdhny abhidhīyate
yatrāsau bhauvano rājā kṣatradharmaparāyaṇaḥ //
170.d:
पुरं भौवनम् आख्यातं गिरिमूर्ध्न्य् अभिधीयते
यत्रासौ भौवनो राजा क्षत्रधर्मपरायणः ॥
170.m:
A city named Bhauvana is declared to be on the peak of a mountain,
where that King Bhauvana, devoted to the dharma of the kṣatriya, ruled.

170.s:
tasmin puravare kaścid brāhmaṇo vṛddhakauśikaḥ
tatputro gautama iti khyāto vedaviduttamaḥ //
170.d:
तस्मिन् पुरवरे कश्चिद् ब्राह्मणो वृद्धकौशिकः
तत्पुत्रो गौतम इति ख्यातो वेदविदुत्तमः ॥
170.m:
In that excellent city there was a certain brāhmaṇa named Vṛddhakauśika.
His son, celebrated as Gautama, was the best of knowers of the Veda.

170.s:
tasya mātur manodoṣād viparīto 'bhavad dvijaḥ
sakhā tasya vaṇik kaścin maṇikuṇḍala ucyate //
170.d:
तस्य मातुर् मनोदोषाद् विपरीतो ऽभवद् द्विजः
सखा तस्य वणिक् कश्चिन् मणिकुण्डल उच्यते ॥
170.m:
Due to a mental defect in his mother, the twice-born became perverse.
His friend was a certain merchant named Maṇikuṇḍala.

170.s:
tena sakhyaṃ dvijasyāsīd viṣamaṃ dvijavaiśyayoḥ
śrīmaddaridrayor nityaṃ parasparahitaiṣiṇoḥ //
170.d:
तेन सख्यं द्विजस्यासीद् विषमं द्विजवैश्ययोः
श्रीमद्दरिद्रयोर् नित्यं परस्परहितैषिणोः ॥
170.m:
Between that twice-born and the vaiśya there was friendship, unequal as between
the wealthy and the poor, yet always desiring mutual welfare.

170.s:
kadācid gautamo vaiśyaṃ vitteśaṃ maṇikuṇḍalam
prāhedaṃ vacanaṃ prītyā rahaḥ sthitvā punaḥ punaḥ //
170.d:
कदाचिद् गौतमो वैश्यं वित्तेशं मणिकुण्डलम्
प्राहेदं वचनं प्रीत्या रहः स्थित्वा पुनः पुनः ॥
170.m:
Once Gautama, sitting in secret, repeatedly spoke these words with affection
to the vaiśya Maṇikuṇḍala, who was a lord of wealth:

170.s:
gautama uvāca
gacchāmo dhanam ādātuṃ parvatān udadhīn api
yauvanaṃ tad vṛthā jñeyaṃ vinā saukhyānukūlyataḥ
dhanaṃ vinā tat kathaṃ syād aho dhiṅ nirdhanaṃ naram //
170.d:
गौतम उवाच
गच्छामो धनम् आदातुं पर्वतान् उदधीन् अपि
यौवनं तद् वृथा ज्ञेयं विना सौख्यानुकूल्यतः
धनं विना तत् कथं स्याद् अहो धिङ् निर्धनं नरम् ॥
170.m:
Gautama said:
"Let us go to the mountains and even the oceans to acquire wealth.
That youth is to be regarded as useless which is without the favor of happiness;
how could that be without wealth? Alas, fie on a wealthless man!"

170.s:
brahmovāca
kuṇḍalo dvijam āhedaṃ matpitropārjitaṃ dhanam
bahv asti kiṃ dhanenādya kariṣye dvijasattama
dvijaḥ punar uvācedaṃ maṇikuṇḍalam ojasā //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कुण्डलो द्विजम् आहेदं मत्पित्रोपार्जितं धनम्
बह्व् अस्ति किं धनेनाद्य करिष्ये द्विजसत्तम
द्विजः पुनर् उवाचेदं मणिकुण्डलम् ओजसा ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
Kuṇḍala said this to the twice-born: "The wealth acquired by my father
is abundant; what shall I do with wealth now, O best of the twice-born?"
The twice-born again said this to Maṇikuṇḍala with vigor:

170.s:
gautama uvāca
dharmārthajñānakāmānāṃ ko nu tṛptaḥ praśasyate
utkarṣaprāptir evaiṣāṃ sakhe ślāghyā śarīriṇām //
170.d:
गौतम उवाच
धर्मार्थज्ञानकामानां को नु तृप्तः प्रशस्यते
उत्कर्षप्राप्तिर् एवैषां सखे श्लाघ्या शरीरिणाम् ॥
170.m:
Gautama said:
"Who indeed is praised for being satiated with dharma, wealth, knowledge, and desires?
The attainment of excellence in these alone is praiseworthy for embodied beings, my friend!

170.s:
svenaiva vyavasāyena dhanyā jīvanti jantavaḥ
paradattārthasaṃtuṣṭāḥ kaṣṭajīvina eva te //
170.d:
स्वेनैव व्यवसायेन धन्या जीवन्ति जन्तवः
परदत्तार्थसंतुष्टाः कष्टजीविन एव ते ॥
170.m:
Living beings live blessed only through their own exertion;
those who are satisfied with wealth given by others are indeed living in misery.

170.s:
sa putraḥ śasyate loke pitṛbhiś cābhinandyate
yaḥ paitryam abhilipseta na vācāpi tu kuṇḍala //
170.d:
स पुत्रः शस्यते लोके पितृभिश् चाभिनन्द्यते
यः पैत्र्यम् अभिलिप्सेत न वाचापि तु कुण्डल ॥
170.m:
He is praised as a son in the world and congratulated by his ancestors,
who would not desire ancestral [wealth] even in speech, O Kuṇḍala!

170.s:
svabāhubalam āśritya yo 'rthān arjayate sutaḥ
sa kṛtārtho bhavel loke paitryaṃ vittaṃ na tu spṛśet //
170.d:
स्वबाहुबलम् आश्रित्य यो ऽर्थान् अर्जयते सुतः
स कृतार्थो भवेल् लोके पैत्र्यं वित्तं न तु स्पृशेत् ॥
170.m:
The son who, relying on the strength of his own arms, earns wealth,
he would be successful in the world; he would not touch ancestral wealth.

170.s:
svayam ārjya suto vittaṃ pitre dāsyati bandhave
taṃ tu putraṃ vijānīyād itaro yonikīṭakaḥ //
170.d:
स्वयम् आर्ज्य सुतो वित्तं पित्रे दास्यति बन्धवे
तं तु पुत्रं विजानीयाद् इतरो योनिकीटकः ॥
170.m:
Having earned wealth by himself, the son who will give it to his father and kinsmen—
know him indeed to be a son; any other is merely a worm born from the womb."

170.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā tu tad vākyaṃ brāhmaṇasyābhilāṣiṇaḥ
tatheti matvā tadvākyaṃ ratnāny ādāya satvaraḥ //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा तु तद् वाक्यं ब्राह्मणस्याभिलाषिणः
तथेति मत्वा तद्वाक्यं रत्नान्य् आदाय सत्वरः ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
Having heard those words of the covetous brāhmaṇa,
thinking his words to be 'So be it,' [Maṇikuṇḍala] swiftly took jewels.

170.s:
ātmakīyāni vittāni gautamāya nyavedayat
dhanenaitena deśāṃś ca paribhramya yathāsukham //
170.d:
आत्मकीयानि वित्तानि गौतमाय न्यवेदयत्
धनेनैतेन देशांश् च परिभ्रम्य यथासुखम् ॥
170.m: He entrusted his own wealth to Gautama, [saying,] / “Having wandered through countries with this wealth at will,

170.s:
dhanāny ādāya vittāni punar eṣyāmahe gṛham
satyam eva vaṇig vakti sa tu vipraḥ pratārakaḥ //
170.d:
धनान्य् आदाय वित्तानि पुनर् एष्यामहे गृहम्
सत्यम् एव वणिग् वक्ति स तु विप्रः प्रतारकः ॥
170.m: and acquired riches and wealth, we shall return home.” / The merchant spoke truthfully indeed, but that brahmin was a deceiver.

170.s:
pāpātmā pāpacittaṃ ca na bubodha vaṇig dvijam
tau parasparam āmantrya mātāpitror ajānatoḥ //
170.d:
पापात्मा पापचित्तं च न बुबोध वणिग् द्विजम्
तौ परस्परम् आमन्त्र्य मातापित्रोर् अजानतोः ॥
170.m: The merchant did not realize that the twice-born was an evil soul with an evil mind. / Taking leave of each other without their parents knowing,

170.s:
deśād deśāntaraṃ yātau dhanārthaṃ tau vaṇigdvijau
vaṇigghastasthitaṃ vittaṃ brāhmaṇo hartum icchati //
170.d:
देशाद् देशान्तरं यातौ धनार्थं तौ वणिग्द्विजौ
वणिग्घस्तस्थितं वित्तं ब्राह्मणो हर्तुम् इच्छति ॥
170.m: the two of them, the merchant and the twice-born, went from one land to another for the sake of wealth; / the brahmin wished to steal the wealth in the merchant's possession.

170.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
yena kenāpy upāyena tad dhanaṃ hi samāhare
aho pṛthivyāṃ ramyāṇi nagarāṇi sahasraśaḥ //
170.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
येन केनाप्य् उपायेन तद् धनं हि समाहरे
अहो पृथिव्यां रम्याणि नगराणि सहस्रशः ॥
170.m:
The brāhmaṇa said:
By whatever means, I must indeed seize that wealth. / Ah, there are thousands of delightful cities on earth,

170.s:
iṣṭapradātryaḥ kāmasya devatā iva yoṣitaḥ
manoharās tatra tatra santi kiṃ kriyate mayā //
170.d:
इष्टप्रदात्र्यः कामस्य देवता इव योषितः
मनोहरास् तत्र तत्र सन्ति किं क्रियते मया ॥
170.m: and alluring women everywhere who grant every desire like goddesses; / what am I to do?

170.s:
dhanam āhṛtya yatnena yoṣidbhyo yadi dīyate
bhujyante tās tato nityaṃ saphalaṃ jīvitaṃ hi tat //
170.d:
धनम् आहृत्य यत्नेन योषिद्भ्यो यदि दीयते
भुज्यन्ते तास् ततो नित्यं सफलं जीवितं हि तत् ॥
170.m: If wealth is gathered with effort and given to women, / and they are constantly enjoyed, then indeed life is fruitful.

170.s:
nṛtyagītarato nityaṃ paṇyastrībhir alaṃkṛtaḥ
bhokṣye kathaṃ tu tad vittaṃ vaiśyān maddhastam āgatam //
170.d:
नृत्यगीतरतो नित्यं पण्यस्त्रीभिर् अलंकृतः
भोक्ष्ये कथं तु तद् वित्तं वैश्यान् मद्धस्तम् आगतम् ॥
170.m: Constantly delighting in dance and song, adorned by courtesans, / how may that wealth of the vaiśya come into my hands for my enjoyment?

170.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ cintayamāno 'sau gautamaḥ prahasann iva
maṇikuṇḍalam āhedam adharmād eva jantavaḥ //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं चिन्तयमानो ऽसौ गौतमः प्रहसन्न् इव
मणिकुण्डलम् आहेदम् अधर्माद् एव जन्तवः ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
Reflecting thus, that Gautama, laughing as it were, / said this to Maṇikuṇḍala: “It is solely from unrighteousness that living beings

170.s:
vṛddhiṃ sukham abhīṣṭāni prāpnuvanti na saṃśayaḥ
dharmiṣṭhāḥ prāṇino loke dṛśyante duḥkhabhāginaḥ //
170.d:
वृद्धिं सुखम् अभीष्टानि प्राप्नुवन्ति न संशयः
धर्मिष्ठाः प्राणिनो लोके दृश्यन्ते दुःखभागिनः ॥
170.m: obtain prosperity, pleasure, and desired things, without a doubt. / In the world, righteous creatures are seen to be partakers of sorrow.

170.s: tasmād dharmeṇa kiṃ tena duḥkhaikaphalahetunā //
170.d: तस्माद् धर्मेण किं तेन दुःखैकफलहेतुना ॥
170.m: Therefore, what is the use of that dharma, which causes only sorrow as its fruit?”

170.s:
brahmovāca
nety uvāca tato vaiśyaḥ sukhaṃ dharme pratiṣṭhitam
pāpe duḥkhaṃ bhayaṃ śoko dāridryaṃ kleśa eva ca
yato dharmas tato muktiḥ svadharmaḥ kiṃ vinaśyati //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नेत्य् उवाच ततो वैश्यः सुखं धर्मे प्रतिष्ठितम्
पापे दुःखं भयं शोको दारिद्र्यं क्लेश एव च
यतो धर्मस् ततो मुक्तिः स्वधर्मः किं विनश्यति ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
Then the vaiśya said: “No, happiness is founded upon dharma; / in sin there is sorrow, fear, grief, poverty, and affliction. / Where there is dharma, there is liberation; does one’s own dharma ever perish?”

170.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ vivadatos tatra saṃparāyas tayor abhūt
yasya pakṣo bhavej jyāyān sa parārtham avāpnuyāt //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं विवदतोस् तत्र संपरायस् तयोर् अभूत्
यस्य पक्षो भवेज् ज्यायान् स परार्थम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
As they disputed thus, a wager arose between the two: / he whose position proved superior would obtain the wealth of the other.

170.s:
pṛcchāvaḥ kasya prābalyaṃ dharmiṇo vāpy adharmiṇaḥ
vedāt tu laukikaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ loke dharmāt sukhaṃ bhavet //
170.d:
पृच्छावः कस्य प्राबल्यं धर्मिणो वाप्य् अधर्मिणः
वेदात् तु लौकिकं ज्येष्ठं लोके धर्मात् सुखं भवेत् ॥
170.m: [They said:] “Let us ask whose strength is greater—of the righteous or of the unrighteous. / Conventional consensus is superior even to the Veda; in the world, happiness comes from dharma.”

170.s:
evaṃ vivadamānau tāv ūcatuḥ sakalāñ janān
dharmasya vāpy adharmasya prābalyam anayor bhuvi //
170.d:
एवं विवदमानौ ताव् ऊचतुः सकलाञ् जनान्
धर्मस्य वाप्य् अधर्मस्य प्राबल्यम् अनयोर् भुवि ॥
170.m: Disputing thus, the two of them asked all the people: / “Between dharma and adharma, which of these has greater power on earth?

170.s:
tad vadantu yathāvṛttam evam ūcatur ojasā
evaṃ tatrocire kecid ye dharmeṇānuvartinaḥ //
170.d:
तद् वदन्तु यथावृत्तम् एवम् ऊचतुर् ओजसा
एवं तत्रोचिरे केचिद् ये धर्मेणानुवर्तिनः ॥
170.m: Tell that according to the fact!” Thus they spoke with force. / Then some people there said: “Those who follow dharma,

170.s:
tair duḥkham anubhūyate pāpiṣṭhāḥ sukhino janāḥ
saṃparāye dhanaṃ sarvaṃ jitaṃ vipre nyavedayat //
170.d:
तैर् दुःखम् अनुभूयते पापिष्ठाः सुखिनो जनाः
संपराये धनं सर्वं जितं विप्रे न्यवेदयत् ॥
170.m: sorrow is experienced by them; the most sinful people are happy.” / In the wager, he surrendered all the wealth that had been won to the vipra.

170.s:
maṇimān dharmavicchreṣṭhaḥ punar dharmaṃ praśaṃsati
maṇimantaṃ dvijaḥ prāha kiṃ dharmam anuśaṃsasi
tatheti cety āha vaiśyo brāhmaṇaḥ punar abravīt //
170.d:
मणिमान् धर्मविच्छ्रेष्ठः पुनर् धर्मं प्रशंसति
मणिमन्तं द्विजः प्राह किं धर्मम् अनुशंससि
तथेति चेत्य् आह वैश्यो ब्राह्मणः पुनर् अब्रवीत् ॥
170.m: Maṇimān, the best knower of dharma, praised dharma once again. / The twice-born said to Maṇimān: “Why do you praise dharma?” / The vaiśya said: “Because it is so”; and the brāhmaṇa spoke again.

170.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
jitaṃ mayā dhanaṃ vaiśya nirlajjaḥ kiṃ nu bhāṣase
mayaiva vijito dharmo yatheṣṭacaraṇātmanā //
170.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
जितं मया धनं वैश्य निर्लज्जः किं नु भाषसे
मयैव विजितो धर्मो यथेष्टचरणात्मना ॥
170.m:
The brāhmaṇa said:
“The wealth has been won by me, O vaiśya! Why do you speak shamelessly? / Dharma has indeed been conquered by me, whose nature is to act as I please.”

170.s:
brahmovāca
tad brāhmaṇavacaḥ śrutvā vaiśyaḥ sasmita ūcivān //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् ब्राह्मणवचः श्रुत्वा वैश्यः सस्मित ऊचिवान् ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
Hearing those words of the brāhmaṇa, the vaiśya spoke with a smile.

170.s:
vaiśya uvāca
pulākā iva dhānyeṣu puttikā iva pakṣiṣu
tathaiva tān sakhe manye yeṣāṃ dharmo na vidyate //
170.d:
वैश्य उवाच
पुलाका इव धान्येषु पुत्तिका इव पक्षिषु
तथैव तान् सखे मन्ये येषां धर्मो न विद्यते ॥
170.m:
The vaiśya said:
“Like empty husks among grains, like gnats among birds, / just so, my friend, I regard those who have no dharma.

170.s:
caturṇāṃ puruṣārthānāṃ dharmaḥ prathama ucyate
paścād arthaś ca kāmaś ca sa dharmo mayi tiṣṭhati
kathaṃ brūṣe dvijaśreṣṭha mayā vijitam ity adaḥ //
170.d:
चतुर्णां पुरुषार्थानां धर्मः प्रथम उच्यते
पश्चाद् अर्थश् च कामश् च स धर्मो मयि तिष्ठति
कथं ब्रूषे द्विजश्रेष्ठ मया विजितम् इत्य् अदः ॥
170.m: Among the four aims of human life, dharma is said to be the first; / thereafter come wealth and pleasure; and that dharma abides in me. / How do you say, O best of twice-born, ‘This has been conquered by me’?”

170.s:
brahmovāca
dvijo vaiśyaṃ punaḥ prāha hastābhyāṃ jāyatāṃ paṇaḥ
tatheti manyate vaiśyas tau gatvā punar ūcatuḥ //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
द्विजो वैश्यं पुनः प्राह हस्ताभ्यां जायतां पणः
तथेति मन्यते वैश्यस् तौ गत्वा पुनर् ऊचतुः ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
The twice-born said to the vaiśya again: “Let the wager be made for our two hands.” / The vaiśya agreed: “So be it.” Having gone, the two asked again.

170.s:
pūrvaval laukikān gatvā jitam ity abravīd dvijaḥ
karau chittvā tataḥ prāha kathaṃ dharmaṃ tu manyase
ākṣipto brāhmaṇenaivaṃ vaiśyo vacanam abravīt //
170.d:
पूर्ववल् लौकिकान् गत्वा जितम् इत्य् अब्रवीद् द्विजः
करौ छित्त्वा ततः प्राह कथं धर्मं तु मन्यसे
आक्षिप्तो ब्राह्मणेनैवं वैश्यो वचनम् अब्रवीत् ॥
170.m: Having approached the common folk as before, the twice-born said: “I have won!” / Then, having cut off his two hands, he said: “How do you regard dharma now?” / Thus taunted by the brāhmaṇa, the vaiśya spoke these words:

170.s:
vaiśya uvāca
dharmam eva paraṃ manye prāṇaiḥ kaṇṭhagatair api
mātā pitā suhṛd bandhur dharma eva śarīriṇām //
170.d:
वैश्य उवाच
धर्मम् एव परं मन्ये प्राणैः कण्ठगतैर् अपि
माता पिता सुहृद् बन्धुर् धर्म एव शरीरिणाम् ॥
170.m:
The vaiśya said:
“I consider dharma alone to be supreme, even when my vital breaths are in my throat. / Dharma alone is mother, father, friend, and kinsman to embodied beings.”

170.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ vivadamānau tāv arthavān brāhmaṇo 'bhavat
vimukto vaiśyakas tatra bāhubhyāṃ ca dhanena ca //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं विवदमानौ ताव् अर्थवान् ब्राह्मणो ऽभवत्
विमुक्तो वैश्यकस् तत्र बाहुभ्यां च धनेन च ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
As they disputed thus, the brāhmaṇa became rich in wealth, / and the poor vaiśya there was deprived of both his arms and his wealth.

170.s:
evaṃ bhramantau saṃprāptau gaṅgāṃ yogeśvaraṃ harim
yadṛcchayā muniśreṣṭha mithas tāv ūcatuḥ punaḥ //
170.d:
एवं भ्रमन्तौ संप्राप्तौ गङ्गां योगेश्वरं हरिम्
यदृच्छया मुनिश्रेष्ठ मिथस् ताव् ऊचतुः पुनः ॥
170.m: Wandering thus, they reached the Gaṅgā and Hari, the Lord of Yoga. / By chance, O best of sages, the two again spoke to each other.

170.s:
vaiśyo gaṅgāṃ tu yogeśaṃ dharmam eva praśaṃsati
atikopād dvijo vaiśyam ākṣipan punar abravīt //
170.d:
वैश्यो गङ्गां तु योगेशं धर्मम् एव प्रशंसति
अतिकोपाद् द्विजो वैश्यम् आक्षिपन् पुनर् अब्रवीत् ॥
170.m: The vaiśya praised the Gaṅgā, the Lord of Yoga, and dharma itself. / In great anger, the twice-born taunted the vaiśya and spoke again:

170.s:
brāhmaṇa uvāca
gataṃ dhanaṃ karau chinnāv avaśiṣṭo śubhir bhavān
tvam anyathā yadi brūṣa āhariṣye 'sinā śiraḥ //
170.d:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
गतं धनं करौ छिन्नाव् अवशिष्टो शुभिर् भवान्
त्वम् अन्यथा यदि ब्रूष आहरिष्ये ऽसिना शिरः ॥
170.m:
The brāhmaṇa said:
“Your wealth is gone, your hands are severed, you remain alive with difficulty; / if you speak otherwise, I will take your head with a sword!”

170.s:
brahmovāca
vihasya punar āhedaṃ vaiśyo gautamam añjasā //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विहस्य पुनर् आहेदं वैश्यो गौतमम् अञ्जसा ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
Smiling, the vaiśya at once said this to Gautama:

170.s:
vaiśya uvāca
dharmam eva paraṃ manye yathecchasi tathā kuru
brāhmaṇāṃś ca gurūn devān vedān dharmaṃ janārdanam //
170.d:
वैश्य उवाच
धर्मम् एव परं मन्ये यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु
ब्राह्मणांश् च गुरून् देवान् वेदान् धर्मं जनार्दनम् ॥
170.m:
The vaiśya said:
“I consider dharma alone to be supreme; do as you please. / One who reviles brāhmaṇas, teachers, gods, the Vedas, dharma, and Janārdana—

170.s:
yas tu nindayate pāpo nāsau spṛśyo 'tha pāpakṛt
upekṣaṇīyo durvṛttaḥ pāpātmā dharmadūṣakaḥ //
170.d:
यस् तु निन्दयते पापो नासौ स्पृश्यो ऽथ पापकृत्
उपेक्षणीयो दुर्वृत्तः पापात्मा धर्मदूषकः ॥
170.m: that sinner should not even be touched; doing evil, / wicked, sinful in nature, and defiler of dharma, he should be disregarded.”

170.s:
brahmovāca
tataḥ prāha sa kopena dharmaṃ yady anuśaṃsasi
āvayoḥ prāṇayor atra paṇaḥ syād iti vai mune //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः प्राह स कोपेन धर्मं यद्य् अनुशंससि
आवयोः प्राणयोर् अत्र पणः स्याद् इति वै मुने ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
Then he said in anger: “If you still praise dharma, / let our lives be the wager here, O sage!”

170.s:
evam ukte gautamena tathety āha vaṇik tadā
punar apy ūcatur ubhau lokāṃl lokās tathocire //
170.d:
एवम् उक्ते गौतमेन तथेत्य् आह वणिक् तदा
पुनर् अप्य् ऊचतुर् उभौ लोकांल् लोकास् तथोचिरे ॥
170.m: When this was said by Gautama, the merchant then agreed: “So be it.” / Both of them asked the people again, and the people said the same thing.

170.s:
yogeśvarasya purato gautamyā dakṣiṇe taṭe
taṃ nipātya viśaṃ vipraś cakṣur utpāṭya cābravīt //
170.d:
योगेश्वरस्य पुरतो गौतम्या दक्षिणे तटे
तं निपात्य विशं विप्रश् चक्षुर् उत्पाट्य चाब्रवीत् ॥
170.m: In front of the Lord of Yoga on the southern bank of the Gautamī, / having struck down that vaiśya and gouged out his eyes, the vipra said:

170.s:
vipra uvāca
gato 'sīmāṃ daśāṃ vaiśya nityaṃ dharmapraśaṃsayā
gataṃ dhanaṃ gataṃ cakṣuś cheditau karapallavau
pṛṣṭo 'si mitra gacchāmi maivaṃ brūyāḥ kathāntare //
170.d:
विप्र उवाच
गतो ऽसीमां दशां वैश्य नित्यं धर्मप्रशंसया
गतं धनं गतं चक्षुश् छेदितौ करपल्लवौ
पृष्टो ऽसि मित्र गच्छामि मैवं ब्रूयाः कथान्तरे ॥
170.m:
The vipra said:
“You have reached this state, O vaiśya, by your constant praise of dharma: / wealth is gone, sight is gone, your sprout-like hands have been severed. / I have asked your leave, my friend, and now I go; do not speak thus in another story!”

170.s:
brahmovāca
tasmin prayāte vaiśyo 'sau cintayām āsa cetasi
hā kaṣṭaṃ me kim abhavad dharmaikamanaso hare //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तस्मिन् प्रयाते वैश्यो ऽसौ चिन्तयाम् आस चेतसि
हा कष्टं मे किम् अभवद् धर्मैकमनसो हरे ॥
170.m:
Brahmā said:
When he had departed, that vaiśya reflected in his mind: / “Alas, what misfortune has befallen me whose mind is devoted solely to dharma, O Hari!”

170.s:
sa kuṇḍalo vaṇikśreṣṭho nirdhano gatabāhukaḥ
gatanetraḥ śucaṃ prāpto dharmam evānusaṃsmaran //
170.d:
स कुण्डलो वणिक्श्रेष्ठो निर्धनो गतबाहुकः
गतनेत्रः शुचं प्राप्तो धर्मम् एवानुसंस्मरन् ॥
170.m: That best of merchants, Kuṇḍala, penniless, armless, / sightless, fell into grief, constantly remembering dharma alone.

170.s:
evaṃ bahuvidhāṃ cintāṃ kurvann āste mahītale
niśceṣṭo 'tha nirutsāhaḥ patitaḥ śokasāgare //
170.d:
एवं बहुविधां चिन्तां कुर्वन्न् आस्ते महीतले
निश्चेष्टो ऽथ निरुत्साहः पतितः शोकसागरे ॥
170.m: Engaged thus in various anxieties, he remained on the surface of the earth, / motionless and despondent, fallen into an ocean of sorrow.

170.s:
dināvasāne śarvaryām udite candramaṇḍale
ekādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣe tatrāyāti vibhīṣaṇaḥ //
170.d:
दिनावसाने शर्वर्याम् उदिते चन्द्रमण्डले
एकादश्यां शुक्लपक्षे तत्रायाति विभीषणः ॥
170.m: At the close of day, at night when the orb of the moon had risen / on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight, Vibhīṣaṇa arrived there.

170.s:
sa tu yogeśvaraṃ devaṃ pūjayitvā yathāvidhi
snātvā tu gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ saputro rākṣasair vṛtaḥ //
170.d:
स तु योगेश्वरं देवं पूजयित्वा यथाविधि
स्नात्वा तु गौतमीं गङ्गां सपुत्रो राक्षसैर् वृतः ॥
170.m: Having duly worshipped the deity, the Lord of Yoga, / and bathed in the Gautamī Gaṅgā, accompanied by his son and surrounded by rākṣasas—

170.s:
vibhīṣaṇasya hi suto vibhīṣaṇa ivāparaḥ
vaibhīṣaṇir iti khyātas tam apaśyad uvāca ha //
170.d:
विभीषणस्य हि सुतो विभीषण इवापरः
वैभीषणिर् इति ख्यातस् तम् अपश्यद् उवाच ह ॥
170.m: the son of Vibhīṣaṇa, like a second Vibhīṣaṇa, / known as Vaibhīṣaṇi, saw him and spoke to him.

170.s:
vaiśyasya vacanaṃ śrutvā yathāvṛttaṃ sa dharmavit
pitre nivedayām āsa laṅkeśāya mahātmane
sa tu laṅkeśvaraḥ prāha putraṃ prītyā guṇākaram //
170.d:
वैश्यस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा यथावृत्तं स धर्मवित्
पित्रे निवेदयाम् आस लङ्केशाय महात्मने
स तु लङ्केश्वरः प्राह पुत्रं प्रीत्या गुणाकरम् ॥
170.m: Having heard the vaiśya’s account as it had happened, that knower of dharma / reported it to his father, the high-souled lord of Laṅkā. / Then that lord of Laṅkā spoke with affection to his son, a mine of virtues:

170.s:
vibhīṣaṇa uvāca
śrīmān rāmo mama gurus tasya mānyaḥ sakhā mama
hanumān iti vikhyātas tenānīto girir mahān //
170.d:
विभीषण उवाच
श्रीमान् रामो मम गुरुस् तस्य मान्यः सखा मम
हनुमान् इति विख्यातस् तेनानीतो गिरिर् महान् ॥
170.m:
Vibhīṣaṇa said:
“The glorious Rāma is my guru; his honored friend, / celebrated as Hanumān, is my friend. By him a great mountain was brought

170.s:
purā kāryāntare prāpte sarvauṣadhyāśrayo 'calaḥ
jāte kārye tam ādāya himavantam athāgamat //
170.d:
पुरा कार्यान्तरे प्राप्ते सर्वौषध्याश्रयो ऽचलः
जाते कार्ये तम् आदाय हिमवन्तम् अथागमत् ॥
170.m: formerly, when a crisis had occurred—a mountain that was the abode of all medicinal herbs; / and when the task was accomplished, he took it and went back to the Himavat.

170.s:
viśalyakaraṇī ceti mṛtasaṃjīvanīti ca
tadānīya mahābuddhī rāmāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe //
170.d:
विशल्यकरणी चेति मृतसंजीवनीति च
तदानीय महाबुद्धी रामायाक्लिष्टकर्मणे ॥
170.m: [Carrying] Viśalyakaraṇī and Mṛtasaṃjīvanī, / that one of great intellect, having brought them for Rāma of untiring deeds

170.s:
nivedayitvā tat sādhyaṃ tasmin vṛtte samāgataḥ
punar giriṃ samādāya āgacchad devaparvatam //
170.d:
निवेदयित्वा तत् साध्यं तस्मिन् वृत्ते समागतः
पुनर् गिरिं समादाय आगच्छद् देवपर्वतम् ॥
170.m: and offered them, when the task was accomplished and he returned, / he took the mountain again and came to the mountain of the gods.”

170.s:
tām ānīyāsya hṛdaye niveśaya hariṃ smaran
tataḥ prāpsyaty ayaṃ sarvam apekṣitam udāradhīḥ //
170.d:
ताम् आनीयास्य हृदये निवेशय हरिं स्मरन्
ततः प्राप्स्यत्य् अयं सर्वम् अपेक्षितम् उदारधीः ॥
170.m: "Bring it and place it on his chest, remembering Hari; / then this noble-minded man will obtain all that he desires."

170.s:
gacchatas tasya vegena viśalyakaraṇī punaḥ
apatad gautamītīre yatra yogeśvaro hariḥ //
170.d:
गच्छतस् तस्य वेगेन विशल्यकरणी पुनः
अपतद् गौतमीतीरे यत्र योगेश्वरो हरिः ॥
170.m: As he was traveling swiftly, the viśalyakaraṇī fell again / on the bank of the Gautamī, where Hari is present as Yogeśvara.

170.s:
vaibhīṣaṇir uvāca
tām oṣadhīṃ mama pitar darśayāśu vilamba mā
parārtiśamanād anyac chreyo na bhuvanatraye //
170.d:
वैभीषणिर् उवाच
ताम् ओषधीं मम पितर् दर्शयाशु विलम्ब मा
परार्तिशमनाद् अन्यच् छ्रेयो न भुवनत्रये ॥
170.m: The son of Vibhīṣaṇa said: / "O my father, show me that herb at once; do not delay! / In the three worlds there is no higher good than soothing the pain of another."

170.s:
brahmovāca
vibhīṣaṇas tathety uktvā tāṃ putrasyāpy adarśayat
iṣe tvety asya vṛkṣasya śākhāṃ ciccheda tatsutaḥ
vaiśyasya cāpi vai prītyā santaḥ parahite ratāḥ //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विभीषणस् तथेत्य् उक्त्वा तां पुत्रस्याप्य् अदर्शयत्
इषे त्वेत्य् अस्य वृक्षस्य शाखां चिच्छेद तत्सुतः
वैश्यस्य चापि वै प्रीत्या सन्तः परहिते रताः ॥
170.m: Brahmā said: / Vibhīṣaṇa said, "So be it," and showed it to his son. / His son cut a branch of this tree, [reciting] "Iṣe tvā..." [for food, thee...], / out of love for the vaiśya; for the virtuous are dedicated to the welfare of others.

170.s:
vibhīṣaṇa uvāca
yatrāpatan nage cāsmin sa vṛkṣas tu pratāpavān
tasya śākhāṃ samādāya hṛdaye 'sya niveśaya
tatspṛṣṭamātra evāsau svakaṃ rūpam avāpnuyāt //
170.d:
विभीषण उवाच
यत्रापतन् नगे चास्मिन् स वृक्षस् तु प्रतापवान्
तस्य शाखां समादाय हृदये ऽस्य निवेशय
तत्स्पृष्टमात्र एवासौ स्वकं रूपम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
170.m: Vibhīṣaṇa said: / "Where it fell on this mountain, there stands that powerful tree. / Take a branch of it and place it on his chest; / the moment he is touched by it, he will regain his own form."

170.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā pitur vākyaṃ vaibhīṣaṇir udāradhīḥ
tathā cakāra vai samyak kāṣṭhakhaṇḍaṃ nyaveśayat //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा पितुर् वाक्यं वैभीषणिर् उदारधीः
तथा चकार वै सम्यक् काष्ठखण्डं न्यवेशयत् ॥
170.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing these words of his father, the noble-minded son of Vibhīṣaṇa / did just so, placing the piece of wood properly.

170.s:
hṛdaye sa tu vaiśyo 'pi sacakṣuḥ sakaro 'bhavat
maṇimantrauṣadhīnāṃ hi vīryaṃ ko 'pi na budhyate //
170.d:
हृदये स तु वैश्यो ऽपि सचक्षुः सकरो ऽभवत्
मणिमन्त्रौषधीनां हि वीर्यं को ऽपि न बुध्यते ॥
170.m: Upon [its touch to] his chest, that vaiśya gained both his eyes and his hands; / for indeed, no one can comprehend the power of jewels, mantras, and herbs.

170.s:
tad eva kāṣṭham ādāya dharmam evānusaṃsmaran
snātvā tu gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ tathā yogeśvaraṃ harim //
170.d:
तद् एव काष्ठम् आदाय धर्मम् एवानुसंस्मरन्
स्नात्वा तु गौतमीं गङ्गां तथा योगेश्वरं हरिम् ॥
170.m: Taking that very wood and meditating on dharma alone, / having bathed in the Gautamī-Gaṅgā, and likewise [worshiping] Hari, the lord of yoga (Yogeśvara),

170.s:
namaskṛtvā punar agāt kāṣṭhakhaṇḍena vaiśyakaḥ
paribhraman nṛpapuraṃ mahāpuram iti śrutam //
170.d:
नमस्कृत्वा पुनर् अगात् काष्ठखण्डेन वैश्यकः
परिभ्रमन् नृपपुरं महापुरम् इति श्रुतम् ॥
170.m: and having bowed down, the vaiśya walked on again with the piece of wood, / wandering until he came to a royal city known as Mahāpura.

170.s:
mahārāja iti khyātas tatra rājā mahābalaḥ
tasya nāsti sutaḥ kaścit putrikā naṣṭalocanā //
170.d:
महाराज इति ख्यातस् तत्र राजा महाबलः
तस्य नास्ति सुतः कश्चित् पुत्रिका नष्टलोचना ॥
170.m: The king there was celebrated as Mahārāja, possessed of great might. / He had no son at all, but only a daughter who had lost her sight.

170.s:
saiva tasya sutā putras tasyāpi vratam īdṛśam
devo vā dānavo vāpi brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo bhavet //
170.d:
सैव तस्य सुता पुत्रस् तस्यापि व्रतम् ईदृशम्
देवो वा दानवो वापि ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो भवेत् ॥
170.m: She alone was both daughter and son to him, and he took such a vow: / "Be he a god, a dānava, a brāhmaṇa, or a kṣatriya,

170.s:
vaiśyo vā śūdrayonir vā saguṇo nirguṇo 'pi vā
tasmai deyā iyaṃ putrī yo netre āhariṣyati //
170.d:
वैश्यो वा शूद्रयोनिर् वा सगुणो निर्गुणो ऽपि वा
तस्मै देया इयं पुत्री यो नेत्रे आहरिष्यति ॥
170.m: or a vaiśya, or of śūdra birth, with virtues or without virtue— / to him this daughter will be given who will restore her eyes;

170.s:
rājyena saha deyeyam iti rājā hy aghoṣayat
aharniśam asau vaiśyaḥ śrutvā ghoṣam athābravīt //
170.d:
राज्येन सह देयेयम् इति राजा ह्य् अघोषयत्
अहर्निशम् असौ वैश्यः श्रुत्वा घोषम् अथाब्रवीत् ॥
170.m: she is to be given along with the kingdom!" Thus the king proclaimed day and night. / Hearing the proclamation, that vaiśya said:

170.s:
vaiśya uvāca
ahaṃ netre āhariṣye rājaputryā asaṃśayam //
170.d:
वैश्य उवाच
अहं नेत्रे आहरिष्ये राजपुत्र्या असंशयम् ॥
170.m: The vaiśya said: / "I shall restore the eyes of the king's daughter without doubt."

170.s:
brahmovāca
taṃ vaiśyaṃ tarasādāya mahārājñe nyavedayat
tatkāṣṭhasparśamātreṇa sanetrābhūn nṛpātmajā //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तं वैश्यं तरसादाय महाराज्ञे न्यवेदयत्
तत्काष्ठस्पर्शमात्रेण सनेत्राभून् नृपात्मजा ॥
170.m: Brahmā said: / Quickly taking that vaiśya, they presented him to the great king. / By the mere touch of that wood, the king's daughter gained her sight.

170.s:
tataḥ savismayo rājā ko bhavān iti cābravīt
vaiśyo rājñe yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayad aśeṣataḥ //
170.d:
ततः सविस्मयो राजा को भवान् इति चाब्रवीत्
वैश्यो राज्ञे यथावृत्तं न्यवेदयद् अशेषतः ॥
170.m: Then the astonished king said, "Who are you?" / And the vaiśya recounted the whole story to the king without omission.

170.s:
vaiśya uvāca
brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādena dharmasya tapasas tathā
dānaprabhāvād yajñaiś ca vividhair bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
divyauṣadhiprabhāvena mama sāmarthyam īdṛśam //
170.d:
वैश्य उवाच
ब्राह्मणानां प्रसादेन धर्मस्य तपसस् तथा
दानप्रभावाद् यज्ञैश् च विविधैर् भूरिदक्षिणैः
दिव्यौषधिप्रभावेन मम सामर्थ्यम् ईदृशम् ॥
170.m: The vaiśya said: / "By the grace of the brāhmaṇas, of dharma, and of austerity, / by the power of gift-giving and various sacrifices with abundant dakṣiṇās, / and by the power of the divine herb, such is my ability."

170.s:
brahmovāca
etad vaiśyavacaḥ śrutvā vismito 'bhūn mahīpatiḥ //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतद् वैश्यवचः श्रुत्वा विस्मितो ऽभून् महीपतिः ॥
170.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing this speech of the vaiśya, the lord of the earth was amazed.

170.s:
rājovāca
aho mahānubhāvo 'yaṃ prāyo vṛndārako bhavet
anyathaitādṛg anyasya sāmarthyaṃ dṛśyate katham
tasmād asmai tu tāṃ kanyāṃ pradāsye rājyapūrvikām //
170.d:
राजोवाच
अहो महानुभावो ऽयं प्रायो वृन्दारको भवेत्
अन्यथैतादृग् अन्यस्य सामर्थ्यं दृश्यते कथम्
तस्माद् अस्मै तु तां कन्यां प्रदास्ये राज्यपूर्विकाम् ॥
170.m: The king said: / "Ah, he is of great majesty; he is likely a celestial! / How else could such power be seen in anyone else? / Therefore I will give him that maiden, preceded by the kingdom."

170.s:
brahmovāca
iti saṃkalpya manasi kanyāṃ rājyaṃ ca dattavān
vihārārthaṃ gataḥ svairaṃ paraṃ khedam upāgataḥ //
170.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इति संकल्प्य मनसि कन्यां राज्यं च दत्तवान्
विहारार्थं गतः स्वैरं परं खेदम् उपागतः ॥
170.m: Brahmā said: / Having resolved thus in his mind, he gave him the maiden and the kingdom. / Going at will to amuse himself, [the vaiśya] fell into profound sorrow:

170.s:
na mitreṇa vinā rājyaṃ na mitreṇa vinā sukham
tam eva satataṃ vipraṃ cintayan vaiśyanandanaḥ //
170.d:
न मित्रेण विना राज्यं न मित्रेण विना सुखम्
तम् एव सततं विप्रं चिन्तयन् वैश्यनन्दनः ॥
170.m: "Without a friend there is no kingdom; without a friend there is no happiness!" / Constantly thinking of that very vipra, the vaiśya's son [reflected].

170.s:
etad eva sujātānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bhuvi dehinām
kṛpārdraṃ yan mano nityaṃ teṣām apy ahiteṣu hi //
170.d:
एतद् एव सुजातानां लक्षणं भुवि देहिनाम्
कृपार्द्रं यन् मनो नित्यं तेषाम् अप्य् अहितेषु हि ॥
170.m: This indeed is the mark of noble-born beings on earth: / that their minds are ever melted with compassion, even toward those who have wronged them.

170.s:
mahānṛpo vanaṃ prāyāt sa rājā maṇikuṇḍalaḥ
tasmiñ śāsati rājyaṃ tu kadācid gautamaṃ dvijam //
170.d:
महानृपो वनं प्रायात् स राजा मणिकुण्डलः
तस्मिञ् शासति राज्यं तु कदाचिद् गौतमं द्विजम् ॥
170.m: The great king went to the forest, and that [vaiśya] Maṇikuṇḍala became king. / While he was ruling the kingdom, one day [he saw] the twice-born Gautama,

170.s:
hṛtasvaṃ dyūtakaiḥ pāpair apaśyan maṇikuṇḍalaḥ
tam ādāya dvijaṃ mitraṃ pūjayām āsa dharmavit //
170.d:
हृतस्वं द्यूतकैः पापैर् अपश्यन् मणिकुण्डलः
तम् आदाय द्विजं मित्रं पूजयाम् आस धर्मवित् ॥
170.m: Maṇikuṇḍala saw him, whose wealth had been stolen by wicked gamblers. / Taking that twice-born friend, he who knew dharma honored him.

170.s:
dharmāṇāṃ tu prabhāvaṃ taṃ tasmai sarvaṃ nyavedayat
snāpayām āsa gaṅgāyāṃ taṃ sarvāghanivṛttaye //
170.d:
धर्माणां तु प्रभावं तं तस्मै सर्वं न्यवेदयत्
स्नापयाम् आस गङ्गायां तं सर्वाघनिवृत्तये ॥
170.m: He told him all about that power of dharmas, / and made him bathe in the Gaṅgā to remove all sin.

170.s:
tena vipreṇa sarvais taiḥ svakīyair gotrajair vṛtaḥ
vaiśyaiḥ svadeśasaṃbhūtair brāhmaṇasya tu bāndhavaiḥ //
170.d:
तेन विप्रेण सर्वैस् तैः स्वकीयैर् गोत्रजैर् वृतः
वैश्यैः स्वदेशसंभूतैर् ब्राह्मणस्य तु बान्धवैः ॥
170.m: Surrounded by that vipra and by all his own kinsmen, / by vaiśyas born in his own country, and by the brāhmaṇa's relatives,

170.s:
vṛddhakauśikamukhyaiś ca tasmin yogeśvarāntike
yajñān iṣṭvā surān pūjya tataḥ svargam upeyivān //
170.d:
वृद्धकौशिकमुख्यैश् च तस्मिन् योगेश्वरान्तिके
यज्ञान् इष्ट्वा सुरान् पूज्य ततः स्वर्गम् उपेयिवान् ॥
170.m: and by the foremost elders of the Kuśika lineage, near that Yogeśvara / he offered sacrifices, worshiped the gods, and then attained heaven.

170.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ mṛtasaṃjīvanaṃ viduḥ
cakṣustīrthaṃ sayogeśaṃ smaraṇād api puṇyadam
manaḥprasādajananaṃ sarvadurbhāvanāśanam //
170.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं मृतसंजीवनं विदुः
चक्षुस्तीर्थं सयोगेशं स्मरणाद् अपि पुण्यदम्
मनःप्रसादजननं सर्वदुर्भावनाशनम् ॥
170.m: From then on, they have known that holy place as Mṛtasaṃjīvana [and] / Cakṣustīrtha, accompanied by Yogeśa; it grants merit even by its remembrance, / produces peace of mind, and destroys all evil thoughts.

171.s:
brahmovāca
urvaśītīrtham ākhyātam aśvamedhaphalapradam
snānadānamahādevavāsudevārcanādibhiḥ //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
उर्वशीतीर्थम् आख्यातम् अश्वमेधफलप्रदम्
स्नानदानमहादेववासुदेवार्चनादिभिः ॥
171.m: Brahmā said: / The holy place Urvaśītīrtha is proclaimed to grant the fruit of the horse sacrifice / through bathing, gift-giving, and the worship of Mahādeva, Vāsudeva, and others.

171.s:
maheśvaro yatra devo yatra śārṅgadharo hariḥ
pramatir nāma rājāsīt sārvabhaumaḥ pratāpavān //
171.d:
महेश्वरो यत्र देवो यत्र शार्ङ्गधरो हरिः
प्रमतिर् नाम राजासीत् सार्वभौमः प्रतापवान् ॥
171.m: Where God is present as Maheśvara and Hari is the bow-bearer Śārṅgadhara, / there once lived a powerful universal monarch named Pramati.

171.s:
ripūñ jitvā jagāmāśu indralokaṃ surair vṛtam
tatrāpaśyat surapatiṃ marudbhiḥ saha nārada //
171.d:
रिपूञ् जित्वा जगामाशु इन्द्रलोकं सुरैर् वृतम्
तत्रापश्यत् सुरपतिं मरुद्भिः सह नारद ॥
171.m: Having conquered his enemies, he quickly went to Indra's world, surrounded by gods; / there he saw the lord of gods along with the Maruts, O Nārada.

171.s:
jahāsendraṃ pāśahastaṃ pramatiḥ kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ
taṃ hasantam athālakṣya hariḥ pramatim abravīt //
171.d:
जहासेन्द्रं पाशहस्तं प्रमतिः क्षत्रियर्षभः
तं हसन्तम् अथालक्ष्य हरिः प्रमतिम् अब्रवीत् ॥
171.m: Pramati, best among kṣatriyas, laughed at Indra holding a snare in his hand. / Noticing him laughing, Indra then said to Pramati:

171.s:
indra uvāca
devālaye mahābuddhe marudbhiḥ krīḍitair alam
diśo jitvā divaṃ prāptaḥ kuru krīḍāṃ mayā saha //
171.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
देवालये महाबुद्धे मरुद्भिः क्रीडितैर् अलम्
दिशो जित्वा दिवं प्राप्तः कुरु क्रीडां मया सह ॥
171.m: Indra said: / "O man of great intellect, enough with playing with the Maruts in the abode of the gods! / Having conquered the quarters and reached heaven, play a game with me."

171.s:
brahmovāca
sakaṣāyaṃ harivaco niśamya pramatir nṛpaḥ
tathety uvāca devendraṃ niṣkṛtiṃ kāṃ tu manyase
tac chrutvā pramater vākyaṃ surarāṇ nṛpam abravīt //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सकषायं हरिवचो निशम्य प्रमतिर् नृपः
तथेत्य् उवाच देवेन्द्रं निष्कृतिं कां तु मन्यसे
तच् छ्रुत्वा प्रमतेर् वाक्यं सुरराण् नृपम् अब्रवीत् ॥
171.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing the harsh words of Indra, King Pramati / said to the lord of gods, "So be it; but what stake do you intend?" / Hearing those words of Pramati, the king of gods said to the king:

171.s:
indra uvāca
urvaśy eva paṇo 'smākaṃ prāpyā yā nikhilair makhaiḥ //
171.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
उर्वश्य् एव पणो ऽस्माकं प्राप्या या निखिलैर् मखैः ॥
171.m: Indra said: / "Urvaśī alone is our wager, who is obtainable only through all the sacrifices."

171.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvendravacanaṃ pramatiḥ prāha garvitaḥ
urvaśīṃ niṣkṛtiṃ manye tvaṃ rājan kiṃ nu manyase //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वेन्द्रवचनं प्रमतिः प्राह गर्वितः
उर्वशीं निष्कृतिं मन्ये त्वं राजन् किं नु मन्यसे ॥
171.m: Brahmā said: / Hearing these words of Indra, Pramati said haughtily: / "I agree that Urvaśī is the stake; but what do you propose, O king?"

171.s:
yad bravīṣi sureśāna tan manye 'haṃ śatakrato
prāhendraṃ pramatis tadvan niṣkṛtyai dakṣiṇaṃ karam
savarma saśaraṃ dharmyaṃ dehi dīvyāmahe vayam //
171.d:
यद् ब्रवीषि सुरेशान तन् मन्ये ऽहं शतक्रतो
प्राहेन्द्रं प्रमतिस् तद्वन् निष्कृत्यै दक्षिणं करम्
सवर्म सशरं धर्म्यं देहि दीव्यामहे वयम् ॥
171.m: "Whatever you say, O lord of gods, O Śatakratu, I accept that." / Pramati likewise said to Indra: "As a stake, / wager your right hand with armor and arrow, according to dharma; let us play!"

171.s:
brahmovāca
tāv evaṃ saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā devanāyopatasthatuḥ
pramatir jitavāṃs tatra urvaśīṃ daivatastriyam
tāṃ jitvā pramatiḥ prāha saṃrambhāt taṃ śatakratum //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ताव् एवं संविदं कृत्वा देवनायोपतस्थतुः
प्रमतिर् जितवांस् तत्र उर्वशीं दैवतस्त्रियम्
तां जित्वा प्रमतिः प्राह संरम्भात् तं शतक्रतुम् ॥
171.m: Brahmā said: / The two of them, having made such an agreement, approached the gambling-board. / Pramati won Urvaśī there, the celestial woman. / Having won her, Pramati in his excitement said to that Śatakratu:

171.s:
pramatir uvāca
niṣkṛtyai punar anyan me paścād dīvye tvayā vibho //
171.d:
प्रमतिर् उवाच
निष्कृत्यै पुनर् अन्यन् मे पश्चाद् दीव्ये त्वया विभो ॥
171.m: Pramati said: / "Stake another thing for me again, O lord, and then I will play with you."

171.s:
indra uvāca
devayogyam atho vajraṃ jaitraṃ saratham uttamam
dīvye 'haṃ tena nṛpate kareṇāpy avicārayan //
171.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
देवयोग्यम् अथो वज्रं जैत्रं सरथम् उत्तमम्
दीव्ये ऽहं तेन नृपते करेणाप्य् अविचारयन् ॥
171.m: Indra said: / "I shall wager the thunderbolt worthy of gods, victorious, with its excellent chariot, / and also my hand without hesitation, O king!"

171.s:
brahmovāca
sa gṛhītvā tadā pāśān anyāṃś ca maṇibhūṣitān
jitam ity abravīc chakraṃ pramatiḥ prahasaṃs tadā //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स गृहीत्वा तदा पाशान् अन्यांश् च मणिभूषितान्
जितम् इत्य् अब्रवीच् छक्रं प्रमतिः प्रहसंस् तदा ॥
171.m: Brahmā said: / Then, taking the dice and others adorned with gems, / Pramati said to Śakra, laughing aloud at that time: "Won!"

171.s:
etasminn antare prāyād akṣajñas tatra nārada
viśvāvasur iti khyāto gandharvāṇāṃ maheśvaraḥ //
171.d:
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे प्रायाद् अक्षज्ञस् तत्र नारद
विश्वावसुर् इति ख्यातो गन्धर्वाणां महेश्वरः ॥
171.m: In the meantime, O Nārada, there arrived one skilled in dice, / known as Viśvāvasu, the sovereign lord of the gandharvas.

171.s:
viśvāvasur uvāca
gandharvavidyayā rājaṃs tayā dīvyāmahe tvayā
tathety uktvā sa nṛpatir jitam ity abravīt tadā //
171.d:
विश्वावसुर् उवाच
गन्धर्वविद्यया राजंस् तया दीव्यामहे त्वया
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा स नृपतिर् जितम् इत्य् अब्रवीत् तदा ॥
171.m: Viśvāvasu said: / "O king, let us play with you with the gandharva lore as stake." / Saying "So be it," the king then said, "Won!"

171.s: tau jitvā nṛpatir maurkhyād devendraṃ prāha kaśmalam //
171.d: तौ जित्वा नृपतिर् मौर्ख्याद् देवेन्द्रं प्राह कश्मलम् ॥
171.m: Having defeated those two, the king out of folly spoke shameful words to the king of the gods:

171.s:
pramatir uvāca
raṇe vā devane vāpi na tvaṃ jetā kathaṃcana
mahendra satataṃ tasmād asmadārādhako bhava
vada kena prakāreṇa jātā devendratā tava //
171.d:
प्रमतिर् उवाच
रणे वा देवने वापि न त्वं जेता कथंचन
महेन्द्र सततं तस्माद् अस्मदाराधको भव
वद केन प्रकारेण जाता देवेन्द्रता तव ॥
171.m:
Pramati said:
"Neither in battle nor in gambling are you ever the victor, / Mahendra; therefore always be my worshipper!
Tell me: in what manner did your lordship over the gods come about?"

171.s:
brahmovāca
tathā prāhorvaśīṃ garvād gaccha karmakarī bhava
urvaśī prāha deveṣu yathā varte tathā tvayi
varteya sarvabhāvena na māṃ dhikkartum arhasi //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथा प्राहोर्वशीं गर्वाद् गच्छ कर्मकरी भव
उर्वशी प्राह देवेषु यथा वर्ते तथा त्वयि
वर्तेय सर्वभावेन न मां धिक्कर्तुम् अर्हसि ॥
171.m:
Brahmā said:
Likewise, out of pride, he said to Urvaśī, "Go, become a servant-maid!"
Urvaśī said, "As I conduct myself toward the gods, so would I conduct myself / toward you with wholehearted devotion; you ought not to disdain me."

171.s:
brahmovāca
tatas tāṃ pramatiḥ prāha tvādṛśyaḥ santi cārikāḥ
tvaṃ kiṃ vilajjase bhadre gaccha karmakarī bhava //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तां प्रमतिः प्राह त्वादृश्यः सन्ति चारिकाः
त्वं किं विलज्जसे भद्रे गच्छ कर्मकरी भव ॥
171.m:
Brahmā said:
Then Pramati said to her, "There are maidservants like you [already].
Why are you ashamed, auspicious lady? Go, become a servant-maid!"

171.s:
etac chrutvā nṛpeṇoktaṃ gandharvādhipatis tadā
citrasena iti khyātaḥ suto viśvāvasor balī //
171.d:
एतच् छ्रुत्वा नृपेणोक्तं गन्धर्वाधिपतिस् तदा
चित्रसेन इति ख्यातः सुतो विश्वावसोर् बली ॥
171.m:
Hearing this spoken by the king, the mighty lord of the Gandharvas,
known as Citrasena, the son of Viśvāvasu, [spoke]:

171.s:
citrasena uvāca
dīvye 'haṃ vai tvayā rājan sarveṇānena bhūpate
rājyena jīvitenāpi madīyena tavāpi ca //
171.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच
दीव्ये ऽहं वै त्वया राजन् सर्वेणानेन भूपते
राज्येन जीवितेनापि मदीयेन तवापि च ॥
171.m:
Citrasena said:
"I will gamble with you, O king, for all of this, O ruler of the earth—
for the kingdom, and even for my life and yours!"

171.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā punar ubhau citrasenanṛpottamau
dīvyetām abhisaṃrabdhau citraseno 'jayat tadā //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा पुनर् उभौ चित्रसेननृपोत्तमौ
दीव्येताम् अभिसंरब्धौ चित्रसेनो ऽजयत् तदा ॥
171.m:
Brahmā said:
Having said, "So be it," both of them—Citrasena and the best of kings—
gambled once more with fierce passion; and then Citrasena won.

171.s:
gāndharvais taṃ mahāpāśair babandha nṛpatiṃ tadā
citraseno 'jayat sarvam urvaśīmukhyataḥ paṇaiḥ //
171.d:
गान्धर्वैस् तं महापाशैर् बबन्ध नृपतिं तदा
चित्रसेनो ऽजयत् सर्वम् उर्वशीमुख्यतः पणैः ॥
171.m:
Then Citrasena bound that king with great Gandharva nooses;
he won everything through the stakes, beginning with Urvaśī:

171.s:
rājyaṃ kośaṃ balaṃ caiva yad anyad vasu kiṃcana
citrasenasya taj jātaṃ yad āsīt pramater dhanam //
171.d:
राज्यं कोशं बलं चैव यद् अन्यद् वसु किंचन
चित्रसेनस्य तज् जातं यद् आसीत् प्रमतेर् धनम् ॥
171.m:
The kingdom, the treasury, the army, and whatever other wealth there was—
whatever was Pramati's property became Citrasena's.

171.s:
tasya putro bāla eva purodhasam uvāca ha
vaiśvāmitraṃ mahāprājñaṃ madhucchandasam ojasā //
171.d:
तस्य पुत्रो बाल एव पुरोधसम् उवाच ह
वैश्वामित्रं महाप्राज्ञं मधुच्छन्दसम् ओजसा ॥
171.m:
His son, though only a boy, addressed the family priest,
the very wise Madhucchandas, son of Viśvāmitra, with vigor:

171.s:
pramatiputra uvāca
kiṃ me pitrā kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ kva vā baddho mahāmatiḥ
katham eṣyati svaṃ sthānaṃ kathaṃ pāśair vimokṣyate //
171.d:
प्रमतिपुत्र उवाच
किं मे पित्रा कृतं पापं क्व वा बद्धो महामतिः
कथम् एष्यति स्वं स्थानं कथं पाशैर् विमोक्ष्यते ॥
171.m:
Pramati's son said:
"What sin was committed by my father? Where is the noble-minded one bound?
How will he return to his own place? How will he be freed from the nooses?"

171.s:
brahmovāca
sumater vacanaṃ śrutvā dhyātvā sa munisattamaḥ
madhucchandā jagādedaṃ pramater vartanaṃ tadā //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सुमतेर् वचनं श्रुत्वा ध्यात्वा स मुनिसत्तमः
मधुच्छन्दा जगादेदं प्रमतेर् वर्तनं तदा ॥
171.m:
Brahmā said:
Hearing Sumati's words and meditating, that best of sages,
Madhucchandas, then described Pramati's condition:

171.s:
madhucchandā uvāca
devaloke tava pitā baddha āste mahāmate
kaitavair bahudoṣaiś ca bhraṣṭarājyo babhūva ha //
171.d:
मधुच्छन्दा उवाच
देवलोके तव पिता बद्ध आस्ते महामते
कैतवैर् बहुदोषैश् च भ्रष्टराज्यो बभूव ह ॥

171.s:
yo yāti kaitavasabhāṃ sa cāpi kleśabhāg bhavet
dyūtamadyāmiṣādīni vyasanāni nṛpātmaja //
171.d:
यो याति कैतवसभां स चापि क्लेशभाग् भवेत्
द्यूतमद्यामिषादीनि व्यसनानि नृपात्मज ॥
171.m:
Whoever goes to a gambling-hall must also partake in misery;
gambling, liquor, meat, and the like are vices, O prince.

171.s:
pāpinām eva jāyante sadā pāpātmakāni hi
ekaikam apy anarthāya pāpāya narakāya ca //
171.d:
पापिनाम् एव जायन्ते सदा पापात्मकानि हि
एकैकम् अप्य् अनर्थाय पापाय नरकाय च ॥
171.m:
They arise only in sinners and are ever sinful by nature;
even a single one leads to disaster, sin, and hell.

171.s:
yānāsanābhilāpādyaiḥ kṛtaiḥ kaitavavartibhiḥ
kulīnāḥ kaluṣībhūtāḥ kiṃ punaḥ kitavo janaḥ //
171.d:
यानासनाभिलापाद्यैः कृतैः कैतववर्तिभिः
कुलीनाः कलुषीभूताः किं पुनः कितवो जनः ॥
171.m: When well-born men are stained merely by making use of the conveyances, seats, / and conversation of those who live by gambling, how much more so the gambler himself?

171.s:
kitavasya tu yā jāyā tapyate nityam eva sā
sa cāpi kitavaḥ pāpo yoṣitaṃ vīkṣya tapyate //
171.d:
कितवस्य तु या जाया तप्यते नित्यम् एव सा
स चापि कितवः पापो योषितं वीक्ष्य तप्यते ॥
171.m:
The wife of a gambler suffers constantly;
and that sinful gambler also suffers on seeing his wife.

171.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vigatānando nityaṃ vadati pāpakṛt
aho saṃsāracakre 'smin mayā tulyo na pātakī //
171.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा विगतानन्दो नित्यं वदति पापकृत्
अहो संसारचक्रे ऽस्मिन् मया तुल्यो न पातकी ॥
171.m:
Deprived of joy upon seeing her, the evildoer constantly says:
'Alas, in this cycle of worldly existence there is no sinner equal to me!'

171.s:
na kiṃcid api yasyāste loke viṣayajaṃ sukham
lokadvaye 'pi na sukhī kitavaḥ kopi dṛśyate //
171.d:
न किंचिद् अपि यस्यास्ते लोके विषयजं सुखम्
लोकद्वये ऽपि न सुखी कितवः कोपि दृश्यते ॥
171.m:
For whom there is not the slightest pleasure born of sense-objects in this world;
no gambler is seen to be happy in either of the two worlds.

171.s:
vibhāti ca tathā nityaṃ lajjayā dagdhamānasaḥ
gatadharmo nirānando grastagarvas tathāṭati //
171.d:
विभाति च तथा नित्यं लज्जया दग्धमानसः
गतधर्मो निरानन्दो ग्रस्तगर्वस् तथाटति ॥
171.m:
And so he constantly appears with his mind consumed by shame;
devoid of dharma, joyless, his pride swallowed up, thus he wanders.

171.s:
akaitavī ca yā vṛttiḥ sā praśastā dvijanmanām
kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyam api kuryān na kaitavam //
171.d:
अकैतवी च या वृत्तिः सा प्रशस्ता द्विजन्मनाम्
कृषिगोरक्ष्यवाणिज्यम् अपि कुर्यान् न कैतवम् ॥
171.m:
The livelihood that is free from gambling is praised for the twice-born;
even if one engages in agriculture, cattle-rearing, or trade, one should not engage in gambling.

171.s:
yas tu kaitavavṛttyā hi dhanam āhartum icchati
dharmārthakāmābhijanaiḥ sa vimucyeta pauruṣāt //
171.d:
यस् तु कैतववृत्त्या हि धनम् आहर्तुम् इच्छति
धर्मार्थकामाभिजनैः स विमुच्येत पौरुषात् ॥
171.m:
He who desires to acquire wealth through the practice of gambling
will be stripped of dharma, wealth, pleasure, high birth, and manliness.

171.s:
vede 'pi dūṣitaṃ karma tava pitrā tadādṛtam
tasmāt kiṃ kurmahe vatsa yad uktaṃ te vidhīyate //
171.d:
वेदे ऽपि दूषितं कर्म तव पित्रा तदादृतम्
तस्मात् किं कुर्महे वत्स यद् उक्तं ते विधीयते ॥
171.m:
That deed condemned even in the Veda was embraced by your father;
therefore, what can we do, dear child? What is ordained for you will take place.

171.s: vidhātṛvihitaṃ mārgaṃ ko nu vātyeti paṇḍitaḥ //
171.d: विधातृविहितं मार्गं को नु वात्येति पण्डितः ॥
171.m: Who indeed, even among the wise, can surpass the path laid down by the Ordainer?"

171.s:
brahmovāca
etat purodhaso vākyaṃ śrutvā sumatir abravīt //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतत् पुरोधसो वाक्यं श्रुत्वा सुमतिर् अब्रवीत् ॥
171.m:
Brahmā said:
Hearing these words of the priest, Sumati said:

171.s:
sumatir uvāca
kiṃ kṛtvā pramatis tātaḥ punā rājyam avāpnuyāt //
171.d:
सुमतिर् उवाच
किं कृत्वा प्रमतिस् तातः पुना राज्यम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
171.m:
Sumati said:
"What must my father Pramati do so that he may regain his kingdom?"

171.s:
brahmovāca
punar dhyātvā madhucchandāḥ sumatiṃ cedam abravīt //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुनर् ध्यात्वा मधुच्छन्दाः सुमतिं चेदम् अब्रवीत् ॥
171.m:
Brahmā said:
Madhucchandas meditated again and said this to Sumati:

171.s:
madhucchandā uvāca
gautamīṃ yāhi vatsa tvaṃ tatra pūjaya śaṃkaram
aditiṃ varuṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ tataḥ pāśād vimokṣyate //
171.d:
मधुच्छन्दा उवाच
गौतमीं याहि वत्स त्वं तत्र पूजय शंकरम्
अदितिं वरुणं विष्णुं ततः पाशाद् विमोक्ष्यते ॥
171.m:
Madhucchandas said:
"Go to the Gautamī, dear child; worship Śaṅkara there,
as well as Aditi, Varuṇa, and Viṣṇu; then he will be freed from the noose."

171.s:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā jagāmāśu gaṅgāṃ natvā janārdanam
pūjayām āsa śaṃbhuṃ ca tapas tepe yatavrataḥ //
171.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा जगामाशु गङ्गां नत्वा जनार्दनम्
पूजयाम् आस शंभुं च तपस् तेपे यतव्रतः ॥
171.m:
Brahmā said:
Saying "So be it," he went swiftly to the Gaṅgā, bowed to Janārdana,
worshipped Śambhu, and, strict in his vows, performed austerities.

171.s:
sahasram ekaṃ varṣāṇāṃ baddhaṃ pitaram ātmanaḥ
mocayām āsa devebhyaḥ punā rājyam avāpa saḥ //
171.d:
सहस्रम् एकं वर्षाणां बद्धं पितरम् आत्मनः
मोचयाम् आस देवेभ्यः पुना राज्यम् अवाप सः ॥
171.m:
For a thousand years [he performed austerities], freed his bound father
from the gods, and [the father] regained his kingdom.

171.s:
śiveśābhyāṃ muktapāśo rājyaṃ prāpa sutāt svakāt
avāpya vidyāṃ gāndharvīṃ priyaś cāsīc chatakratoḥ //
171.d:
शिवेशाभ्यां मुक्तपाशो राज्यं प्राप सुतात् स्वकात्
अवाप्य विद्यां गान्धर्वीं प्रियश् चासीच् छतक्रतोः ॥
171.m:
Freed from the nooses by Śiva and the Lord, he regained his kingdom through his own son;
having acquired the Gandharva lore, he became dear to Indra.

171.s:
śāṃbhavaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ caiva urvaśītīrtham eva ca
tataḥprabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ kaitavaṃ ceti viśrutam //
171.d:
शांभवं वैष्णवं चैव उर्वशीतीर्थम् एव च
ततःप्रभृति तत् तीर्थं कैतवं चेति विश्रुतम् ॥
171.m:
From then on, that tīrtha became renowned as
Śāmbhava, Vaiṣṇava, Urvaśītīrtha, and Kaitava.

171.s:
śivaviṣṇusarinmātuprasādād āpyate na kim
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca bahupuṇyaphalapradam
pāpapāśavimokṣaṃ tu sarvadurgatināśanam //
171.d:
शिवविष्णुसरिन्मातुप्रसादाद् आप्यते न किम्
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च बहुपुण्यफलप्रदम्
पापपाशविमोक्षं तु सर्वदुर्गतिनाशनम् ॥
171.m:
What is not attained by the grace of Śiva, Viṣṇu, and the Mother of Rivers?
Bathing and gifting there bestow the fruit of great merit,
giving release from the nooses of sin and destroying all misfortune.

172.s:
brahmovāca
sāmudraṃ tīrtham ākhyātaṃ sarvatīrthaphalapradam
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tanmanāḥ //
172.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सामुद्रं तीर्थम् आख्यातं सर्वतीर्थफलप्रदम्
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद तन्मनाः ॥

172.s:
visṛṣṭā gautamenāsau gaṅgā pāpapraṇāśanī
lokānām upakārārthaṃ prāyāt pūrvārṇavaṃ prati //
172.d:
विसृष्टा गौतमेनासौ गङ्गा पापप्रणाशनी
लोकानाम् उपकारार्थं प्रायात् पूर्वार्णवं प्रति ॥
172.m:
Released by Gautama, this Gaṅgā, the destroyer of sins,
flowed toward the eastern ocean for the benefit of the worlds.

172.s:
āgacchantī devanadī kamaṇḍaludhṛtā mayā
śirasā ca dhṛtā devī śaṃbhunā paramātmanā //
172.d:
आगच्छन्ती देवनदी कमण्डलुधृता मया
शिरसा च धृता देवी शंभुना परमात्मना ॥
172.m:
As the divine river approached, she was held in the water-pot by me,
and the goddess was held on the head by Śambhu, the supreme self.

172.s:
viṣṇupādāt prasūtāṃ tāṃ brāhmaṇena mahātmanā
ānītāṃ martyabhavanaṃ smaraṇād aghanāśanīm //
172.d:
विष्णुपादात् प्रसूतां तां ब्राह्मणेन महात्मना
आनीतां मर्त्यभवनं स्मरणाद् अघनाशनीम् ॥
172.m:
Born from the foot of Viṣṇu, brought to the mortal realm by that great-souled brāhmaṇa,
she destroys sins by mere remembrance.

172.s:
guror gurutamāṃ sindhur dṛṣṭvā kṛtyam acintayat
yā vandyā jagatām īśā brahmeśādyair namaskṛtā //
172.d:
गुरोर् गुरुतमां सिन्धुर् दृष्ट्वा कृत्यम् अचिन्तयत्
या वन्द्या जगताम् ईशा ब्रह्मेशाद्यैर् नमस्कृता ॥
172.m:
Seeing her, the most venerable of teachers, the ocean reflected on his duty:
'She who is to be worshipped, ruler of the worlds, saluted by Brahmā, Īśa, and others—

172.s:
tām ahaṃ pratigaccheyaṃ no cet syād dharmadūṣaṇam
āgacchantaṃ mahātmānaṃ yo mohān nopatiṣṭhate //
172.d:
ताम् अहं प्रतिगच्छेयं नो चेत् स्याद् धर्मदूषणम्
आगच्छन्तं महात्मानं यो मोहान् नोपतिष्ठते ॥
172.m:
I should go forward to meet her; otherwise it would be a violation of dharma.
He who out of delusion does not rise to greet a great soul who is approaching—

172.s:
na tasya kopi trātāsti pāpino lokayor dvayoḥ
evaṃ vimṛśya ratneśo mūrtimān vinayānvitaḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭo gaṅgām āhedaṃ saritāṃpatiḥ //
172.d:
न तस्य कोपि त्रातास्ति पापिनो लोकयोर् द्वयोः
एवं विमृश्य रत्नेशो मूर्तिमान् विनयान्वितः
कृताञ्जलिपुटो गङ्गाम् आहेदं सरितांपतिः ॥
172.m:
that sinner has no protector in either of the two worlds.'
Reflecting thus, the lord of jewels, embodied, filled with humility,
joined his palms reverently and spoke this to the Gaṅgā, the lord of rivers [saying]:

172.s:
sindhur uvāca
rasātalagataṃ vāri pṛthivyāṃ yan nabhastale
tan mām evātra viśatu nāhaṃ vakṣyāmi kiṃcana //
172.d:
सिन्धुर् उवाच
रसातलगतं वारि पृथिव्यां यन् नभस्तले
तन् माम् एवात्र विशतु नाहं वक्ष्यामि किंचन ॥
172.m:
The Ocean said:
'Whatever water there is in the nether world, on the earth, or in the sky—
let that enter into me here; I shall say nothing [in protest].

172.s:
mayi ratnāni pīyūṣaṃ parvatā rākṣasāsurāḥ
etān apy akhilān anyān bhīmān saṃdhārayāmy aham //
172.d:
मयि रत्नानि पीयूषं पर्वता राक्षसासुराः
एतान् अप्य् अखिलान् अन्यान् भीमान् संधारयाम्य् अहम् ॥
172.m:
In me are jewels, nectar, mountains, Rākṣasas, and Asuras;
even all these other formidable things I sustain.

172.s:
mamāntaḥ kamalāyukto viṣṇuḥ svapiti nityadā
mamāśakyaṃ na kimapi vidyate sacarācare //
172.d:
ममान्तः कमलायुक्तो विष्णुः स्वपिति नित्यदा
ममाशक्यं न किमपि विद्यते सचराचरे ॥
172.m:
Within me, Viṣṇu sleeps perpetually accompanied by Kamalā;
nothing whatsoever is impossible for me among the moving and unmoving.

172.s:
mahaty abhyāgate kuryāt pratyutthānaṃ na yo madāt
sa dharmādiparibhraṣṭo nirayaṃ tu samāpnuyāt //
172.d:
महत्य् अभ्यागते कुर्यात् प्रत्युत्थानं न यो मदात्
स धर्मादिपरिभ्रष्टो निरयं तु समाप्नुयात् ॥
172.m:
He who out of arrogance does not rise to greet a great person who has arrived,
having fallen from dharma and the rest, would surely go to hell.

172.s:
na tān me bibhrataḥ khedo vināgastyaparābhavāt
kiṃ tu tvaṃ gauraveṇaiṣām atiriktā tatas tv aham //
172.d:
न तान् मे बिभ्रतः खेदो विनागस्त्यपराभवात्
किं तु त्वं गौरवेणैषाम् अतिरिक्ता ततस् त्व् अहम् ॥
172.m:
There is no weariness for me in bearing them, except for the humiliation from Agastya;
nevertheless, you surpass these [all] in greatness; therefore I

172.s:
bravīmi devi gaṅge māṃ tvaṃ sāmyāt saṃgatā bhava
naikarūpām ahaṃ śaktaḥ saṃgantuṃ bahudhā yadi //
172.d:
ब्रवीमि देवि गङ्गे मां त्वं साम्यात् संगता भव
नैकरूपाम् अहं शक्तः संगन्तुं बहुधा यदि ॥
172.m:
say, O goddess Gaṅgā, unite with me as an equal;
I am unable to unite with you in manifold forms if you do not come in a single form.'

172.s:
saṅgam eṣyasi devi tvaṃ saṃgacche 'haṃ na cānyathā
gaṅge sameṣyasi yadi bahudhā tad vicāraye //
172.d:
सङ्गम् एष्यसि देवि त्वं संगच्छे ऽहं न चान्यथा
गङ्गे समेष्यसि यदि बहुधा तद् विचारये ॥
172.m: You will unite with me, O goddess, and I will unite with you, not otherwise. / If you will unite in many streams, O Gaṅgā, then I shall consider it.”

172.s:
brahmovāca
tam evaṃvādinaṃ sindhum apām īśaṃ tadābravīt
gaṅgā sā gautamī devī kuru caitad vaco mama //
172.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तम् एवंवादिनं सिन्धुम् अपाम् ईशं तदाब्रवीत्
गङ्गा सा गौतमी देवी कुरु चैतद् वचो मम ॥
172.m: Brahmā said: / To the Ocean, the lord of waters, who was speaking thus, / the goddess Gaṅgā, the Gautamī, then replied: “Fulfill this word of mine:

172.s:
saptarṣīṇāṃ ca yā bhāryā arundhatipurogamāḥ
bhartṛbhiḥ sahitāḥ sarvā ānaya tvaṃ tadā tv aham //
172.d:
सप्तर्षीणां च या भार्या अरुन्धतिपुरोगमाः
भर्तृभिः सहिताः सर्वा आनय त्वं तदा त्व् अहम् ॥
172.m: Bring all the wives of the Seven Sages, headed by Arundhatī, / together with their husbands; then I

172.s:
alpabhūtā bhaviṣyāmi tataḥ syāṃ tava saṃgatā
tathety uktvā saptarṣīṇāṃ bhāryābhir ṛṣibhir vṛtaḥ //
172.d:
अल्पभूता भविष्यामि ततः स्यां तव संगता
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा सप्तर्षीणां भार्याभिर् ऋषिभिर् वृतः ॥
172.m: shall become small, and thereupon I may unite with you.” / Saying “So be it,” accompanied by the sages with the wives of the Seven Sages,

172.s:
ānayām āsa tāṃ devī saptadhā sā vyabhajyata
sā ceyaṃ gautamī gaṅgā saptadhā sāgaraṃ gatā //
172.d:
आनयाम् आस तां देवी सप्तधा सा व्यभज्यत
सा चेयं गौतमी गङ्गा सप्तधा सागरं गता ॥
172.m: he brought that goddess, and she divided into seven parts. / And this Gautamī Gaṅgā entered the ocean in seven streams.

172.s:
saptarṣīṇāṃ tu nāmnā tu sapta gaṅgās tato 'bhavan
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca śravaṇaṃ paṭhanaṃ tathā //
172.d:
सप्तर्षीणां तु नाम्ना तु सप्त गङ्गास् ततो ऽभवन्
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च श्रवणं पठनं तथा ॥
172.m: From the names of the Seven Sages there then arose the seven Gaṅgās. / Bathing, charitable giving, listening, and reciting there,

172.s:
smaraṇaṃ cāpi yad bhaktyā sarvakāmapradaṃ bhavet
nāsmād anyat paraṃ tīrthaṃ samudrād bhuvanatraye
pāpahānau bhuktimuktiprāptau ca manaso mude //
172.d:
स्मरणं चापि यद् भक्त्या सर्वकामप्रदं भवेत्
नास्माद् अन्यत् परं तीर्थं समुद्राद् भुवनत्रये
पापहानौ भुक्तिमुक्तिप्राप्तौ च मनसो मुदे ॥
172.m: as well as remembering with devotion, grants all desires. / In the three worlds there is no higher tīrtha than this ocean / for the destruction of sin, for the attainment of enjoyment and liberation, and for the joy of the mind.

173.s:
brahmovāca
ṛṣisattram iti khyātam ṛṣayaḥ sapta nārada
niṣedus tapase yatra yatra bhīmeśvaraḥ śivaḥ //
173.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ऋषिसत्त्रम् इति ख्यातम् ऋषयः सप्त नारद
निषेदुस् तपसे यत्र यत्र भीमेश्वरः शिवः ॥
173.m: Brahmā said: / In the place known as the Sages' Session, where the Seven Sages, O Nārada, / sat down for austerities, and where Śiva is Bhīmeśvara,

173.s:
tatredaṃ vṛttam ākhyāsye devarṣipitṛbṛṃhitam
śṛṇu yatnena vakṣyāmi sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham //
173.d:
तत्रेदं वृत्तम् आख्यास्ये देवर्षिपितृबृंहितम्
शृणु यत्नेन वक्ष्यामि सर्वकामप्रदं शुभम् ॥
173.m: I shall narrate this account there, enhanced by divine sages and ancestors. / Listen with care; I will recount it, auspicious and granting all desires.

173.s:
saptadhā vyabhajan gaṅgām ṛṣayaḥ sapta nārada
vāsiṣṭhī dākṣiṇeyī syād vaiśvāmitrī taduttarā //
173.d:
सप्तधा व्यभजन् गङ्गाम् ऋषयः सप्त नारद
वासिष्ठी दाक्षिणेयी स्याद् वैश्वामित्री तदुत्तरा ॥
173.m: The Seven Sages divided the Gaṅgā sevenfold, O Nārada: / Vāsiṣṭhī would be the southern stream, and Vaiśvāmitrī the one to its north;

173.s:
vāmadevy aparā jñeyā gautamī madhyataḥ śubhā
bhāradvājī smṛtā cānyā ātreyī cety athāparā //
173.d:
वामदेव्य् अपरा ज्ञेया गौतमी मध्यतः शुभा
भारद्वाजी स्मृता चान्या आत्रेयी चेत्य् अथापरा ॥
173.m: Vāmadevī is to be known as another, and the auspicious Gautamī in the middle; / another is remembered as Bhāradvājī, and another as Ātreyī;

173.s:
jāmadagnī tathā cānyā vyapadiṣṭā tu saptadhā
taiḥ sarvair ṛṣibhis tatra yaṣṭum iṣṭair mahātmabhiḥ //
173.d:
जामदग्नी तथा चान्या व्यपदिष्टा तु सप्तधा
तैः सर्वैर् ऋषिभिस् तत्र यष्टुम् इष्टैर् महात्मभिः ॥
173.m: and yet another is Jāmadagnī; thus it is designated sevenfold. / There, by all those noble sages desirous of sacrificing,

173.s:
niṣpāditaṃ mahāsattram ṛṣibhiḥ pāradarśibhiḥ
etasminn antare tatra devānāṃ prabalo ripuḥ //
173.d:
निष्पादितं महासत्त्रम् ऋषिभिः पारदर्शिभिः
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र देवानां प्रबलो रिपुः ॥
173.m: a great sacrificial session was performed by the sages who see the beyond. / In the meantime, the mighty enemy of the gods,

173.s:
viśvarūpa iti khyāto munīnāṃ sattram abhyagāt
brahmacaryeṇa tapasā tān ārādhya yathāvidhi
vinayenātha papraccha ṛṣīn sarvān anukramāt //
173.d:
विश्वरूप इति ख्यातो मुनीनां सत्त्रम् अभ्यगात्
ब्रह्मचर्येण तपसा तान् आराध्य यथाविधि
विनयेनाथ पप्रच्छ ऋषीन् सर्वान् अनुक्रमात् ॥
173.m: known as Viśvarūpa, approached the sages' sacrificial session. / Having properly propitiated them through celibacy and ascetic heat, / he then humbly questioned all the sages in turn.

173.s:
viśvarūpa uvāca
dhruvaṃ sarve yathākāmaṃ mama svāsthyena hetunā
yathā syād balavān putro devānām api durdharaḥ
yajñair vā tapasā vāpi munayo vaktum arhatha //
173.d:
विश्वरूप उवाच
ध्रुवं सर्वे यथाकामं मम स्वास्थ्येन हेतुना
यथा स्याद् बलवान् पुत्रो देवानाम् अपि दुर्धरः
यज्ञैर् वा तपसा वापि मुनयो वक्तुम् अर्हथ ॥
173.m: Viśvarūpa said: / “Assuredly all of you, according to desire, for the sake of my well-being, / should tell me how a strong son, unendurable even to the gods, / may be obtained by sacrifices or by tapas, O sages.”

173.s:
brahmovāca
tatra prāha mahābuddhir viśvāmitro mahāmanāḥ //
173.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तत्र प्राह महाबुद्धिर् विश्वामित्रो महामनाः ॥
173.m: Brahmā said: / Thereupon the very wise and high-minded Viśvāmitra spoke:

173.s:
viśvāmitra uvāca
karmaṇā tāta labhyante phalāni vividhāni ca
trayāṇāṃ kāraṇānāṃ ca karma prathamakāraṇam //
173.d:
विश्वामित्र उवाच
कर्मणा तात लभ्यन्ते फलानि विविधानि च
त्रयाणां कारणानां च कर्म प्रथमकारणम् ॥
173.m: Viśvāmitra said: / “Through action, my dear child, manifold fruits are obtained. / And among the three causes, action is the primary cause.

173.s:
tataś ca kāraṇaṃ kartā tataś cānyat prakīrtitam
upādānaṃ tathā bījaṃ na ca karma vidur budhāḥ //
173.d:
ततश् च कारणं कर्ता ततश् चान्यत् प्रकीर्तितम्
उपादानं तथा बीजं न च कर्म विदुर् बुधाः ॥
173.m: From that the agent is the cause, and another is proclaimed beyond that; / the wise do not consider the material cause or the seed to be action.

173.s:
karmaṇāṃ kāraṇatvaṃ ca kāraṇe puṣkale sati
bhāvābhāvau phale dṛṣṭau tasmāt karmāśritaṃ phalam //
173.d:
कर्मणां कारणत्वं च कारणे पुष्कले सति
भावाभावौ फले दृष्टौ तस्मात् कर्माश्रितं फलम् ॥
173.m: And action is the cause when the cause is abundant: / presence and absence are observed in the fruit; therefore the fruit depends on action.

173.s:
karmāpi dvividhaṃ jñeyaṃ kriyamāṇaṃ tathā kṛtam
kartavyaṃ kriyamāṇasya sādhanaṃ yad yad ucyate //
173.d:
कर्मापि द्विविधं ज्ञेयं क्रियमाणं तथा कृतम्
कर्तव्यं क्रियमाणस्य साधनं यद् यद् उच्यते ॥
173.m: Action also is to be understood as twofold: that which is being done and that which has been done. / Whatever means is spoken of for what is to be done,

173.s:
tadbhāvāḥ karmasiddhau ca ubhayatrāpi kāraṇam
yad yad bhāvayate jantuḥ karma kurvan vicakṣaṇaḥ //
173.d:
तद्भावाः कर्मसिद्धौ च उभयत्रापि कारणम्
यद् यद् भावयते जन्तुः कर्म कुर्वन् विचक्षणः ॥
173.m: the intentions regarding that are the cause in the accomplishment of action in both cases. / Whatever a creature conceives while performing action wisely,

173.s:
tadbhāvanānurūpeṇa phalaniṣpattir ucyate
karoti karma vidhivad vinā bhāvanayā yadi //
173.d:
तद्भावनानुरूपेण फलनिष्पत्तिर् उच्यते
करोति कर्म विधिवद् विना भावनया यदि ॥
173.m: the production of the fruit is said to correspond to that intention. / If one performs an action according to rule, but without intention,

173.s:
anyathā syāt phalaṃ sarvaṃ tasya bhāvānurūpataḥ
tasmāt tapo vrataṃ dānaṃ japayajñādikāḥ kriyāḥ //
173.d:
अन्यथा स्यात् फलं सर्वं तस्य भावानुरूपतः
तस्मात् तपो व्रतं दानं जपयज्ञादिकाः क्रियाः ॥
173.m: the entire fruit will be otherwise, in accordance with one's intention. / Therefore austerities, vows, gifts, rituals such as recitation and sacrifice,

173.s:
karmaṇas tv anurūpeṇa phalaṃ dāsyanti bhāvataḥ
tasmād bhāvānurūpeṇa karma vai dāsyate phalam //
173.d:
कर्मणस् त्व् अनुरूपेण फलं दास्यन्ति भावतः
तस्माद् भावानुरूपेण कर्म वै दास्यते फलम् ॥
173.m: will yield fruit in accordance with the action, through intention. / Therefore, action will indeed grant fruit corresponding to intention.

173.s:
bhāvas tu trividho jñeyaḥ sāttviko rājasas tathā
tāmasas tu tathā jñeyaḥ phalaṃ karmānusārataḥ //
173.d:
भावस् तु त्रिविधो ज्ञेयः सात्त्विको राजसस् तथा
तामसस् तु तथा ज्ञेयः फलं कर्मानुसारतः ॥
173.m: And intention is to be known as threefold: sāttvika, rājasa, / and tāmasa; the fruit corresponds to the action,

173.s:
bhāvanānuguṇaṃ ceti vicitrā karmaṇāṃ sthitiḥ
tasmād icchānusāreṇa bhāvaṃ kuryād vicakṣaṇaḥ //
173.d:
भावनानुगुणं चेति विचित्रा कर्मणां स्थितिः
तस्माद् इच्छानुसारेण भावं कुर्याद् विचक्षणः ॥
173.m: and conforms to the intention—such is the manifold nature of actions. / Therefore the wise person should form his intention according to his wish,

173.s:
paścāt karmāpi kartavyaṃ phaladātāpi tadvidham
phalaṃ dadāti phalināṃ phale yadi pravartate //
173.d:
पश्चात् कर्मापि कर्तव्यं फलदातापि तद्विधम्
फलं ददाति फलिनां फले यदि प्रवर्तते ॥
173.m: and afterwards the action should also be performed. The bestower of fruit likewise / grants such fruit to those entitled to it, if he proceeds toward the fruit.

173.s:
karmakāro na tatrāsti kuryāt karma svabhāvataḥ
tad eva copadānādi sattvādiguṇabhedataḥ //
173.d:
कर्मकारो न तत्रास्ति कुर्यात् कर्म स्वभावतः
तद् एव चोपदानादि सत्त्वादिगुणभेदतः ॥
173.m: The agent of action does not exist apart from that; he performs action by his own nature. / And that very material cause and the rest, through the distinction of qualities such as sattva,

173.s:
bhāvāt prārabhate tadvad bhāvaiḥ phalam avāpyate
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ karma caiva hi kāraṇam //
173.d:
भावात् प्रारभते तद्वद् भावैः फलम् अवाप्यते
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां कर्म चैव हि कारणम् ॥
173.m: undertakes from intention, and likewise the fruit is obtained through intentions. / Action is indeed the cause of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation.

173.s:
bhāvasthitaṃ bhavet karma muktidaṃ bandhakāraṇam
svabhāvānuguṇaṃ karma svasyaiveha paratra ca //
173.d:
भावस्थितं भवेत् कर्म मुक्तिदं बन्धकारणम्
स्वभावानुगुणं कर्म स्वस्यैवेह परत्र च ॥
173.m: An action grounded in intention can grant liberation or be a cause of bondage. / An action that conforms to one's own nature, here and hereafter,

173.s:
phalāni vividhāny āśu karoti samatānugam
eka eva padārtho 'sau bhāvair bhedaḥ pradṛśyate //
173.d:
फलानि विविधान्य् आशु करोति समतानुगम्
एक एव पदार्थो ऽसौ भावैर् भेदः प्रदृश्यते ॥
173.m: quickly produces manifold fruits following equanimity. / That entity is only one; difference is perceived through intentions.

173.s:
kriyate bhujyate vāpi tasmād bhāvo viśiṣyate
yathābhāvaṃ karma kuru yathepsitam avāpsyasi //
173.d:
क्रियते भुज्यते वापि तस्माद् भावो विशिष्यते
यथाभावं कर्म कुरु यथेप्सितम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
173.m: It is performed or it is experienced; therefore intention is pre-eminent. / Perform action according to your intention; you will obtain what is desired.”

173.s:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā ṛṣer vākyaṃ viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ
tapas taptvā bahukālaṃ tāmasaṃ bhāvam āśritaḥ //
173.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा ऋषेर् वाक्यं विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः
तपस् तप्त्वा बहुकालं तामसं भावम् आश्रितः ॥
173.m: Brahmā said: / Having heard these words of the wise sage Viśvāmitra, / and having practiced tapas for a long time, resorting to a tāmasa intention,

173.s:
viśvarūpaḥ karma bhīmaṃ cakāra surabhīṣaṇam
paśyatsu ṛṣimukhyeṣu vāryamāṇo 'pi nityaśaḥ //
173.d:
विश्वरूपः कर्म भीमं चकार सुरभीषणम्
पश्यत्सु ऋषिमुख्येषु वार्यमाणो ऽपि नित्यशः ॥
173.m: Viśvarūpa performed a terrible rite, frightening even to the gods. / While the foremost sages looked on, though repeatedly forbidden by them,

173.s:
ātmakopānusāreṇa bhīmaṃ karma tathākarot
bhīṣaṇe kuṇḍakhāte tu bhīṣaṇe jātavedasi //
173.d:
आत्मकोपानुसारेण भीमं कर्म तथाकरोत्
भीषणे कुण्डखाते तु भीषणे जातवेदसि ॥
173.m: he performed the terrible rite according to his own rage. / In a frightful sacrificial pit, into the frightful Fire,

173.s:
bhīṣaṇaṃ raudrapuruṣaṃ dhyātvātmānaṃ guhāśayam
evaṃ tapantam ālakṣya vāg uvācāśarīriṇī //
173.d:
भीषणं रौद्रपुरुषं ध्यात्वात्मानं गुहाशयम्
एवं तपन्तम् आलक्ष्य वाग् उवाचाशरीरिणी ॥
173.m: having meditated on himself dwelling in the cave [of the heart] as a frightful Rudra-like puruṣa— / seeing him thus engaged in ascetic heat, a bodiless voice spoke:

173.s:
jaṭājūṭaṃ vinātmānaṃ na ca vṛtro vyajīyata
vṛthātmānaṃ viśvarūpo juhuyāj jātavedasi //
173.d:
जटाजूटं विनात्मानं न च वृत्रो व्यजीयत
वृथात्मानं विश्वरूपो जुहुयाज् जातवेदसि ॥
173.m: “Without his self, [offered as] a matted lock of hair, Vṛtra was not conquered. / In vain would Viśvarūpa offer himself into Fire.

173.s:
sa evendraḥ sa varuṇaḥ sa ca syāt sarvam eva ca
tyaktvātmānaṃ jaṭāmātraṃ hutavān vṛjinodbhavaḥ //
173.d:
स एवेन्द्रः स वरुणः स च स्यात् सर्वम् एव च
त्यक्त्वात्मानं जटामात्रं हुतवान् वृजिनोद्भवः ॥
173.m: He alone is Indra, he is Varuṇa, and he indeed would be everything. / Leaving his self aside, the one born of affliction offered only a matted lock.

173.s:
vṛtra ity ucyate vede sa cāpi vṛjino 'bhavat
bhīmasya mahimānaṃ ko jānāti jagadīśituḥ //
173.d:
वृत्र इत्य् उच्यते वेदे स चापि वृजिनो ऽभवत्
भीमस्य महिमानं को जानाति जगदीशितुः ॥
173.m: He is called Vṛtra in the Veda, and he too became afflicted. / Who knows the greatness of Bhīma, the lord of the universe,

173.s:
sṛjaty aśeṣam api yo na ca saṅgena lipyate
virarāmeti saṃkīrtya sā vāṇy enaṃ munīśvarāḥ //
173.d:
सृजत्य् अशेषम् अपि यो न च सङ्गेन लिप्यते
विररामेति संकीर्त्य सा वाण्य् एनं मुनीश्वराः ॥
173.m: who creates the entire universe and is not tainted by attachment?” / Having proclaimed this to him, that voice ceased, O best of sages.

173.s:
bhīmeśvaraṃ namaskṛtya jagmuḥ svaṃ svam athāśramam
viśvarūpo mahābhīmo bhīmakarmā tathākṛtiḥ //
173.d:
भीमेश्वरं नमस्कृत्य जग्मुः स्वं स्वम् अथाश्रमम्
विश्वरूपो महाभीमो भीमकर्मा तथाकृतिः ॥
173.m: Having bowed to Bhīmeśvara, they then went to their respective hermitages. / Viśvarūpa was exceedingly terrible, of terrible deeds and of like form.

173.s:
bhīmabhāvo bhīmatanuṃ dhyātvātmānaṃ juhāva ha
tasmād bhīmeśvaro devaḥ purāṇe paripaṭhyate
tatra snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca muktidaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ //
173.d:
भीमभावो भीमतनुं ध्यात्वात्मानं जुहाव ह
तस्माद् भीमेश्वरो देवः पुराणे परिपठ्यते
तत्र स्नानं च दानं च मुक्तिदं नात्र संशयः ॥
173.m: Having meditated upon his own terrible state and terrible body, he sacrificed himself; / therefore the god is celebrated in the Purāṇa as Bhīmeśvara. / Bathing and making gifts there bestow liberation; there is no doubt about this.

173.s:
iti paṭhati śṛṇoti yaś ca bhaktyā
vibudhapatiṃ śivam atra bhīmarūpam
jagati viditam aśeṣapāpahāri
smṛtipadaśaraṇena muktidaś ca
173.d:
इति पठति शृणोति यश् च भक्त्या
विबुधपतिं शिवम् अत्र भीमरूपम्
जगति विदितम् अशेषपापहारि
स्मृतिपदशरणेन मुक्तिदश् च
173.m: He who reads or hears with devotion about the lord of the gods, / Śiva in this fearful form, celebrated in the world, / who takes away all sins, / bestows liberation through taking refuge at the mention of his name.

173.s:
godāvarī tāvad aśeṣapāpa
samūhahantrī paramārthadātrī
sadaiva sarvatra viśeṣatas tu
yatrāmburāśiṃ samanupraviṣṭā
173.d:
गोदावरी तावद् अशेषपाप
समूहहन्त्री परमार्थदात्री
सदैव सर्वत्र विशेषतस् तु
यत्राम्बुराशिं समनुप्रविष्टा
173.m: The Godāvarī indeed destroys all multitude of sins / and bestows the ultimate reality / always and everywhere, but especially / where it enters the ocean.

173.s:
snātvā tu tasmin sukṛtī śarīrī
godāvarīvāridhisaṃgame yaḥ
uddhṛtya tīvrān nirayād aśeṣāt
sa pūrvajān yāti puraṃ purāreḥ
173.d:
स्नात्वा तु तस्मिन् सुकृती शरीरी
गोदावरीवारिधिसंगमे यः
उद्धृत्य तीव्रान् निरयाद् अशेषात्
स पूर्वजान् याति पुरं पुरारेः
173.m: A meritorious embodied soul, having bathed in that confluence / of the Godāvarī and the ocean, / raises his ancestors from severe and endless hell / and goes to the city of the enemy of Pura.

173.s:
vedāntavedyaṃ yad upāsitavyaṃ
tad brahma sākṣāt khalu bhīmanāthaḥ
dṛṣṭe hi tasmin na punar viśanti
śarīriṇaḥ saṃsmṛtim ugraduḥkhām
173.d:
वेदान्तवेद्यं यद् उपासितव्यं
तद् ब्रह्म साक्षात् खलु भीमनाथः
दृष्टे हि तस्मिन् न पुनर् विशन्ति
शरीरिणः संस्मृतिम् उग्रदुःखाम्
173.m: That Brahman, which is to be known through the Vedānta and worshipped, / is indeed directly the lord Bhīmanātha. / For when he is seen, embodied souls do not enter again / into the cycle of worldly existence, which is full of fierce suffering.

174.s:
brahmovāca
sā saṃgatā pūrvam apāṃpatiṃ taṃ
gaṅgā surāṇām api vandanīyā
devaiś ca sarvair anugamyamānā
saṃstūyamānā munibhir marudbhiḥ
174.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सा संगता पूर्वम् अपांपतिं तं
गङ्गा सुराणाम् अपि वन्दनीया
देवैश् च सर्वैर् अनुगम्यमाना
संस्तूयमाना मुनिभिर् मरुद्भिः
174.m: Brahmā said: / In ancient times, that Gaṅgā, worthy of worship even by the gods, / joined that lord of waters, / followed by all the gods / and praised by the sages and the Maruts.

174.s:
vasiṣṭhajābālisayājñavalkya
kratvaṅgirodakṣamarīcivaiṣṇavāḥ
śātātapaḥ śaunakadevarāta
bhṛgvagniveśyātrimarīcimukhyāḥ
174.d:
वसिष्ठजाबालिसयाज्ञवल्क्य
क्रत्वङ्गिरोदक्षमरीचिवैष्णवाः
शातातपः शौनकदेवरात
भृग्वग्निवेश्यात्रिमरीचिमुख्याः
174.m: Vasiṣṭha, Jābāli, along with Yājñavalkya, / Kratu, Aṅgiras, Dakṣa, Marīci, the Vaiṣṇavas, / Śātātapa, Śaunaka, Devarāta, / Bhṛgu, Agniveśya, Atri, Marīci, and other foremost [sages],

174.s:
sudhūtapāpā manugautamādayaḥ
sakauśikās tumbaruparvatādyāḥ
agastyamārkaṇḍasapippalādyāḥ
sagālavā yogaparāyaṇāś ca
174.d:
सुधूतपापा मनुगौतमादयः
सकौशिकास् तुम्बरुपर्वताद्याः
अगस्त्यमार्कण्डसपिप्पलाद्याः
सगालवा योगपरायणाश् च
174.m: their sins thoroughly washed away: Manu, Gautama, and others, / along with Kauśika, Tumburu, Parvata, and others, / Agastya, Mārkaṇḍa, along with Pippala and others, / along with Gālava, dedicated to yoga,

174.s:
savāmadevāṅgiraso 'tha bhārgavāḥ
smṛtipravīṇāḥ śrutibhir manojñāḥ
sarve purāṇārthavido bahujñās
te gautamīṃ devanadīṃ tu gatvā
174.d:
सवामदेवाङ्गिरसो ऽथ भार्गवाः
स्मृतिप्रवीणाः श्रुतिभिर् मनोज्ञाः
सर्वे पुराणार्थविदो बहुज्ञास्
ते गौतमीं देवनदीं तु गत्वा
174.m: along with Vāmadeva, the Aṅgirases, and the Bhārgavas, / skilled in the Smṛti, pleasing with Vedic scriptures, / all knowers of the meaning of the Purāṇas, men of great learning; / having gone to the divine river Gautamī,

174.s:
stoṣyanti mantraiḥ śrutibhiḥ prabhūtair
hṛdyaiś ca tuṣṭair muditair manobhiḥ
tāṃ saṃgatāṃ vīkṣya śivo hariś ca
ātmānam ādarśayatāṃ munibhyaḥ
174.d:
स्तोष्यन्ति मन्त्रैः श्रुतिभिः प्रभूतैर्
हृद्यैश् च तुष्टैर् मुदितैर् मनोभिः
तां संगतां वीक्ष्य शिवो हरिश् च
आत्मानम् आदर्शयतां मुनिभ्यः
174.m: they will praise [her] with abundant Vedic mantras / and pleasing, contented, and joyous minds. / Seeing that she had met [the ocean], Śiva and Hari / revealed themselves to the sages.

174.s:
ādityā vasavo rudrā maruto lokapālakāḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve stuvanti hariśaṃkarau //
174.d:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा मरुतो लोकपालकाः
कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे स्तुवन्ति हरिशंकरौ ॥
174.m: The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Maruts, and world-protectors, / all with folded hands, praise Hari and Śaṅkara.

174.s:
saṃgameṣu prasiddheṣu nityaṃ saptasu nārada
samudrasya ca gaṅgāyā nityaṃ devau pratiṣṭhitau //
174.d:
संगमेषु प्रसिद्धेषु नित्यं सप्तसु नारद
समुद्रस्य च गङ्गाया नित्यं देवौ प्रतिष्ठितौ ॥
174.m: O Nārada, at the seven renowned confluences / of the ocean and the Gaṅgā, / the two gods are eternally established.

174.s:
gautameśvara ākhyāto yatra devo maheśvaraḥ
nityaṃ saṃnihitas tatra mādhavo ramayā saha //
174.d:
गौतमेश्वर आख्यातो यत्र देवो महेश्वरः
नित्यं संनिहितस् तत्र माधवो रमया सह ॥
174.m: Where the god is celebrated as Gautameśvara, the great lord, / there Mādhava is eternally present along with Ramā.

174.s:
brahmeśvara iti khyāto mayaiva sthāpitaḥ śivaḥ
lokānām upakārārtham ātmanaḥ kāraṇāntare //
174.d:
ब्रह्मेश्वर इति ख्यातो मयैव स्थापितः शिवः
लोकानाम् उपकारार्थम् आत्मनः कारणान्तरे ॥
174.m: Śiva was installed by me alone as known by the name Brahmeśvara, / for the welfare of the worlds, for a special reason of my own.

174.s:
cakrapāṇir iti khyātaḥ stuto devair mayā saha
tatra saṃnihito viṣṇur devaiḥ saha marudgaṇaiḥ //
174.d:
चक्रपाणिर् इति ख्यातः स्तुतो देवैर् मया सह
तत्र संनिहितो विष्णुर् देवैः सह मरुद्गणैः ॥
174.m: He is praised as Cakrapāṇi by the gods along with me; / Viṣṇu is present there along with the gods and the hosts of Maruts.

174.s:
aindratīrtham iti khyātaṃ tad eva hayamūrdhakam
hayamūrdhā tatra viṣṇus tanmūrdhani surā api
somatīrtham iti khyātaṃ yatra someśvaraḥ śivaḥ //
174.d:
ऐन्द्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं तद् एव हयमूर्धकम्
हयमूर्धा तत्र विष्णुस् तन्मूर्धनि सुरा अपि
सोमतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं यत्र सोमेश्वरः शिवः ॥
174.m: It is known as Aindratīrtha, and that very one is Hayamūrdhaka; / there Viṣṇu is Hayamūrdhan, and the gods are upon his head. / It is known as Somatīrtha where Śiva is Someśvara.

174.s:
indrasya somaśravaso devaiś ca ṛṣibhis tathā
prārthitaḥ soma evādāv indrāyendo parisrava //
174.d:
इन्द्रस्य सोमश्रवसो देवैश् च ऋषिभिस् तथा
प्रार्थितः सोम एवादाव् इन्द्रायेन्दो परिस्रव ॥
174.m: By Indra, who listens to the soma, and by the gods and the sages, / Soma was prayed to at the beginning: 'Flow around for Indra, O Indu!'

174.s:
sapta diśo nānāsūryāḥ sapta hotāra ṛtvijaḥ
devā ādityā ye sapta tebhiḥ somābhirakṣa na //
174.d:
सप्त दिशो नानासूर्याः सप्त होतार ऋत्विजः
देवा आदित्या ये सप्त तेभिः सोमाभिरक्ष न ॥
174.m:
The seven directions, the various suns, the seven Hotṛ priests;
by those gods who are the seven Ādityas, protect us, O Soma! / Flow, drop, for Indra!

174.s:
yat te rājañ chṛtaṃ havis tena somābhirakṣa naḥ
arātīvā mā nas tārīn mo ca naḥ kiṃcanāmamad //
174.d:
यत् ते राजञ् छृतं हविस् तेन सोमाभिरक्ष नः
अरातीवा मा नस् तारीन् मो च नः किंचनाममद् ॥
174.m:
With that oblation of yours, O King, which has been cooked, protect us, O Soma!
May the malicious one not overcome us, and may nothing cause us distress! / Flow, drop, for Indra!

174.s:
ṛṣe mantrakṛtāṃ stomaiḥ kaśyapodvardhayan giraḥ
somaṃ namasya rājānaṃ yo jajñe vīrudhāṃ patir //
174.d:
ऋषे मन्त्रकृतां स्तोमैः कश्यपोद्वर्धयन् गिरः
सोमं नमस्य राजानं यो जज्ञे वीरुधां पतिर् ॥
174.m:
O sage Kaśyapa, exalting your words with the praises of the hymn-makers,
pay homage to King Soma, who was born as lord of plants! / Flow, drop, for Indra!

174.s:
kārur ahaṃ tato bhiṣag upalaprakṣiṇī nanā
nānādhiyo vasūyavo 'nu gā iva tasthima //
174.d:
कारुर् अहं ततो भिषग् उपलप्रक्षिणी नना
नानाधियो वसूयवो ऽनु गा इव तस्थिम ॥
174.m:
I am a poet, my father a physician, my mother a grinder of corn on stone.
With different thoughts, seeking wealth, we follow [our desires] like cattle. / Flow, drop, for Indra!

174.s:
evam uktvā ca ṛṣibhiḥ somaṃ prāpya ca vajriṇe
tebhyo dattvā tato yajñaḥ pūrṇo jātaḥ śatakratoḥ //
174.d:
एवम् उक्त्वा च ऋषिभिः सोमं प्राप्य च वज्रिणे
तेभ्यो दत्त्वा ततो यज्ञः पूर्णो जातः शतक्रतोः ॥
174.m: Having spoken thus, the sages, having obtained Soma, gave it to the wielder of the thunderbolt; / and then the sacrifice of Śatakratu became complete.

174.s:
tat somatīrtham ākhyātam āgneyaṃ puratas tu tat
agnir iṣṭvā mahāyajñair mām ārādhya manīṣitam //
174.d:
तत् सोमतीर्थम् आख्यातम् आग्नेयं पुरतस् तु तत्
अग्निर् इष्ट्वा महायज्ञैर् माम् आराध्य मनीषितम् ॥
174.m: That is celebrated as Somatīrtha, and before it is Āgneyatīrtha; / Agni, having sacrificed with great sacrifices and having worshipped me,

174.s:
saṃprāptavān matprasādād ahaṃ tatraiva nityaśaḥ
sthito lokopakārārthaṃ tatra viṣṇuḥ śivas tathā //
174.d:
संप्राप्तवान् मत्प्रसादाद् अहं तत्रैव नित्यशः
स्थितो लोकोपकारार्थं तत्र विष्णुः शिवस् तथा ॥
174.m: obtained what he desired by my grace. I am eternally / situated right there for the welfare of the worlds, and likewise Viṣṇu and Śiva are there.

174.s:
tasmād āgneyam ākhyātam ādityaṃ tadanantaram
yatrādityo vedamayo nityam eti upāsitum //
174.d:
तस्माद् आग्नेयम् आख्यातम् आदित्यं तदनन्तरम्
यत्रादित्यो वेदमयो नित्यम् एति उपासितुम् ॥
174.m: Therefore it is called Āgneya; immediately after it is Ādityatīrtha, / where the sun, consisting of the Veda, comes daily to worship.

174.s:
rūpāntareṇa madhyāhne draṣṭuṃ māṃ śaṃkaraṃ harim
namaskāryas tatra sadā madhyāhne sakalo janaḥ //
174.d:
रूपान्तरेण मध्याह्ने द्रष्टुं मां शंकरं हरिम्
नमस्कार्यस् तत्र सदा मध्याह्ने सकलो जनः ॥
174.m: In another form at midday, to see me, Śaṅkara, and Hari; / all people there should always be saluted at midday,

174.s:
rūpeṇa kena savitā samāyātīty aniścayāt
tasmād ādityam ākhyātaṃ bārhaspatyam anantaram //
174.d:
रूपेण केन सविता समायातीत्य् अनिश्चयात्
तस्माद् आदित्यम् आख्यातं बार्हस्पत्यम् अनन्तरम् ॥
174.m: because of the uncertainty: 'In what form does the sun arrive?' / Therefore it is called Āditya; immediately after it is Bārhaspatyatīrtha.

174.s:
bṛhaspatiḥ suraiḥ pūjāṃ tasmāt tīrthād avāpa ha
īje ca yajñān vividhān bārhaspatyaṃ tato viduḥ //
174.d:
बृहस्पतिः सुरैः पूजां तस्मात् तीर्थाद् अवाप ह
ईजे च यज्ञान् विविधान् बार्हस्पत्यं ततो विदुः ॥
174.m: Bṛhaspati obtained worship from the gods through that tīrtha, / and he performed various sacrifices; therefore they know it as Bārhaspatya.

174.s:
tattīrthasmaraṇād eva grahaśāntir bhaviṣyati
tasmād apy aparaṃ tīrtham indragope nagottame //
174.d:
तत्तीर्थस्मरणाद् एव ग्रहशान्तिर् भविष्यति
तस्माद् अप्य् अपरं तीर्थम् इन्द्रगोपे नगोत्तमे ॥
174.m: Merely from remembering that tīrtha, pacification of the planets will occur. / Beyond that is another tīrtha, on the excellent mountain Indragopa.

174.s:
pratiṣṭhitaṃ mahāliṅgaṃ kasmiṃścit kāraṇāntare
himālayena tat tīrtham adritīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
174.d:
