etaiś cānyaiś ca kīrṇāni samantāj jalacāribhiḥ //
178.d:
कारण्डवैर् बकैर् हंसैः कूर्मैर् मद्गुभिर् एव च
एतैश् चान्यैश् च कीर्णानि समन्ताज् जलचारिभिः ॥
178.m: Kāraṇḍava ducks, herons, swans, tortoises, and cormorants, / scattered all around with these and other aquatic creatures.

178.s:
krameṇaiva tathā sā tu vanaṃ babhrāma taiḥ saha
evaṃ dṛṣṭvā vanaṃ ramyaṃ taiḥ sārdhaṃ paramādbhutam //
178.d:
क्रमेणैव तथा सा तु वनं बभ्राम तैः सह
एवं दृष्ट्वा वनं रम्यं तैः सार्धं परमाद्भुतम् ॥
178.m: In this way she gradually roamed the forest with them. / Having thus seen the delightful and most wonderful forest with them,

178.s:
vismayotphullanayanā sā babhūva varāṅganā
provāca vāyuṃ kāmaṃ ca vasantaṃ ca dvijottamāḥ //
178.d:
विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयना सा बभूव वराङ्गना
प्रोवाच वायुं कामं च वसन्तं च द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
178.m: Her eyes wide with wonder, that excellent woman, / O best of the twice-born, spoke to the Wind, Kāma, and Spring:

178.s:
pramlocovāca
kurudhvaṃ mama sāhāyyaṃ yūyaṃ sarve pṛthak pṛthak //
178.d:
प्रम्लोचोवाच
कुरुध्वं मम साहाय्यं यूयं सर्वे पृथक् पृथक् ॥
178.m: Pramlocā said: / "Give me your assistance, each and every one of you!"

178.s:
brahmovāca
evam uktvā tadā sā tu tathety uktā surair dvijāḥ
pratyuvācādya yāsyāmi yatrāsau saṃsthito muniḥ //
178.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् उक्त्वा तदा सा तु तथेत्य् उक्ता सुरैर् द्विजाः
प्रत्युवाचाद्य यास्यामि यत्रासौ संस्थितो मुनिः ॥
178.m: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, O twice-born, and having been told 'So be it' by the gods, / she answered: 'Today I will go to where this sage resides.

178.s:
adya taṃ dehayantāraṃ prayuktendriyavājinam
smaraśastragaladraśmiṃ kariṣyāmi kusārathim //
178.d:
अद्य तं देहयन्तारं प्रयुक्तेन्द्रियवाजिनम्
स्मरशस्त्रगलद्रश्मिं करिष्यामि कुसारथिम् ॥
178.m: Today I will make him who drives the chariot of the body with harnessed horses of the senses / a poor charioteer whose reins slip before the weapon of Smara.

178.s:
brahmā janārdano vāpi yadi vā nīlalohitaḥ
tathāpy adya kariṣyāmi kāmabāṇakṣatāntaram //
178.d:
ब्रह्मा जनार्दनो वापि यदि वा नीललोहितः
तथाप्य् अद्य करिष्यामि कामबाणक्षतान्तरम् ॥
178.m: Whether he be Brahmā, or Janārdana, or even Nīlalohita, / I shall nonetheless wound his heart today with the arrows of love.'"

178.s:
ity uktvā prayayau sātha yatrāsau tiṣṭhate muniḥ
munes tapaḥprabhāveṇa praśāntaśvāpadāśramam //
178.d:
इत्य् उक्त्वा प्रययौ साथ यत्रासौ तिष्ठते मुनिः
मुनेस् तपःप्रभावेण प्रशान्तश्वापदाश्रमम् ॥
178.m: Having spoken thus, she went to where that sage stayed, / in the hermitage where wild beasts were pacified by the power of the sage's austerities.

178.s:
sā puṃskokilamādhurye nadītīre vyavasthitā
stokamātraṃ sthitā tasmād agāyata varāpsarāḥ //
178.d:
सा पुंस्कोकिलमाधुर्ये नदीतीरे व्यवस्थिता
स्तोकमात्रं स्थिता तस्माद् अगायत वराप्सराः ॥
178.m: Stationed on the riverbank sweet with the calls of male cuckoos, / pausing just a little while away from him, the excellent apsaras sang.

178.s:
tato vasantaḥ sahasā balaṃ samakarot tadā
kokilārāvamadhuram akālikamanoharam //
178.d:
ततो वसन्तः सहसा बलं समकरोत् तदा
कोकिलारावमधुरम् अकालिकमनोहरम् ॥
178.m: Then Spring at once gathered his strength, / sweet with the calling of cuckoos, enchanting out of season.

178.s:
vavau gandhavahaś caiva malayādriniketanaḥ
puṣpān uccāvacān medhyān pātayaṃś ca śanaiḥ śanaiḥ //
178.d:
ववौ गन्धवहश् चैव मलयाद्रिनिकेतनः
पुष्पान् उच्चावचान् मेध्यान् पातयंश् च शनैः शनैः ॥
178.m: The fragrance-bearing wind dwelling on Mount Malaya blew, / gently and steadily scattering pure, diverse flowers.

178.s:
puṣpabāṇadharaś caiva gatvā tasya samīpataḥ
muneś ca kṣobhayām āsa kāmas tasyāpi mānasam //
178.d:
पुष्पबाणधरश् चैव गत्वा तस्य समीपतः
मुनेश् च क्षोभयाम् आस कामस् तस्यापि मानसम् ॥
178.m: Approaching him, the bearer of flower-arrows, / Kāma, agitated the mind of that sage.

178.s:
tato gītadhvaniṃ śrutvā munir vismitamānasaḥ
jagāma yatra sā subhrūḥ kāmabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ //
178.d:
ततो गीतध्वनिं श्रुत्वा मुनिर् विस्मितमानसः
जगाम यत्र सा सुभ्रूः कामबाणप्रपीडितः ॥
178.m: Then, hearing the sound of the song, his mind filled with wonder, / afflicted by the arrows of love, the sage went to where that fair-browed woman was.

178.s:
dṛṣṭvā tām āha saṃdṛṣṭo vismayotphullalocanaḥ
bhraṣṭottarīyo vikalaḥ pulakāñcitavigrahaḥ //
178.d:
दृष्ट्वा ताम् आह संदृष्टो विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः
भ्रष्टोत्तरीयो विकलः पुलकाञ्चितविग्रहः ॥
178.m: Seeing her, gazing upon her with eyes wide with wonder, / his upper garment slipping down, agitated, his body bristling with horripilation, he said:

178.s:
ṛṣir uvāca
kāsi kasyāsi suśroṇi subhage cāruhāsini
mano harasi me subhru brūhi satyaṃ sumadhyame //
178.d:
ऋषिर् उवाच
कासि कस्यासि सुश्रोणि सुभगे चारुहासिनि
मनो हरसि मे सुभ्रु ब्रूहि सत्यं सुमध्यमे ॥
178.m: The ṛṣi said: / "Who are you? Whose are you, O fair-hipped, fortunate, lovely-smiling lady? / You captivate my mind, O fair-browed one! Tell me the truth, O slender-waisted woman!"

178.s:
pramlocovāca
tava karmakarā cāhaṃ puṣpārtham aham āgatā
ādeśaṃ dehi me kṣipraṃ kiṃ karomi tavājñayā //
178.d:
प्रम्लोचोवाच
तव कर्मकरा चाहं पुष्पार्थम् अहम् आगता
आदेशं देहि मे क्षिप्रं किं करोमि तवाज्ञया ॥
178.m: Pramlocā said: / "I am your servant, and I have come for flowers; / give me your command quickly; what shall I do at your bidding?"

178.s:
vyāsa uvāca
śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ tasyās tyaktvā dhairyaṃ vimohitaḥ
ādāya haste tāṃ bālāṃ praviveśa svam āśramam //
178.d:
व्यास उवाच
श्रुत्वैवं वचनं तस्यास् त्यक्त्वा धैर्यं विमोहितः
आदाय हस्ते तां बालां प्रविवेश स्वम् आश्रमम् ॥
178.m: Vyāsa said: / Hearing these words of hers, abandoning his steadfastness and deluded, / taking the maiden by the hand, he entered his own hermitage.

178.s:
tataḥ kāmaś ca vāyuś ca vasantaś ca dvijottamāḥ
jagmur yathāgataṃ sarve kṛtakṛtyās triviṣṭapam //
178.d:
ततः कामश् च वायुश् च वसन्तश् च द्विजोत्तमाः
जग्मुर् यथागतं सर्वे कृतकृत्यास् त्रिविष्टपम् ॥
178.m: Then, O best of the twice-born, Kāma, the Wind, and Spring, / having accomplished their purpose, all departed as they had come to heaven.

178.s:
śaśaṃsuś ca hariṃ gatvā tasyās tasya ca ceṣṭitam
śrutvā śakras tadā devāḥ prītāḥ sumanaso 'bhavan //
178.d:
शशंसुश् च हरिं गत्वा तस्यास् तस्य च चेष्टितम्
श्रुत्वा शक्रस् तदा देवाः प्रीताः सुमनसो ऽभवन् ॥
178.m: Approaching Hari, they reported her conduct and his; / hearing it, Śakra and the gods then became pleased and glad at heart.

178.s:
sa ca kaṇḍus tayā sārdhaṃ praviśann eva cāśramam
ātmanaḥ paramaṃ rūpaṃ cakāra madanākṛti //
178.d:
स च कण्डुस् तया सार्धं प्रविशन्न् एव चाश्रमम्
आत्मनः परमं रूपं चकार मदनाकृति ॥
178.m: And that Kaṇḍu, entering the hermitage along with her, / assumed a supreme form for himself with the appearance of the god of love,

178.s:
rūpayauvanasaṃpannam atīva sumanoharam
divyālaṃkārasaṃyuktaṃ ṣoḍaśavatsarākṛti //
178.d:
रूपयौवनसंपन्नम् अतीव सुमनोहरम्
दिव्यालंकारसंयुक्तं षोडशवत्सराकृति ॥
178.m: Endowed with beauty and youth, exceedingly captivating, / adorned with celestial ornaments, appearing as sixteen years of age.

178.s:
divyavastradharaṃ kāntaṃ divyasraggandhabhūṣitam
sarvopabhogasaṃpannaṃ sahasā tapaso balāt //
178.d:
दिव्यवस्त्रधरं कान्तं दिव्यस्रग्गन्धभूषितम्
सर्वोपभोगसंपन्नं सहसा तपसो बलात् ॥
178.m: wearing celestial garments, handsome, adorned with divine garlands and perfumes, / endowed with all enjoyments, suddenly, by the power of his austerity.

178.s:
dṛṣṭvā sā tasya tad vīryaṃ paraṃ vismayam āgatā
aho 'sya tapaso vīryam ity uktvā muditābhavat //
178.d:
दृष्ट्वा सा तस्य तद् वीर्यं परं विस्मयम् आगता
अहो ऽस्य तपसो वीर्यम् इत्य् उक्त्वा मुदिताभवत् ॥
178.m: Seeing that virility of his, she was filled with supreme wonder; / saying, “Ah, the virility of his austerity!” she became delighted.

178.s:
snānaṃ saṃdhyāṃ japaṃ homaṃ svādhyāyaṃ devatārcanam
vratopavāsaniyamaṃ dhyānaṃ ca munisattamāḥ //
178.d:
स्नानं संध्यां जपं होमं स्वाध्यायं देवतार्चनम्
व्रतोपवासनियमं ध्यानं च मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
178.m: Bathing, twilight worship, recitation, fire offering, Vedic study, worship of the gods, / vows, fasts, observances, and meditation, O best of sages,

178.s:
tyaktvā sa reme muditas tayā sārdham aharniśam
manmathāviṣṭahṛdayo na bubodha tapaḥkṣayam //
178.d:
त्यक्त्वा स रेमे मुदितस् तया सार्धम् अहर्निशम्
मन्मथाविष्टहृदयो न बुबोध तपःक्षयम् ॥
178.m: abandoning [all these], he sported with her day and night, delighted. / His heart possessed by love, he did not perceive the loss of his austerity.

178.s:
saṃdhyārātridivāpakṣamāsartvayanahāyanam
na bubodha gataṃ kālaṃ viṣayāsaktamānasaḥ //
178.d:
संध्यारात्रिदिवापक्षमासर्त्वयनहायनम्
न बुबोध गतं कालं विषयासक्तमानसः ॥
178.m: Twilight, night, day, fortnight, month, season, solstice, and year— / he did not notice time passing, his mind attached to objects of the senses.

178.s:
sā ca taṃ kāmajair bhāvair vidagdhā rahasi dvijāḥ
varayām āsa suśroṇiḥ pralāpakuśalā tadā //
178.d:
सा च तं कामजैर् भावैर् विदग्धा रहसि द्विजाः
वरयाम् आस सुश्रोणिः प्रलापकुशला तदा ॥
178.m: And she, clever in amorous emotions, seductive in private, O twice-born, / of fair hips, skilled in sweet talk, then wooed him.

178.s:
evaṃ kaṇḍus tayā sārdhaṃ varṣāṇām adhikaṃ śatam
atiṣṭhan mandaradroṇyāṃ grāmyadharmarato muniḥ //
178.d:
एवं कण्डुस् तया सार्धं वर्षाणाम् अधिकं शतम्
अतिष्ठन् मन्दरद्रोण्यां ग्राम्यधर्मरतो मुनिः ॥
178.m: Thus Kaṇḍu, devoted to the carnal way, / stayed with her for more than a hundred years in the valley of Mount Mandara, the sage.

178.s:
sā taṃ prāha mahābhāgaṃ gantum icchāmy ahaṃ divam
prasādasumukho brahmann anujñātuṃ tvam arhasi //
178.d:
सा तं प्राह महाभागं गन्तुम् इच्छाम्य् अहं दिवम्
प्रसादसुमुखो ब्रह्मन्न् अनुज्ञातुं त्वम् अर्हसि ॥
178.m: She said to that illustrious one: “I wish to go to heaven; / gracious-faced, O Brahmin, you ought to grant me leave.”

178.s:
tayaivam uktaḥ sa munis tasyām āsaktamānasaḥ
dināni katicid bhadre sthīyatām ity abhāṣata //
178.d:
तयैवम् उक्तः स मुनिस् तस्याम् आसक्तमानसः
दिनानि कतिचिद् भद्रे स्थीयताम् इत्य् अभाषत ॥
178.m: Addressed thus by her, the sage, his mind attached to her, / spoke: “Stay for a few days, fair lady.”

178.s:
evam uktā tatas tena sāgraṃ varṣaśataṃ punaḥ
bubhuje viṣayāṃs tanvī tena sārdhaṃ mahātmanā //
178.d:
एवम् उक्ता ततस् तेन साग्रं वर्षशतं पुनः
बुभुजे विषयांस् तन्वी तेन सार्धं महात्मना ॥
178.m: Spoken to thus by him, the slender woman then / enjoyed sense pleasures again with that great-souled one for fully a hundred years.

178.s:
anujñāṃ dehi bhagavan vrajāmi tridaśālayam
uktas tayeti sa punaḥ sthīyatām ity abhāṣata //
178.d:
अनुज्ञां देहि भगवन् व्रजामि त्रिदशालयम्
उक्तस् तयेति स पुनः स्थीयताम् इत्य् अभाषत ॥
178.m: “Grant me permission, lord; let me go to the abode of the gods.” / Addressed thus by her, he spoke again: “Stay!”

178.s:
punar gate varṣaśate sādhike sā śubhānanā
yāmy ahaṃ tridivaṃ brahman praṇayasmitaśobhanam //
178.d:
पुनर् गते वर्षशते साधिके सा शुभानना
याम्य् अहं त्रिदिवं ब्रह्मन् प्रणयस्मितशोभनम् ॥
178.m: When another hundred years and more had passed, that fair-faced lady [said]: / “I am going to heaven, O Brahmin,” charming with an affectionate smile.

178.s:
uktas tayaivaṃ sa muniḥ punar āhāyatekṣaṇām
ihāsyatāṃ mayā subhru ciraṃ kālaṃ gamiṣyasi //
178.d:
उक्तस् तयैवं स मुनिः पुनर् आहायतेक्षणाम्
इहास्यतां मया सुभ्रु चिरं कालं गमिष्यसि ॥
178.m: Addressed thus by her, the sage spoke again to the large-eyed one: / “Stay here with me, fair-browed lady; you shall go after a long time.”

178.s:
tacchāpabhītā suśroṇī saha tenarṣiṇā punaḥ
śatadvayaṃ kiṃcid ūnaṃ varṣāṇāṃ samatiṣṭhata //
178.d:
तच्छापभीता सुश्रोणी सह तेनर्षिणा पुनः
शतद्वयं किंचिद् ऊनं वर्षाणां समतिष्ठत ॥
178.m: Afraid of his curse, the woman of fair hips / stayed with that ṛṣi again for nearly two hundred years.

178.s:
gamanāya mahābhāgo devarājaniveśanam
proktaḥ proktas tayā tanvyā sthīyatām ity abhāṣata //
178.d:
गमनाय महाभागो देवराजनिवेशनम्
प्रोक्तः प्रोक्तस् तया तन्व्या स्थीयताम् इत्य् अभाषत ॥
178.m: Whenever the illustrious one was addressed by that slender woman / to go to the abode of the king of gods, he said: “Stay!”

178.s:
tasya śāpabhayād bhīrur dākṣiṇyena ca dakṣiṇā
proktā praṇayabhaṅgārtivedinī na jahau munim //
178.d:
तस्य शापभयाद् भीरुर् दाक्षिण्येन च दक्षिणा
प्रोक्ता प्रणयभङ्गार्तिवेदिनी न जहौ मुनिम् ॥
178.m: Afraid of his curse, timid, and courteous out of politeness, / when addressed, understanding the pain of broken love, she did not leave the sage.

178.s:
tayā ca ramatas tasya paramarṣer aharniśam
navaṃ navam abhūt prema manmathāsaktacetasaḥ //
178.d:
तया च रमतस् तस्य परमर्षेर् अहर्निशम्
नवं नवम् अभूत् प्रेम मन्मथासक्तचेतसः ॥
178.m: And as that supreme ṛṣi sported with her day and night, / his love was ever new, his mind attached to desire.

178.s:
ekadā tu tvarāyukto niścakrāmoṭajān muniḥ
niṣkrāmantaṃ ca kutreti gamyate prāha sā śubhā //
178.d:
एकदा तु त्वरायुक्तो निश्चक्रामोटजान् मुनिः
निष्क्रामन्तं च कुत्रेति गम्यते प्राह सा शुभा ॥
178.m: Once, however, the sage came out of the hut in haste; / and seeing him come out, that fair woman said: “Where are you going?”

178.s:
ity uktaḥ sa tayā prāha parivṛttam ahaḥ śubhe
saṃdhyopāstiṃ kariṣyāmi kriyālopo 'nyathā bhavet //
178.d:
इत्य् उक्तः स तया प्राह परिवृत्तम् अहः शुभे
संध्योपास्तिं करिष्यामि क्रियालोपो ऽन्यथा भवेत् ॥
178.m: Addressed thus by her, he said: “Fair lady, the day has turned; / I must perform the twilight worship, otherwise my rite would be neglected.”

178.s:
tataḥ prahasya muditā sā taṃ prāha mahāmunim
kim adya sarvadharmajña parivṛttam ahas tava
gatam etan na kurute vismayaṃ kasya kathyate //
178.d:
ततः प्रहस्य मुदिता सा तं प्राह महामुनिम्
किम् अद्य सर्वधर्मज्ञ परिवृत्तम् अहस् तव
गतम् एतन् न कुरुते विस्मयं कस्य कथ्यते ॥
178.m: Then, laughing, delighted, she said to that great sage: / “Has only today turned for you, O knower of all dharma? / This [much time] has passed; whose wonder does it not excite? Tell me!”

178.s:
munir uvāca
prātas tvam āgatā bhadre nadītīram idaṃ śubham
mayā dṛṣṭāsi suśroṇi praviṣṭā ca mamāśramam //
178.d:
मुनिर् उवाच
प्रातस् त्वम् आगता भद्रे नदीतीरम् इदं शुभम्
मया दृष्टासि सुश्रोणि प्रविष्टा च ममाश्रमम् ॥
178.m: The sage said: / “You came this morning, fair lady, to this auspicious riverbank; / you were seen by me, O fair-hipped woman, and you entered my hermitage.

178.s:
iyaṃ ca vartate saṃdhyā pariṇāmam aho gatam
avahāsaḥ kimartho 'yaṃ sadbhāvaḥ kathyatāṃ mama //
178.d:
इयं च वर्तते संध्या परिणामम् अहो गतम्
अवहासः किमर्थो ऽयं सद्भावः कथ्यतां मम ॥
178.m: And now it is twilight; the day has come to its close. / Why this laughter? Tell me the truth!”

178.s:
pramlocovāca
pratyūṣasy āgatā brahman satyam etan na me mṛṣā
kiṃtv adya tasya kālasya gatāny abdaśatāni te //
178.d:
प्रम्लोचोवाच
प्रत्यूषस्य् आगता ब्रह्मन् सत्यम् एतन् न मे मृषा
किंत्व् अद्य तस्य कालस्य गतान्य् अब्दशतानि ते ॥
178.m: Pramlocā said: / “You came at dawn, O Brahmin; this is true, not false of me; / but hundreds of years have passed for you since that time!”

178.s:
tataḥ sasādhvaso vipras tāṃ papracchāyatekṣaṇām
kathyatāṃ bhīru kaḥ kālas tvayā me ramataḥ sadā //
178.d:
ततः ससाध्वसो विप्रस् तां पप्रच्छायतेक्षणाम्
कथ्यतां भीरु कः कालस् त्वया मे रमतः सदा ॥
178.m: Then, filled with dismay, the Brahmin asked that large-eyed one: / “Tell me, timid lady, how much time has passed while I sported with you constantly?”

178.s:
pramlocovāca
saptottarāṇy atītāni navavarṣaśatāni ca
māsāś ca ṣaṭ tathaivānyat samatītaṃ dinatrayam //
178.d:
प्रम्लोचोवाच
सप्तोत्तराण्य् अतीतानि नववर्षशतानि च
मासाश् च षट् तथैवान्यत् समतीतं दिनत्रयम् ॥
178.m: Pramlocā said: / “Nine hundred and seven years have passed, / and six months, and also another three days have elapsed.”

178.s:
ṛṣir uvāca
satyaṃ bhīru vadasy etat parihāso 'thavā śubhe
dinam ekam ahaṃ manye tvayā sārdham ihoṣitam //
178.d:
ऋषिर् उवाच
सत्यं भीरु वदस्य् एतत् परिहासो ऽथवा शुभे
दिनम् एकम् अहं मन्ये त्वया सार्धम् इहोषितम् ॥
178.m: The ṛṣi said: / “Do you speak the truth, timid one, or is this a jest, fair lady? / I think I have lived here with you for a single day!”

178.s:
pramlocovāca
vadiṣyāmy anṛtaṃ brahman katham atra tavāntike
viśeṣād adya bhavatā pṛṣṭā mārgānugāminā //
178.d:
प्रम्लोचोवाच
वदिष्याम्य् अनृतं ब्रह्मन् कथम् अत्र तवान्तिके
विशेषाद् अद्य भवता पृष्टा मार्गानुगामिना ॥
178.m: Pramlocā said: / “How could I speak an untruth in your presence here, O Brahmin, / especially today when questioned by you who walk in the path [of truth]?”

178.s:
vyāsa uvāca
niśamya tad vacas tasyāḥ sa munir dvijasattamāḥ
dhig dhiṅ mām ity anācāraṃ vinindyātmānam ātmanā //
178.d:
व्यास उवाच
निशम्य तद् वचस् तस्याः स मुनिर् द्विजसत्तमाः
धिग् धिङ् माम् इत्य् अनाचारं विनिन्द्यात्मानम् आत्मना ॥
178.m: Vyāsa said: / Hearing those words of hers, O best of twice-born, the sage / reproached himself, saying, “Fie, fie on me of bad conduct!”

178.s:
munir uvāca
tapāṃsi mama naṣṭāni hataṃ brahmavidāṃ dhanam
hṛto vivekaḥ kenāpi yoṣin mohāya nirmitā //
178.d:
मुनिर् उवाच
तपांसि मम नष्टानि हतं ब्रह्मविदां धनम्
हृतो विवेकः केनापि योषिन् मोहाय निर्मिता ॥
178.m: The sage said: / “My austerities are ruined; the wealth of those who know brahman is destroyed; / my discernment has been stolen by someone! Woman was created for delusion!

178.s:
ūrmiṣaṭkātigaṃ brahma jñeyam ātmajayena me
gatir eṣā kṛtā yena dhik taṃ kāmamahāgraham //
178.d:
ऊर्मिषट्कातिगं ब्रह्म ज्ञेयम् आत्मजयेन मे
गतिर् एषा कृता येन धिक् तं काममहाग्रहम् ॥
178.m: Brahman, beyond the six waves [of existence], was to be known by me through mastery of self; / fie on that great eclipse of desire by which this state was brought about!

178.s:
vratāni sarvavedāś ca kāraṇāny akhilāni ca
narakagrāmamārgeṇa kāmenādya hatāni me //
178.d:
व्रतानि सर्ववेदाश् च कारणान्य् अखिलानि च
नरकग्राममार्गेण कामेनाद्य हतानि मे ॥
178.m: Vows, all the Vedas, and all reasons [for virtue] / have been destroyed today by desire, the path to the hamlet of hell!”

178.s:
ṛṣir uvāca
na tvāṃ karomy ahaṃ bhasma krodhatīvreṇa vahninā
satāṃ sāptapadaṃ maitryam uṣito 'haṃ tvayā saha //
178.d:
ऋषिर् उवाच
न त्वां करोम्य् अहं भस्म क्रोधतीव्रेण वह्निना
सतां साप्तपदं मैत्र्यम् उषितो ऽहं त्वया सह ॥
178.m: I will not reduce you to ashes with the fierce fire of my anger; / friendship among the virtuous is formed in seven steps, and I have lived together with you.

178.s:
athavā tava doṣaḥ kaḥ kiṃ vā kuryām ahaṃ tava
mamaiva doṣo nitarāṃ yenāham ajitendriyaḥ //
178.d:
अथवा तव दोषः कः किं वा कुर्याम् अहं तव
ममैव दोषो नितरां येनाहम् अजितेन्द्रियः ॥
178.m: Or rather, what fault is yours? What could I do to you? / The fault is entirely mine, because I failed to conquer my senses.

178.s:
yathā śakrapriyārthinyā kṛto mattapaso vyayaḥ
tvayā dṛṣṭimahāmohamanunāhaṃ jugupsitaḥ //
178.d:
यथा शक्रप्रियार्थिन्या कृतो मत्तपसो व्ययः
त्वया दृष्टिमहामोहमनुनाहं जुगुप्सितः ॥
178.m: Just as you, seeking to please Śakra, caused the ruin of my austerity, / I have been degraded by you through the great delusion that is the charm of sight.”

178.s:
vyāsa uvāca
yāvad itthaṃ sa viprarṣis tāṃ bravīti sumadhyamām
tāvat skhalatsvedajalā sā babhūvātivepathuḥ //
178.d:
व्यास उवाच
यावद् इत्थं स विप्रर्षिस् तां ब्रवीति सुमध्यमाम्
तावत् स्खलत्स्वेदजला सा बभूवातिवेपथुः ॥
178.m: Vyāsa said: / While the Brahmin-sage was speaking thus to that slender-waisted woman, / drops of sweat trickled from her, and she began to tremble exceedingly.

178.s:
pravepamānāṃ sa ca tāṃ svinnagātralatāṃ satīm
gaccha gaccheti sakrodham uvāca munisattamaḥ //
178.d:
प्रवेपमानां स च तां स्विन्नगात्रलतां सतीम्
गच्छ गच्छेति सक्रोधम् उवाच मुनिसत्तमः ॥
178.m: And to her, trembling, her creeper-like body sweating, the chaste woman, / the best of sages angrily said: “Go! Go!”

178.s:
sā tu nirbhartsitā tena viniṣkramya tadāśramāt
ākāśagāminī svedaṃ mamārja tarupallavaiḥ //
178.d:
सा तु निर्भर्त्सिता तेन विनिष्क्रम्य तदाश्रमात्
आकाशगामिनी स्वेदं ममार्ज तरुपल्लवैः ॥
178.m: Rebuked by him, coming out from that hermitage, / moving through the sky, she wiped her sweat on the leaves of the trees.

178.s:
vṛkṣād vṛkṣaṃ yayau bālā udagrāruṇapallavaiḥ
nirmamārja ca gātrāṇi galatsvedajalāni vai //
178.d:
वृक्षाद् वृक्षं ययौ बाला उदग्रारुणपल्लवैः
निर्ममार्ज च गात्राणि गलत्स्वेदजलानि वै ॥
178.m: The young woman went from tree to tree and with their high reddish sprouts / wiped her limbs, from which streams of sweat were flowing.

178.s:
ṛṣiṇā yas tadā garbhas tasyā dehe samāhitaḥ
nirjagāma saromāñcasvedarūpī tadaṅgataḥ //
178.d:
ऋषिणा यस् तदा गर्भस् तस्या देहे समाहितः
निर्जगाम सरोमाञ्चस्वेदरूपी तदङ्गतः ॥
178.m: The embryo that had then been placed in her body by the ṛṣi / came forth from her limbs in the form of sweat with bristling hair.

178.s:
taṃ vṛkṣā jagṛhur garbham ekaṃ cakre ca mārutaḥ
somenāpyāyito gobhiḥ sa tadā vavṛddhe śanaiḥ //
178.d:
तं वृक्षा जगृहुर् गर्भम् एकं चक्रे च मारुतः
सोमेनाप्यायितो गोभिः स तदा ववृद्धे शनैः ॥
178.m: The trees received that embryo, and the wind gathered it into one; / nourished by Soma with his rays, it then grew slowly.

178.s:
māriṣā nāma kanyābhūd vṛkṣāṇāṃ cārulocanā
prācetasānāṃ sā bhāryā dakṣasya jananī dvijāḥ //
178.d:
मारिषा नाम कन्याभूद् वृक्षाणां चारुलोचना
प्राचेतसानां सा भार्या दक्षस्य जननी द्विजाः ॥
178.m: She became a lovely-eyed maiden of the trees named Māriṣā; / she was the wife of the Pracetases and mother of Dakṣa, O twice-born.

178.s:
sa cāpi bhagavān kaṇḍuḥ kṣīṇe tapasi sattamaḥ
puruṣottamākhyaṃ bho viprā viṣṇor āyatanaṃ yayau //
178.d:
स चापि भगवान् कण्डुः क्षीणे तपसि सत्तमः
पुरुषोत्तमाख्यं भो विप्रा विष्णोर् आयतनं ययौ ॥
178.m: And that blessed Kaṇḍu, the best of men, his austerity depleted, / went, O Brahmins, to the abode of Viṣṇu named Puruṣottama.

178.s:
dadarśa paramaṃ kṣetraṃ muktidaṃ bhuvi durlabham
dakṣiṇasyodadhes tīre sarvakāmaphalapradam //
178.d:
ददर्श परमं क्षेत्रं मुक्तिदं भुवि दुर्लभम्
दक्षिणस्योदधेस् तीरे सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
178.m: He saw that supreme sacred field, granting liberation, rare on earth, / on the shore of the southern ocean, granting the fruit of all desires,

178.s:
suramyaṃ vālukākīrṇaṃ ketakīvanaśobhitam
nānādrumalatākīrṇaṃ nānāpakṣirutaṃ śivam //
178.d:
सुरम्यं वालुकाकीर्णं केतकीवनशोभितम्
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णं नानापक्षिरुतं शिवम् ॥
178.m: delightful, strewn with sand, adorned with ketakī groves, / covered with various trees and creepers, resounding with the cries of various birds, auspicious,

178.s:
sarvatra sukhasaṃcāraṃ sarvartukusumānvitam
sarvasaukhyapradaṃ nṝṇāṃ dhanyaṃ sarvaguṇākaram //
178.d:
सर्वत्र सुखसंचारं सर्वर्तुकुसुमान्वितम्
सर्वसौख्यप्रदं नॄणां धन्यं सर्वगुणाकरम् ॥
178.m: easy to traverse everywhere, endowed with flowers of all seasons, / conferring all happiness on mortals, blessed, a mine of all virtues,

178.s:
bhṛgvādyaiḥ sevitaṃ pūrvaṃ munisiddhavarais tathā
gandharvaiḥ kiṃnarair yakṣais tathānyair mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ //
178.d:
भृग्वाद्यैः सेवितं पूर्वं मुनिसिद्धवरैस् तथा
गन्धर्वैः किंनरैर् यक्षैस् तथान्यैर् मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः ॥
178.m: frequented in earlier times by Bhṛgu and others, and by the best of sages and perfected beings, / by gandharvas, kiṃnaras, yakṣas, and other seekers of liberation.

178.s:
dadarśa ca hariṃ tatra devaiḥ sarvair alaṃkṛtam
brāhmaṇādyais tathā varṇair āśramasthair niṣevitam //
178.d:
ददर्श च हरिं तत्र देवैः सर्वैर् अलंकृतम्
ब्राह्मणाद्यैस् तथा वर्णैर् आश्रमस्थैर् निषेवितम् ॥
178.m: And there he saw Hari, adorned by all the gods, / and attended by the castes, beginning with the brāhmaṇas, dwelling in their hermitages.

178.s:
dṛṣṭvaiva sa tadā kṣetraṃ devaṃ ca puruṣottamam
kṛtakṛtyam ivātmānaṃ mene sa munisattamaḥ //
178.d:
दृष्ट्वैव स तदा क्षेत्रं देवं च पुरुषोत्तमम्
कृतकृत्यम् इवात्मानं मेने स मुनिसत्तमः ॥
178.m: As soon as he saw that sacred field and the god Puruṣottama, / that best of sages considered himself to have achieved his purpose.

178.s:
tatraikāgramanā bhūtvā cakārārādhanaṃ hareḥ
brahmapāramayaṃ kurvañ japam ekāgramānasaḥ
ūrdhvabāhur mahāyogī sthitvāsau munisattamaḥ //
178.d:
तत्रैकाग्रमना भूत्वा चकाराराधनं हरेः
ब्रह्मपारमयं कुर्वञ् जपम् एकाग्रमानसः
ऊर्ध्वबाहुर् महायोगी स्थित्वासौ मुनिसत्तमः ॥
178.m: Becoming single-minded there, he worshiped Hari; / standing with arms raised, a great yogin, / that best of sages, his mind concentrated, performed the Brahmapāra recitation:

178.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
brahmapāraṃ mune śrotum icchāmaḥ paramaṃ śubham
japatā kaṇḍunā devo yenārādhyata keśavaḥ //
178.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
ब्रह्मपारं मुने श्रोतुम् इच्छामः परमं शुभम्
जपता कण्डुना देवो येनाराध्यत केशवः ॥
178.m: The sages said: / O sage, we wish to hear the supreme and auspicious Brahmapāra [hymn], / by reciting which the god Keśava was worshiped by Kaṇḍu.

178.s:
vyāsa uvāca
pāraṃ paraṃ viṣṇur apārapāraḥ
paraḥ parebhyaḥ paramātmarūpaḥ
sa brahmapāraḥ parapārabhūtaḥ
paraḥ parāṇām api pārapāraḥ
178.d:
व्यास उवाच
पारं परं विष्णुर् अपारपारः
परः परेभ्यः परमात्मरूपः
स ब्रह्मपारः परपारभूतः
परः पराणाम् अपि पारपारः
178.m: Vyāsa said: / Viṣṇu is the shore beyond, the supreme, the shore of the shoreless, / higher than the high, whose form is the supreme self; / he is the Brahmapāra, existing as the shore beyond the beyond, / higher than the high, the ultimate shore of even the shores beyond.

178.s:
sa kāraṇaṃ kāraṇasaṃśrito 'pi
tasyāpi hetuḥ parahetuhetuḥ
kāryo 'pi caiṣa saha karmakartṛ
rūpair anekair avatīha sarvam
178.d:
स कारणं कारणसंश्रितो ऽपि
तस्यापि हेतुः परहेतुहेतुः
कार्यो ऽपि चैष सह कर्मकर्तृ
रूपैर् अनेकैर् अवतीह सर्वम्
178.m: He is the cause, though resting in the cause; / he is the reason even of that, the cause of the supreme cause; / though an effect, together with the multiple forms / of action and agent, he protects everything here.

178.s:
brahma prabhur brahma sa sarvabhūto
brahma prajānāṃ patir acyuto 'sau
brahmāvyayaṃ nityam ajaṃ sa viṣṇur
apakṣayādyair akhilair asaṅgaḥ
178.d:
ब्रह्म प्रभुर् ब्रह्म स सर्वभूतो
ब्रह्म प्रजानां पतिर् अच्युतो ऽसौ
ब्रह्माव्ययं नित्यम् अजं स विष्णुर्
अपक्षयाद्यैर् अखिलैर् असङ्गः
178.m: The Lord is Brahman; he is Brahman, having become all beings; / he, Acyuta, is Brahman, the lord of creatures; / Viṣṇu is imperishable, eternal, unborn Brahman, / untouched by decay and all other [modifications].

178.s:
brahmākṣaram ajaṃ nityaṃ yathāsau puruṣottamaḥ
tathā rāgādayo doṣāḥ prayāntu praśamaṃ mama //
178.d:
ब्रह्माक्षरम् अजं नित्यं यथासौ पुरुषोत्तमः
तथा रागादयो दोषाः प्रयान्तु प्रशमं मम ॥
178.m: Just as this Puruṣottama is imperishable, unborn, and eternal Brahman, / so may my defects, such as passion, come to pacification.

178.s:
vyāsa uvāca
śrutvā tasya muner jāpyaṃ brahmapāraṃ dvijottamāḥ
bhaktiṃ ca paramāṃ jñātvā sudṛḍhāṃ puruṣottamaḥ //
178.d:
व्यास उवाच
श्रुत्वा तस्य मुनेर् जाप्यं ब्रह्मपारं द्विजोत्तमाः
भक्तिं च परमां ज्ञात्वा सुदृढां पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
178.m: Vyāsa said: / Having heard the Brahmapāra recitation of that sage, O best of the twice-born, / and knowing his supreme and steadfast devotion, Puruṣottama—

178.s:
prītyā sa parayā devas tadāsau bhaktavatsalaḥ
gatvā tasya samīpaṃ tu provāca madhusūdanaḥ //
178.d:
प्रीत्या स परया देवस् तदासौ भक्तवत्सलः
गत्वा तस्य समीपं तु प्रोवाच मधुसूदनः ॥
178.m: that god, fond of his devotees, filled with supreme love— / Madhusūdana went near him and spoke,

178.s:
meghagambhīrayā vācā diśaḥ saṃnādayann iva
āruhya garuḍaṃ viprā vinatākulanandanam //
178.d:
मेघगम्भीरया वाचा दिशः संनादयन्न् इव
आरुह्य गरुडं विप्रा विनताकुलनन्दनम् ॥
178.m: making the quarters resound, as it were, with a voice deep as thunder, / having mounted Garuḍa, O brāhmaṇas, the delighter of Vinatā's family.

178.s:
śrībhagavān uvāca
mune brūhi paraṃ kāryaṃ yat te manasi vartate
varado 'ham anuprāpto varaṃ varaya suvrata //
178.d:
श्रीभगवान् उवाच
मुने ब्रूहि परं कार्यं यत् ते मनसि वर्तते
वरदो ऽहम् अनुप्राप्तो वरं वरय सुव्रत ॥
178.m: The Holy One said: / O sage, speak the ultimate desire that is in your heart; / I have arrived as the giver of boons; choose a boon, O you of noble vows!

178.s:
śrutvaivaṃ vacanaṃ tasya devadevasya cakriṇaḥ
cakṣur unmīlya sahasā dadarśa purato harim //
178.d:
श्रुत्वैवं वचनं तस्य देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः
चक्षुर् उन्मील्य सहसा ददर्श पुरतो हरिम् ॥
178.m: Hearing these words of the god of gods who wields the discus, / he opened his eyes and suddenly saw Hari before him:

178.s:
atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ padmapattrāyatekṣaṇam
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiṃ mukuṭāṅgadadhāriṇam //
178.d:
अतसीपुष्पसंकाशं पद्मपत्त्रायतेक्षणम्
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिं मुकुटाङ्गदधारिणम् ॥
178.m: resembling an atasī flower, with long eyes like lotus petals, / holding the conch, discus, and mace in his hands, wearing a crown and armlets,

178.s:
caturbāhum udārāṅgaṃ pītavastradharaṃ śubham
śrīvatsalakṣmasaṃyuktaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣitam //
178.d:
चतुर्बाहुम् उदाराङ्गं पीतवस्त्रधरं शुभम्
श्रीवत्सलक्ष्मसंयुक्तं वनमालाविभूषितम् ॥
178.m: four-armed, noble-limbed, wearing auspicious yellow garments, / marked with the Śrīvatsa, adorned with a garland of forest flowers,

178.s:
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ sarvaratnavibhūṣitam
divyacandanaliptāṅgaṃ divyamālyavibhūṣitam //
178.d:
सर्वलक्षणसंयुक्तं सर्वरत्नविभूषितम्
दिव्यचन्दनलिप्ताङ्गं दिव्यमाल्यविभूषितम् ॥
178.m: endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with all jewels, / his limbs smeared with divine sandalwood paste, adorned with divine garlands.

178.s:
tataḥ sa vismayāviṣṭo romāñcitatanūruhaḥ
daṇḍavat praṇipatyorvyāṃ praṇāmam akarot tadā //
178.d:
ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो रोमाञ्चिततनूरुहः
दण्डवत् प्रणिपत्योर्व्यां प्रणामम् अकरोत् तदा ॥
178.m: Then, overcome with wonder, the hair on his body bristling with joy, / he prostrated like a staff on the earth and made obeisance.

178.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalaṃ tapaḥ
ity uktvā muniśārdūlās taṃ stotum upacakrame //
178.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलं तपः
इत्य् उक्त्वा मुनिशार्दूलास् तं स्तोतुम् उपचक्रमे ॥
178.m: “Today my birth has borne fruit; today my asceticism has borne fruit!” / Having said this, O tigers among sages, he began to praise him:

178.s:
kaṇḍur uvāca
nārāyaṇa hare kṛṣṇa śrīvatsāṅka jagatpate
jagadbīja jagaddhāma jagatsākṣin namo 'stu te //
178.d:
कण्डुर् उवाच
नारायण हरे कृष्ण श्रीवत्साङ्क जगत्पते
जगद्बीज जगद्धाम जगत्साक्षिन् नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: Kaṇḍu said: / O Nārāyaṇa, O Hari, O Kṛṣṇa, O one marked by the Śrīvatsa, O lord of the universe! / O seed of the universe, O abode of the universe, O witness of the universe, homage to you!

178.s:
avyakta jiṣṇo prabhava pradhānapuruṣottama
puṇḍarīkākṣa govinda lokanātha namo 'stu te //
178.d:
अव्यक्त जिष्णो प्रभव प्रधानपुरुषोत्तम
पुण्डरीकाक्ष गोविन्द लोकनाथ नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: O unmanifest one, O victorious one, O origin, O Puruṣottama of the pradhāna! / O lotus-eyed one, O Govinda, O protector of the world, homage to you!

178.s:
hiraṇyagarbha śrīnātha padmanātha sanātana
bhūgarbha dhruva īśāna hṛṣīkeśa namo 'stu te //
178.d:
हिरण्यगर्भ श्रीनाथ पद्मनाथ सनातन
भूगर्भ ध्रुव ईशान हृषीकेश नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: O Hiraṇyagarbha, O lord of Śrī, O lord of the lotus, O eternal one! / O womb of the earth, O immovable one, O ruler, O Hṛṣīkeśa, homage to you!

178.s:
anādyantāmṛtājeya jaya tvaṃ jayatāṃ vara
ajitākhaṇḍa śrīkṛṣṇa śrīnivāsa namo 'stu te //
178.d:
अनाद्यन्तामृताजेय जय त्वं जयतां वर
अजिताखण्ड श्रीकृष्ण श्रीनिवास नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: O one without beginning or end, O immortal one, O unconquerable one, be victorious, O best among the victorious! / O unconquered one, O undivided one, O Śrīkṛṣṇa, O abode of Śrī, homage to you!

178.s:
parjanyadharmakartā ca duṣpāra duradhiṣṭhita
duḥkhārtināśana hare jalaśāyin namo 'stu te //
178.d:
पर्जन्यधर्मकर्ता च दुष्पार दुरधिष्ठित
दुःखार्तिनाशन हरे जलशायिन् नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: O rain cloud, O maker of dharma, O hard to cross, O difficult to attain, / O destroyer of grief and pain, O Hari, O one reclining on the waters, homage to you!

178.s:
bhūtapāvyakta bhūteśa bhūtatattvair anākula
bhūtādhivāsa bhūtātman bhūtagarbha namo 'stu te //
178.d:
भूतपाव्यक्त भूतेश भूततत्त्वैर् अनाकुल
भूताधिवास भूतात्मन् भूतगर्भ नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: O protector of beings, O unmanifest one, O lord of beings, unperturbed by the principles of beings, / O dwelling of beings, O self of beings, O womb of beings, homage to you!

178.s:
yajñayajvan yajñadhara yajñadhātābhayaprada
yajñagarbha hiraṇyāṅga pṛśnigarbha namo 'stu te //
178.d:
यज्ञयज्वन् यज्ञधर यज्ञधाताभयप्रद
यज्ञगर्भ हिरण्याङ्ग पृश्निगर्भ नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: O sacrifice, O sacrificer, O upholder of the sacrifice, O dispenser of the sacrifice, O granter of fearlessness, / O womb of the sacrifice, O golden-limbed one, O Pṛśnigarbha, homage to you!

178.s:
kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetrabhṛt kṣetrī kṣetrahā kṣetrakṛd vaśī
kṣetrātman kṣetrarahita kṣetrasraṣṭre namo 'stu te //
178.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञः क्षेत्रभृत् क्षेत्री क्षेत्रहा क्षेत्रकृद् वशी
क्षेत्रात्मन् क्षेत्ररहित क्षेत्रस्रष्ट्रे नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: You are the knower of the field, the supporter of the field, the possessor of the field, the destroyer of the field, the maker of the field, the controller; / O self of the field, O one free from the field, homage to the creator of the field!

178.s:
guṇālaya guṇāvāsa guṇāśraya guṇāvaha
guṇabhoktṛ guṇārāma guṇatyāgin namo 'stu te //
178.d:
गुणालय गुणावास गुणाश्रय गुणावह
गुणभोक्तृ गुणाराम गुणत्यागिन् नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: O abode of qualities, O dwelling of qualities, O refuge of qualities, O bringer of qualities, / O experiencer of qualities, O one delighting in qualities, O renouncer of qualities, homage to you!

178.s:
tvaṃ viṣṇus tvaṃ hariś cakrī tvaṃ jiṣṇus tvaṃ janārdanaḥ
tvaṃ bhūtas tvaṃ vaṣaṭkāras tvaṃ bhavyas tvaṃ bhavatprabhuḥ //
178.d:
त्वं विष्णुस् त्वं हरिश् चक्री त्वं जिष्णुस् त्वं जनार्दनः
त्वं भूतस् त्वं वषट्कारस् त्वं भव्यस् त्वं भवत्प्रभुः ॥
178.m: You are Viṣṇu, you are Hari, the discus-wielder; you are victorious, you are Janārdana; / you are the past, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the future, you are the Lord of what is becoming;

178.s:
tvaṃ bhūtakṛt tvam avyaktas tvaṃ bhavo bhūtabhṛd bhavān
tvaṃ bhūtabhāvano devas tvām āhur ajam īśvaram //
178.d:
त्वं भूतकृत् त्वम् अव्यक्तस् त्वं भवो भूतभृद् भवान्
त्वं भूतभावनो देवस् त्वाम् आहुर् अजम् ईश्वरम् ॥
178.m: You are the creator of beings, you are the unmanifest, you are existence, you support beings; / you are the originator of beings, the god; they call you the unborn Sovereign;

178.s:
tvam anantaḥ kṛtajñas tvaṃ prakṛtis tvaṃ vṛṣākapiḥ
tvaṃ rudras tvaṃ durādharṣas tvam amoghas tvam īśvaraḥ //
178.d:
त्वम् अनन्तः कृतज्ञस् त्वं प्रकृतिस् त्वं वृषाकपिः
त्वं रुद्रस् त्वं दुराधर्षस् त्वम् अमोघस् त्वम् ईश्वरः ॥
178.m: You are Ananta, you are grateful, you are nature, you are Vṛṣākapi; / you are Rudra, you are invincible, you are unfailing, you are the Sovereign;

178.s:
tvaṃ viśvakarmā jiṣṇus tvaṃ tvaṃ śaṃbhus tvaṃ vṛṣākṛtiḥ
tvaṃ śaṃkaras tvam uśanā tvaṃ satyaṃ tvaṃ tapo janaḥ //
178.d:
त्वं विश्वकर्मा जिष्णुस् त्वं त्वं शंभुस् त्वं वृषाकृतिः
त्वं शंकरस् त्वम् उशना त्वं सत्यं त्वं तपो जनः ॥
178.m: You are Viśvakarman, you are victorious, you are Śambhu, you have the form of a bull; / you are Śaṅkara, you are Uśanas, you are truth, you are asceticism, you are Janaloka;

178.s:
tvaṃ viśvajetā tvaṃ śarma tvaṃ śaraṇyas tvam akṣaram
tvaṃ śaṃbhus tvaṃ svayaṃbhūś ca tvaṃ jyeṣṭhas tvaṃ parāyaṇaḥ //
178.d:
त्वं विश्वजेता त्वं शर्म त्वं शरण्यस् त्वम् अक्षरम्
त्वं शंभुस् त्वं स्वयंभूश् च त्वं ज्येष्ठस् त्वं परायणः ॥
178.m: You are the conqueror of all, you are shelter, you are refuge, you are the imperishable; / you are Śambhu, and you are Svayambhū; you are the eldest, you are the supreme resort;

178.s:
tvam ādityas tvam oṃkāras tvaṃ prāṇas tvaṃ tamisrahā
tvaṃ parjanyas tvaṃ prathitas tvaṃ vedhās tvaṃ sureśvaraḥ //
178.d:
त्वम् आदित्यस् त्वम् ओंकारस् त्वं प्राणस् त्वं तमिस्रहा
त्वं पर्जन्यस् त्वं प्रथितस् त्वं वेधास् त्वं सुरेश्वरः ॥
178.m: You are the sun, you are the syllable Oṃ, you are breath, you are the dispeller of darkness; / you are the rain cloud, you are renowned, you are the creator, you are the lord of the gods;

178.s:
tvam ṛg yajuḥ sāma caiva tvam ātmā saṃmato bhavān
tvam agnis tvaṃ ca pavanas tvam āpo vasudhā bhavān //
178.d:
त्वम् ऋग् यजुः साम चैव त्वम् आत्मा संमतो भवान्
त्वम् अग्निस् त्वं च पवनस् त्वम् आपो वसुधा भवान् ॥
178.m: You are the Ṛg, the Yajur, and the Sāma; you are acknowledged as the Self; / you are Agni, and you are the wind; you are the waters; you are the earth;

178.s:
tvaṃ sraṣṭā tvaṃ tathā bhoktā hotā tvaṃ ca haviḥ kratuḥ
tvaṃ prabhus tvaṃ vibhuḥ śreṣṭhas tvaṃ lokapatir acyutaḥ //
178.d:
त्वं स्रष्टा त्वं तथा भोक्ता होता त्वं च हविः क्रतुः
त्वं प्रभुस् त्वं विभुः श्रेष्ठस् त्वं लोकपतिर् अच्युतः ॥
178.m: You are the creator, and likewise the enjoyer; you are the hotṛ-priest, the oblation, and the sacrificial rite; / you are the lord, you are all-pervading, the highest, you are the lord of the worlds, Acyuta;

178.s:
tvaṃ sarvadarśanaḥ śrīmāṃs tvaṃ sarvadamano 'rihā
tvam ahas tvaṃ tathā rātris tvām āhur vatsaraṃ budhāḥ //
178.d:
त्वं सर्वदर्शनः श्रीमांस् त्वं सर्वदमनो ऽरिहा
त्वम् अहस् त्वं तथा रात्रिस् त्वाम् आहुर् वत्सरं बुधाः ॥
178.m: You are all-seeing, glorious; you are the tamer of all, the slayer of foes; / you are day, and likewise night; the wise call you the year;

178.s:
tvaṃ kālas tvaṃ kalā kāṣṭhā tvaṃ muhūrtaḥ kṣaṇā lavāḥ
tvaṃ bālas tvaṃ tathā vṛddhas tvaṃ pumān strī napuṃsakaḥ //
178.d:
त्वं कालस् त्वं कला काष्ठा त्वं मुहूर्तः क्षणा लवाः
त्वं बालस् त्वं तथा वृद्धस् त्वं पुमान् स्त्री नपुंसकः ॥
178.m: You are time, you are the kalā, the kāṣṭhā, you are the muhūrta, the moments, and the seconds; / you are the youth, and likewise the elder; you are male, female, and neuter;

178.s:
tvaṃ viśvayonis tvaṃ cakṣus tvaṃ sthāṇus tvaṃ śuciśravāḥ
tvaṃ śāśvatas tvam ajitas tvam upendras tvam uttamaḥ //
178.d:
त्वं विश्वयोनिस् त्वं चक्षुस् त्वं स्थाणुस् त्वं शुचिश्रवाः
त्वं शाश्वतस् त्वम् अजितस् त्वम् उपेन्द्रस् त्वम् उत्तमः ॥
178.m: You are the source of all, you are the eye, you are immovable, you are Śuciśravas; / you are eternal, you are unconquered, you are Upendra, you are the highest;

178.s:
tvaṃ sarvaviśvasukhadas tvaṃ vedāṅgaṃ tvam avyayaḥ
tvaṃ vedavedas tvaṃ dhātā vidhātā tvaṃ samāhitaḥ //
178.d:
त्वं सर्वविश्वसुखदस् त्वं वेदाङ्गं त्वम् अव्ययः
त्वं वेदवेदस् त्वं धाता विधाता त्वं समाहितः ॥
178.m: You grant happiness to the entire universe, you are the Vedāṅgas, you are imperishable; / you are what is known through the Vedas, you are the creator, the ordainer, you are concentrated;

178.s:
tvaṃ jalanidhir āmūlaṃ tvaṃ dhātā tvaṃ punar vasuḥ
tvaṃ vaidyas tvaṃ dhṛtātmā ca tvam atīndriyagocaraḥ //
178.d:
त्वं जलनिधिर् आमूलं त्वं धाता त्वं पुनर् वसुः
त्वं वैद्यस् त्वं धृतात्मा च त्वम् अतीन्द्रियगोचरः ॥
178.m: You are the ocean to its depths, you are the sustainer, you are the Vasu; / you are the physician, and the steadfast self; you are beyond the reach of the senses;

178.s:
tvam agraṇīr grāmaṇīs tvaṃ tvaṃ suparṇas tvam ādimān
tvaṃ saṃgrahas tvaṃ sumahat tvaṃ dhṛtātmā tvam acyutaḥ //
178.d:
त्वम् अग्रणीर् ग्रामणीस् त्वं त्वं सुपर्णस् त्वम् आदिमान्
त्वं संग्रहस् त्वं सुमहत् त्वं धृतात्मा त्वम् अच्युतः ॥
178.m: You are the leader, you are the village chief, you are Garuḍa, you are the primal one; / you are the collection, you are the great intellect-principle, you are the steadfast self, you are Acyuta;

178.s:
tvaṃ yamas tvaṃ ca niyamas tvaṃ prāṃśus tvaṃ caturbhujaḥ
tvam evānnāntarātmā tvaṃ paramātmā tvam ucyate //
178.d:
त्वं यमस् त्वं च नियमस् त्वं प्रांशुस् त्वं चतुर्भुजः
त्वम् एवान्नान्तरात्मा त्वं परमात्मा त्वम् उच्यते ॥
178.m: You are the restrainer, and you are the rule; you are tall, you are four-armed; / you alone are the inner self of food; you are called the supreme self;

178.s:
tvaṃ gurus tvaṃ gurutamas tvaṃ vāmas tvaṃ pradakṣiṇaḥ
tvaṃ pippalas tvam agamas tvaṃ vyaktas tvaṃ prajāpatiḥ //
178.d:
त्वं गुरुस् त्वं गुरुतमस् त्वं वामस् त्वं प्रदक्षिणः
त्वं पिप्पलस् त्वम् अगमस् त्वं व्यक्तस् त्वं प्रजापतिः ॥
178.m: You are the elder, you are the highest teacher; you are left, you are right; / you are the holy fig tree, you are immovable; you are manifest, you are the lord of creatures.

178.s:
hiraṇyanābhas tvaṃ devas tvaṃ śaśī tvaṃ prajāpatiḥ
anirdeśyavapus tvaṃ vai tvaṃ yamas tvaṃ surārihā //
178.d:
हिरण्यनाभस् त्वं देवस् त्वं शशी त्वं प्रजापतिः
अनिर्देश्यवपुस् त्वं वै त्वं यमस् त्वं सुरारिहा ॥
178.m: You are the golden-naveled god; you are the moon; you are the lord of creatures; / you whose form is beyond definition; indeed, you are Yama; you are the slayer of the gods' enemies.

178.s:
tvaṃ ca saṃkarṣaṇo devas tvaṃ kartā tvaṃ sanātanaḥ
tvaṃ vāsudevo 'meyātmā tvam eva guṇavarjitaḥ //
178.d:
त्वं च संकर्षणो देवस् त्वं कर्ता त्वं सनातनः
त्वं वासुदेवो ऽमेयात्मा त्वम् एव गुणवर्जितः ॥
178.m: And you are the god Saṃkarṣaṇa; you are the creator; you are eternal; / you are Vāsudeva of immeasurable self; you alone are free of the guṇas.

178.s:
tvaṃ jyeṣṭhas tvaṃ variṣṭhas tvaṃ tvaṃ sahiṣṇuś ca mādhavaḥ
sahasraśīrṣā tvaṃ devas tvam avyaktaḥ sahasradṛk //
178.d:
त्वं ज्येष्ठस् त्वं वरिष्ठस् त्वं त्वं सहिष्णुश् च माधवः
सहस्रशीर्षा त्वं देवस् त्वम् अव्यक्तः सहस्रदृक् ॥
178.m: You are the eldest; you are the foremost; you are patient, and [you are] Mādhava; / thousand-headed are you, O god; you are the unmanifest, thousand-eyed;

178.s:
sahasrapādas tvaṃ devas tvaṃ virāṭ tvaṃ suraprabhuḥ
tvam eva tiṣṭhase bhūyo devadeva daśāṅgulaḥ //
178.d:
सहस्रपादस् त्वं देवस् त्वं विराट् त्वं सुरप्रभुः
त्वम् एव तिष्ठसे भूयो देवदेव दशाङ्गुलः ॥
178.m: thousand-footed are you, O god; you are the cosmic person; you are the lord of the gods; / you alone stand further, O god of gods, by ten fingers' width.

178.s:
yad bhūtaṃ tat tvam evoktaḥ puruṣaḥ śakra uttamaḥ
yad bhāvyaṃ tat tvam īśānas tvam ṛtas tvaṃ tathāmṛtaḥ //
178.d:
यद् भूतं तत् त्वम् एवोक्तः पुरुषः शक्र उत्तमः
यद् भाव्यं तत् त्वम् ईशानस् त्वम् ऋतस् त्वं तथामृतः ॥
178.m: Whatever has been, that indeed are you called—the supreme puruṣa, Śakra; / whatever is to be, that [too] are you, the ruler; you are truth, and likewise the immortal.

178.s:
tvatto rohaty ayaṃ loko mahīyāṃs tvam anuttamaḥ
tvaṃ jyāyān puruṣas tvaṃ ca tvaṃ deva daśadhā sthitaḥ //
178.d:
त्वत्तो रोहत्य् अयं लोको महीयांस् त्वम् अनुत्तमः
त्वं ज्यायान् पुरुषस् त्वं च त्वं देव दशधा स्थितः ॥
178.m: From you grows this world; you are the greater one, unexcelled; / you are the senior puruṣa, and you, O god, stand in tenfold form.

178.s:
viśvabhūtaś caturbhāgo navabhāgo 'mṛto divi
navabhāgo 'ntarikṣasthaḥ pauruṣeyaḥ sanātanaḥ //
178.d:
विश्वभूतश् चतुर्भागो नवभागो ऽमृतो दिवि
नवभागो ऽन्तरिक्षस्थः पौरुषेयः सनातनः ॥
178.m: Having become all beings, one quarter [lies here]; nine parts are immortal in heaven; / nine parts dwell in the intermediate space, belonging to the puruṣa, eternal.

178.s:
bhāgadvayaṃ ca bhūsaṃsthaṃ caturbhāgo 'py abhūd iha
tvatto yajñāḥ saṃbhavanti jagato vṛṣṭikāraṇam //
178.d:
भागद्वयं च भूसंस्थं चतुर्भागो ऽप्य् अभूद् इह
त्वत्तो यज्ञाः संभवन्ति जगतो वृष्टिकारणम् ॥
178.m: And two parts dwell on earth; a fourth part also existed here. / From you arise the sacrifices, the cause of rain for the world.

178.s:
tvatto virāṭ samutpanno jagato hṛdi yaḥ pumān
so 'tiricyata bhūtebhyas tejasā yaśasā śriyā //
178.d:
त्वत्तो विराट् समुत्पन्नो जगतो हृदि यः पुमान्
सो ऽतिरिच्यत भूतेभ्यस् तेजसा यशसा श्रिया ॥
178.m: From you the cosmic person was born, the puruṣa who is in the heart of the world; / he surpassed all beings in splendor, fame, and majesty.

178.s:
tvattaḥ surāṇām āhāraḥ pṛṣadājyam ajāyata
grāmyāraṇyāś cauṣadhayas tvattaḥ paśumṛgādayaḥ //
178.d:
त्वत्तः सुराणाम् आहारः पृषदाज्यम् अजायत
ग्राम्यारण्याश् चौषधयस् त्वत्तः पशुमृगादयः ॥
178.m: From you the food of the gods, the speckled clarified butter, was produced; / [and from you arose] domestic and wild medicinal plants, domestic beasts, wild animals, and the rest.

178.s:
dhyeyadhyānaparas tvaṃ ca kṛtavān asi cauṣadhīḥ
tvaṃ devadeva saptāsya kālākhyo dīptavigrahaḥ //
178.d:
ध्येयध्यानपरस् त्वं च कृतवान् असि चौषधीः
त्वं देवदेव सप्तास्य कालाख्यो दीप्तविग्रहः ॥
178.m: Intent on meditation upon the object of meditation, you also created the plants. / You, O god of gods, are seven-faced, named Time, of blazing bodily form.

178.s:
jaṅgamājaṅgamaṃ sarvaṃ jagad etac carācaram
tvattaḥ sarvam idaṃ jātaṃ tvayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam //
178.d:
जङ्गमाजङ्गमं सर्वं जगद् एतच् चराचरम्
त्वत्तः सर्वम् इदं जातं त्वयि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
178.m: Everything moving and unmoving, this entire world animate and inanimate— / from you all this was born, and in you all is established.

178.s:
aniruddhas tvaṃ mādhavas tvaṃ pradyumnaḥ surārihā
deva sarvasuraśreṣṭha sarvalokaparāyaṇa //
178.d:
अनिरुद्धस् त्वं माधवस् त्वं प्रद्युम्नः सुरारिहा
देव सर्वसुरश्रेष्ठ सर्वलोकपरायण ॥
178.m: You are Aniruddha; you are Mādhava; you are Pradyumna, slayer of the gods' enemies, / O god, supreme among all the gods, final refuge of all the worlds!

178.s:
trāhi mām aravindākṣa nārāyaṇa namo 'stu te
namas te bhagavan viṣṇo namas te puruṣottama //
178.d:
त्राहि माम् अरविन्दाक्ष नारायण नमो ऽस्तु ते
नमस् ते भगवन् विष्णो नमस् ते पुरुषोत्तम ॥
178.m: Protect me, O lotus-eyed one! O Nārāyaṇa, reverence to you! / Reverence to you, O Lord Viṣṇu! Reverence to you, O Puruṣottama!

178.s:
namas te sarvalokeśa namas te kamalālaya
guṇālaya namas te 'stu namas te 'stu guṇākara //
178.d:
नमस् ते सर्वलोकेश नमस् ते कमलालय
गुणालय नमस् ते ऽस्तु नमस् ते ऽस्तु गुणाकर ॥
178.m: Reverence to you, O ruler of all worlds! Reverence to you, abode of the lotus goddess! / Abode of virtues, reverence to you! Reverence to you, mine of virtues!

178.s:
vāsudeva namas te 'stu namas te 'stu surottama
janārdana namas te 'stu namas te 'stu sanātana //
178.d:
वासुदेव नमस् ते ऽस्तु नमस् ते ऽस्तु सुरोत्तम
जनार्दन नमस् ते ऽस्तु नमस् ते ऽस्तु सनातन ॥
178.m: O Vāsudeva, reverence to you! Reverence to you, best of the gods! / O Janārdana, reverence to you! Reverence to you, eternal one!

178.s:
namas te yogināṃ gamya yogāvāsa namo 'stu te
gopate śrīpate viṣṇo namas te 'stu marutpate //
178.d:
नमस् ते योगिनां गम्य योगावास नमो ऽस्तु ते
गोपते श्रीपते विष्णो नमस् ते ऽस्तु मरुत्पते ॥
178.m: Reverence to you, accessible to yogins! Dwelling place of yoga, reverence to you! / Lord of cattle, lord of Śrī, O Viṣṇu, reverence to you, lord of the Maruts!

178.s:
jagatpate jagatsūte namas te jñānināṃ pate
divaspate namas te 'stu namas te 'stu mahīpate //
178.d:
जगत्पते जगत्सूते नमस् ते ज्ञानिनां पते
दिवस्पते नमस् ते ऽस्तु नमस् ते ऽस्तु महीपते ॥
178.m: Lord of the universe, source of the universe, reverence to you, lord of the wise! / Reverence to you, lord of heaven! Reverence to you, lord of the earth!

178.s:
namas te madhuhantre ca namas te puṣkarekṣaṇa
kaiṭabhaghna namas te 'stu subrahmaṇya namo 'stu te //
178.d:
नमस् ते मधुहन्त्रे च नमस् ते पुष्करेक्षण
कैटभघ्न नमस् ते ऽस्तु सुब्रह्मण्य नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
178.m: Reverence to you, slayer of Madhu! And reverence to you, lotus-eyed one! / O slayer of Kaiṭabha, reverence to you! Very dear to the brahmins, reverence to you!

178.s:
namo 'stu te mahāmīna śrutipṛṣṭhadharācyuta
samudrasalilakṣobha padmajāhlādakāriṇe //
178.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते महामीन श्रुतिपृष्ठधराच्युत
समुद्रसलिलक्षोभ पद्मजाह्लादकारिणे ॥
178.m: Reverence to you, great Fish, O Achyuta who bore the Vedas on your back, / who churned the ocean waters, who brought delight to the lotus-born [Brahmā]!

178.s:
aśvaśīrṣa mahāghoṇa mahāpuruṣavigraha
madhukaiṭabhahantre ca namas te turagānana //
178.d:
अश्वशीर्ष महाघोण महापुरुषविग्रह
मधुकैटभहन्त्रे च नमस् ते तुरगानन ॥
178.m: O horse-headed one, great-snouted, having the bodily form of the Great Person, / slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, reverence to you, horse-faced one!

178.s:
mahākamaṭhabhogāya pṛthivyuddharaṇāya ca
vidhṛtādrisvarūpāya mahākūrmāya te namaḥ //
178.d:
महाकमठभोगाय पृथिव्युद्धरणाय च
विधृताद्रिस्वरूपाय महाकूर्माय ते नमः ॥
178.m: To you whose form is the great tortoise, who uplifted the earth, / whose essential nature bore the mountain—reverence to you, the Great Tortoise!

178.s:
namo mahāvarāhāya pṛthivyuddhārakāriṇe
namaś cādivarāhāya viśvarūpāya vedhase //
178.d:
नमो महावराहाय पृथिव्युद्धारकारिणे
नमश् चादिवराहाय विश्वरूपाय वेधसे ॥
178.m: Reverence to the Great Boar, who achieved the uplift of the earth; / and reverence to the Primordial Boar of universal form, the creator!

178.s:
namo 'nantāya sūkṣmāya mukhyāya ca varāya ca
paramāṇusvarūpāya yogigamyāya te namaḥ //
178.d:
नमो ऽनन्ताय सूक्ष्माय मुख्याय च वराय च
परमाणुस्वरूपाय योगिगम्याय ते नमः ॥
178.m: Reverence to the infinite, the subtle, the foremost, and the best; / to you whose nature is the atomic particle, accessible to yogins, reverence!

178.s:
tasmai namaḥ kāraṇakāraṇāya
yogīndravṛttanilayāya sudurvidāya
kṣīrārṇavāśritamahāhisutalpagāya
tubhyaṃ namaḥ kanakaratnasukuṇḍalāya
178.d:
तस्मै नमः कारणकारणाय
योगीन्द्रवृत्तनिलयाय सुदुर्विदाय
क्षीरार्णवाश्रितमहाहिसुतल्पगाय
तुभ्यं नमः कनकरत्नसुकुण्डलाय
178.m: Reverence to him, the cause of causes, / who abides in the state of the lords of yoga, very difficult to know, / who rests on the great serpent-son bed in the Ocean of Milk; / to you, who wear beautiful earrings of gold and jewels, reverence!

178.s:
vyāsa uvāca
itthaṃ stutas tadā tena prītaḥ provāca mādhavaḥ
kṣipraṃ brūhi muniśreṣṭha matto yad abhivāñchasi //
178.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्थं स्तुतस् तदा तेन प्रीतः प्रोवाच माधवः
क्षिप्रं ब्रूहि मुनिश्रेष्ठ मत्तो यद् अभिवाञ्छसि ॥
178.m: Vyāsa said: / Praised in this manner by him then, Mādhava, pleased, said: / “Speak quickly, best of sages, what you desire from me.”

178.s:
kaṇḍur uvāca
saṃsāre 'smiñ jagannātha dustare lomaharṣaṇe
anitye duḥkhabahule kadalīdalasaṃnibhe //
178.d:
कण्डुर् उवाच
संसारे ऽस्मिञ् जगन्नाथ दुस्तरे लोमहर्षणे
अनित्ये दुःखबहुले कदलीदलसंनिभे ॥
178.m: Kaṇḍu said: / “In this saṃsāra, O Lord of the Universe, difficult to cross, hair-raising, / impermanent, full of suffering, resembling the leaf of a plantain tree,

178.s:
nirāśraye nirālambe jalabudbudacañcale
sarvopadravasaṃyukte dustare cātibhairave //
178.d:
निराश्रये निरालम्बे जलबुद्बुदचञ्चले
सर्वोपद्रवसंयुक्ते दुस्तरे चातिभैरवे ॥
178.m: shelterless, supportless, unsteady as a water bubble, / full of all kinds of distress, impassable and exceedingly terrifying,

178.s:
bhramāmi suciraṃ kālaṃ māyayā mohitas tava
na cāntam abhigacchāmi viṣayāsaktamānasaḥ //
178.d:
भ्रमामि सुचिरं कालं मायया मोहितस् तव
न चान्तम् अभिगच्छामि विषयासक्तमानसः ॥
178.m: I wander for a very long time, deluded by your illusory power, / and find no end, my mind attached to sense objects.

178.s:
tvām ahaṃ cādya deveśa saṃsārabhayapīḍitaḥ
gato 'smi śaraṇaṃ kṛṣṇa mām uddhara bhavārṇavāt //
178.d:
त्वाम् अहं चाद्य देवेश संसारभयपीडितः
गतो ऽस्मि शरणं कृष्ण माम् उद्धर भवार्णवात् ॥
178.m: And today, afflicted by the fear of saṃsāra, O lord of gods, / I have gone to you for refuge, O Kṛṣṇa; rescue me from the ocean of worldly existence!

178.s:
gantum icchāmi paramaṃ padaṃ yat te sanātanam
prasādāt tava deveśa punarāvṛttidurlabham //
178.d:
गन्तुम् इच्छामि परमं पदं यत् ते सनातनम्
प्रसादात् तव देवेश पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥
178.m: I wish to go to that supreme, eternal abode of yours, / from which return is hard to occur, by your grace, O lord of gods!”

178.s:
śrībhagavān uvāca
bhakto 'si me muniśreṣṭha mām ārādhaya nityaśaḥ
matprasādād dhruvaṃ mokṣaṃ prāpyasi tvaṃ samīhitam //
178.d:
श्रीभगवान् उवाच
भक्तो ऽसि मे मुनिश्रेष्ठ माम् आराधय नित्यशः
मत्प्रसादाद् ध्रुवं मोक्षं प्राप्यसि त्वं समीहितम् ॥
178.m: The Blessed Lord said: / “You are my devotee, best of sages; worship me constantly. / By my grace you will surely attain the desired liberation.

178.s:
madbhaktāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ striyaḥ śūdrāntyajātijāḥ
prāpnuvanti parāṃ siddhiṃ kiṃ punas tvaṃ dvijottama //
178.d:
मद्भक्ताः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः स्त्रियः शूद्रान्त्यजातिजाः
प्राप्नुवन्ति परां सिद्धिं किं पुनस् त्वं द्विजोत्तम ॥
178.m: Devoted to me, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, women, śūdras, and those born of the lowest castes / attain supreme perfection—how much more so you, O best of the twice-born!

178.s:
śvapāko 'pi ca madbhaktaḥ samyak śraddhāsamanvitaḥ
prāpnoty abhimatāṃ siddhim anyeṣāṃ tatra kā kathā //
178.d:
श्वपाको ऽपि च मद्भक्तः सम्यक् श्रद्धासमन्वितः
प्राप्नोत्य् अभिमतां सिद्धिम् अन्येषां तत्र का कथा ॥
178.m: Even a dog-cooker who is devoted to me and endowed with complete faith / attains the desired perfection; what need be said of others in this regard?”

178.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evam uktvā tu taṃ viprāḥ sa devo bhaktavatsalaḥ
durvijñeyagatir viṣṇus tatraivāntaradhīyata //
178.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवम् उक्त्वा तु तं विप्राः स देवो भक्तवत्सलः
दुर्विज्ञेयगतिर् विष्णुस् तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
178.m: Vyāsa said: / Having spoken thus to him, O brahmins, that god who is affectionate to his devotees, / Viṣṇu, whose path is hard to comprehend, disappeared right there.

178.s:
gate tasmin muniśreṣṭhāḥ kaṇḍuḥ saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ
sarvān kāmān parityajya svasthacitto bhavat punaḥ //
178.d:
गते तस्मिन् मुनिश्रेष्ठाः कण्डुः संहृष्टमानसः
सर्वान् कामान् परित्यज्य स्वस्थचित्तो भवत् पुनः ॥
178.m: When he had departed, O best of sages, Kaṇḍu, with an overjoyed mind, / cast aside all desires and became tranquil in mind once more.

178.s:
sarvendriyāṇi saṃyamya nirmamo nirahaṃkṛtiḥ
ekāgramānasaḥ samyag dhyātvā taṃ puruṣottamam //
178.d:
सर्वेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य निर्ममो निरहंकृतिः
एकाग्रमानसः सम्यग् ध्यात्वा तं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
178.m: Restraining all his sense organs, free from possessiveness, devoid of egotism, / with single-pointed mind, meditating properly upon that Puruṣottama

178.s:
nirlepaṃ nirguṇaṃ śāntaṃ sattāmātravyavasthitam
avāpa paramaṃ mokṣaṃ surāṇām api durlabham //
178.d:
निर्लेपं निर्गुणं शान्तं सत्तामात्रव्यवस्थितम्
अवाप परमं मोक्षं सुराणाम् अपि दुर्लभम् ॥
178.m: who is taintless, devoid of guṇas, tranquil, abiding purely in pure existence, / he attained supreme liberation, difficult even for the gods to achieve.

178.s:
yaḥ paṭhec chṛṇuyād vāpi kathāṃ kaṇḍor mahātmanaḥ
vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ svargalokaṃ sa gacchati //
178.d:
यः पठेच् छृणुयाद् वापि कथां कण्डोर् महात्मनः
विमुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यः स्वर्गलोकं स गच्छति ॥
178.m: Whoever reads or hears the story of the great-souled Kaṇḍu, / freed from all sins, goes to the world of heaven.

178.s:
evaṃ mayā muniśreṣṭhāḥ karmabhūmir udāhṛtā
mokṣakṣetraṃ ca paramaṃ devaṃ ca puruṣottamam //
178.d:
एवं मया मुनिश्रेष्ठाः कर्मभूमिर् उदाहृता
मोक्षक्षेत्रं च परमं देवं च पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
178.m: Thus, O best of sages, has been described by me the land of ritual action, / the supreme field of liberation, and the god Puruṣottama.

178.s:
ye paśyanti vibhuṃ stuvanti varadaṃ dhyāyanti muktipradaṃ
bhaktyā śrīpuruṣottamākhyam ajaraṃ saṃsāraduḥkhāpaham //
178.d:
ये पश्यन्ति विभुं स्तुवन्ति वरदं ध्यायन्ति मुक्तिप्रदं
भक्त्या श्रीपुरुषोत्तमाख्यम् अजरं संसारदुःखापहम् ॥
178.m: Those who behold, praise, and meditate with devotion upon the all-pervading, boon-granting, / liberation-giving one named glorious Puruṣottama, ageless, who removes the suffering of saṃsāra:

178.s:
te bhuktvā manujendrabhogam amalāḥ svarge ca divyaṃ sukhaṃ
paścād yānti samastadoṣarahitāḥ sthānaṃ harer avyayam //
178.d:
ते भुक्त्वा मनुजेन्द्रभोगम् अमलाः स्वर्गे च दिव्यं सुखं
पश्चाद् यान्ति समस्तदोषरहिताः स्थानं हरेर् अव्ययम् ॥
178.m: Having enjoyed the pleasures of monarchs and spotless divine bliss in heaven, / they, freed from all faults, afterwards go to the imperishable abode of Hari.

179.s:
lomaharṣaṇa uvāca
vyāsasya vacanaṃ śrutvā munayaḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ
prītā babhūvuḥ saṃhṛṣṭā vismitāś ca punaḥ punaḥ //
179.d:
लोमहर्षण उवाच
व्यासस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा मुनयः संयतेन्द्रियाः
प्रीता बभूवुः संहृष्टा विस्मिताश् च पुनः पुनः ॥
179.m: Lomaharṣaṇa said: / Having heard the word of Vyāsa, the sages of restrained senses / were pleased, delighted, and repeatedly filled with wonder.

179.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
aho bhāratavarṣasya tvayā saṃkīrtitā guṇāḥ
tadvac chrīpuruṣākhyasya kṣetrasya puruṣottama //
179.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
अहो भारतवर्षस्य त्वया संकीर्तिता गुणाः
तद्वच् छ्रीपुरुषाख्यस्य क्षेत्रस्य पुरुषोत्तम ॥
179.m: The sages said: / Ah, you have proclaimed the virtues of Bhāratavarṣa, / and likewise, O Puruṣottama, of the sacred site named Śrīpuruṣa.

179.s:
vismayo hi na caikasya śrutvā māhātmyam uttamam
puruṣākhyasya kṣetrasya prītiś ca vadatāṃ vara //
179.d:
विस्मयो हि न चैकस्य श्रुत्वा माहात्म्यम् उत्तमम्
पुरुषाख्यस्य क्षेत्रस्य प्रीतिश् च वदतां वर ॥
179.m: For not merely of one was the wonder upon hearing the supreme majesty / of the sacred site named Puruṣa, and the delight, O best of speakers!

179.s:
cirāt prabhṛti cāsmākaṃ saṃśayo hṛdi vartate
tvadṛte saṃśayasyāsya cchettā nānyo 'sti bhūtale //
179.d:
चिरात् प्रभृति चास्माकं संशयो हृदि वर्तते
त्वदृते संशयस्यास्य च्छेत्ता नान्यो ऽस्ति भूतले ॥
179.m: And for a long time a doubt has dwelt in our hearts; / on earth there is no other dispeller of this doubt except you.

179.s:
utpattiṃ baladevasya kṛṣṇasya ca mahītale
bhadrāyāś caiva kārtsnyena pṛcchāmas tvāṃ mahāmune //
179.d:
उत्पत्तिं बलदेवस्य कृष्णस्य च महीतले
भद्रायाश् चैव कार्त्स्न्येन पृच्छामस् त्वां महामुने ॥
179.m: We ask you in full, O great sage, / about the birth of Baladeva and Kṛṣṇa, and of Bhadrā, upon the earth.

179.s:
kimarthaṃ tau samutpannau kṛṣṇasaṃkarṣaṇāv ubhau
vasudevasutau vīrau sthitau nandagṛhe mune //
179.d:
किमर्थं तौ समुत्पन्नौ कृष्णसंकर्षणाव् उभौ
वसुदेवसुतौ वीरौ स्थितौ नन्दगृहे मुने ॥
179.m: For what purpose were both Kṛṣṇa and Saṃkarṣaṇa born, / the two heroic sons of Vasudeva, and dwelt in Nanda's house, O sage?

179.s:
niḥsāre mṛtyuloke 'smin duḥkhaprāye 'ticañcale
jalabudbudasaṃkāśe bhairave lomaharṣaṇe //
179.d:
निःसारे मृत्युलोके ऽस्मिन् दुःखप्राये ऽतिचञ्चले
जलबुद्बुदसंकाशे भैरवे लोमहर्षणे ॥
179.m: In this mortal world, devoid of essence, full of suffering, extremely fickle, / resembling a water bubble, terrible, hair-raising—

179.s:
viṇmūtrapicchalaṃ kaṣṭaṃ saṃkaṭaṃ duḥkhadāyakam
kathaṃ ghorataraṃ teṣāṃ garbhavāsam arocata //
179.d:
विण्मूत्रपिच्छलं कष्टं संकटं दुःखदायकम्
कथं घोरतरं तेषां गर्भवासम् अरोचत ॥
179.m: slippery with feces and urine, painful, cramped, causing suffering— / how did that most dreadful dwelling in the womb please them?

179.s:
yāni karmāṇi cakrus te samutpannā mahītale
vistareṇa mune tāni brūhi no vadatāṃ vara //
179.d:
यानि कर्माणि चक्रुस् ते समुत्पन्ना महीतले
विस्तरेण मुने तानि ब्रूहि नो वदतां वर ॥
179.m: The deeds they performed when born upon the earth— / tell them to us in detail, O sage, best of speakers!

179.s:
samagraṃ caritaṃ teṣām adbhutaṃ cātimānuṣam
kathaṃ sa bhagavān devaḥ sureśaḥ surasattamaḥ //
179.d:
समग्रं चरितं तेषाम् अद्भुतं चातिमानुषम्
कथं स भगवान् देवः सुरेशः सुरसत्तमः ॥
179.m: Their entire deed is wonderful and superhuman. / How did that blessed god, lord of the gods, best of the gods,

179.s:
vasudevakule dhīmān vāsudevatvam āgataḥ
amaraiś cāvṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyakṛdbhir alaṃkṛtam //
179.d:
वसुदेवकुले धीमान् वासुदेवत्वम् आगतः
अमरैश् चावृतं पुण्यं पुण्यकृद्भिर् अलंकृतम् ॥
179.m: wise, come to the state of Vāsudeva in the family of Vasudeva? / And leaving the world of gods surrounded by immortals, holy, adorned by the meritorious,

179.s:
devalokaṃ kim utsṛjya martyaloka ihāgataḥ
devamānuṣayor netā dyor bhuvaḥ prabhavo 'vyayaḥ //
179.d:
देवलोकं किम् उत्सृज्य मर्त्यलोक इहागतः
देवमानुषयोर् नेता द्योर् भुवः प्रभवो ऽव्ययः ॥
179.m: why did he come here to the world of mortals— / he who is the leader of gods and humans, the imperishable source of heaven and earth?

179.s:
kimarthaṃ divyam ātmānaṃ mānuṣeṣu nyayojayat
yaś cakraṃ vartayaty eko mānuṣāṇām anāmayam //
179.d:
किमर्थं दिव्यम् आत्मानं मानुषेषु न्ययोजयत्
यश् चक्रं वर्तयत्य् एको मानुषाणाम् अनामयम् ॥
179.m: For what reason did he unite his divine self among humans, / he who alone turns the disease-free wheel of humans?

179.s:
sa mānuṣye kathaṃ buddhiṃ cakre cakragadādharaḥ
gopāyanaṃ yaḥ kurute jagataḥ sārvabhautikam //
179.d:
स मानुष्ये कथं बुद्धिं चक्रे चक्रगदाधरः
गोपायनं यः कुरुते जगतः सार्वभौतिकम् ॥
179.m: How did he set his mind on human existence, the bearer of the discus and mace, / he who provides universal protection to the world?

179.s:
sa kathaṃ gāṃ gato viṣṇur gopatvam akarot prabhuḥ
mahābhūtāni bhūtātmā yo dadhāra cakāra ca //
179.d:
स कथं गां गतो विष्णुर् गोपत्वम् अकरोत् प्रभुः
महाभूतानि भूतात्मा यो दधार चकार च ॥
179.m: How did that lord Viṣṇu, having gone to the earth, act as a cowherd— / he who, the self of all beings, held and created the great elements?

179.s:
śrīgarbhaḥ sa kathaṃ garbhe striyā bhūcarayā dhṛtaḥ
yena lokān kramair jitvā tribhir vai tridaśepsayā //
179.d:
श्रीगर्भः स कथं गर्भे स्त्रिया भूचरया धृतः
येन लोकान् क्रमैर् जित्वा त्रिभिर् वै त्रिदशेप्सया ॥
179.m: He who has Śrī in his womb—how was he held in the womb of an earth-dwelling woman— / he by whom, having conquered the worlds with three strides out of a desire [to help] the gods,

179.s:
sthāpitā jagato mārgās trivargāś cābhavaṃs trayaḥ
yo 'ntakāle jagat pītvā kṛtvā toyamayaṃ vapuḥ //
179.d:
स्थापिता जगतो मार्गास् त्रिवर्गाश् चाभवंस् त्रयः
यो ऽन्तकाले जगत् पीत्वा कृत्वा तोयमयं वपुः ॥
179.m: the paths of the world and the three aims of life were established; / he who, having drunk the world at the end of time, making his body of water,

179.s:
lokam ekārṇavaṃ cakre dṛśyādṛśyena cātmanā
yaḥ purāṇaḥ purāṇātmā vārāhaṃ rūpam āsthitaḥ //
179.d:
लोकम् एकार्णवं चक्रे दृश्यादृश्येन चात्मना
यः पुराणः पुराणात्मा वाराहं रूपम् आस्थितः ॥
179.m: turned the world into a single ocean through his visible and invisible self; / who, ancient, the ancient self, assuming the boar form,

179.s:
viṣāṇāgreṇa vasudhām ujjahārārisūdanaḥ
yaḥ purā puruhūtārthe trailokyam idam avyayam //
179.d:
विषाणाग्रेण वसुधाम् उज्जहारारिसूदनः
यः पुरा पुरुहूतार्थे त्रैलोक्यम् इदम् अव्ययम् ॥
179.m: the slayer of foes, lifted up the earth with the tip of his tusk; / who of old, for the sake of Puruhūta, having conquered this imperishable earth,

179.s:
dadau jitvā vasumatīṃ surāṇāṃ surasattamaḥ
yena saiṃhavapuḥ kṛtvā dvidhā kṛtvā ca tat punaḥ //
179.d:
ददौ जित्वा वसुमतीं सुराणां सुरसत्तमः
येन सैंहवपुः कृत्वा द्विधा कृत्वा च तत् पुनः ॥
179.m: gave the three worlds to the gods, the best of the gods; / by whom, having assumed a lion's form and split it in two,

179.s:
pūrvadaityo mahāvīryo hiraṇyakaśipur hataḥ
yaḥ purā hy analo bhūtvā aurvaḥ saṃvartako vibhuḥ //
179.d:
पूर्वदैत्यो महावीर्यो हिरण्यकशिपुर् हतः
यः पुरा ह्य् अनलो भूत्वा और्वः संवर्तको विभुः ॥
179.m: the primeval Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu of great valor was slain; / who of old, having become fire, the all-pervading Aurva fire of dissolution,

179.s:
pātālastho 'rṇavarasaṃ papau toyamayaṃ hariḥ
sahasracaraṇaṃ brahma sahasrāṃśusahasradam //
179.d:
पातालस्थो ऽर्णवरसं पपौ तोयमयं हरिः
सहस्रचरणं ब्रह्म सहस्रांशुसहस्रदम् ॥
179.m: standing in the netherworld, drank the water-formed ocean sap, Hari; / who is the thousand-footed Brahman, granter of a thousand rays,

179.s:
sahasraśirasaṃ devaṃ yam āhur vai yuge yuge
nābhyāṃ padmaṃ samudbhūtaṃ yasya paitāmahaṃ gṛham //
179.d:
सहस्रशिरसं देवं यम् आहुर् वै युगे युगे
नाभ्यां पद्मं समुद्भूतं यस्य पैतामहं गृहम् ॥
179.m: the thousand-headed god whom they indeed call age after age; / from whose navel arose the lotus, the house of the grandfather,

179.s:
ekārṇave nāgaloke saddhiraṇmayapaṅkajam
yena te nihatā daityāḥ saṃgrāme tārakāmaye //
179.d:
एकार्णवे नागलोके सद्धिरण्मयपङ्कजम्
येन ते निहता दैत्याः संग्रामे तारकामये ॥
179.m: the noble golden lotus in the single ocean, in the world of serpents; / by whom those Daityas were slain in the battle involving Tārakā;

179.s:
yena devamayaṃ kṛtvā sarvāyudhadharaṃ vapuḥ
guhāsaṃsthena cotsiktaḥ kālanemir nipātitaḥ //
179.d:
येन देवमयं कृत्वा सर्वायुधधरं वपुः
गुहासंस्थेन चोत्सिक्तः कालनेमिर् निपातितः ॥
179.m: by whom, having made a divine body bearing all weapons, / dwelling in the cave, the arrogant Kālanemi was brought down;

179.s:
uttarānte samudrasya kṣīrodasyāmṛtodadhau
yaḥ śete śāśvataṃ yogam āsthāya timiraṃ mahat //
179.d:
उत्तरान्ते समुद्रस्य क्षीरोदस्यामृतोदधौ
यः शेते शाश्वतं योगम् आस्थाय तिमिरं महत् ॥
179.m: who, having resorted to eternal yoga, sleeps in the great darkness / at the northern end of the ocean, the ocean of milk, the ocean of nectar;

179.s:
surāraṇī garbham adhatta divyaṃ
tapaḥprakarṣād aditiḥ purāṇam
śakraṃ ca yo daityagaṇāvaruddhaṃ
garbhāvadhānena kṛtaṃ cakāra
179.d:
सुरारणी गर्भम् अधत्त दिव्यं
तपःप्रकर्षाद् अदितिः पुराणम्
शक्रं च यो दैत्यगणावरुद्धं
गर्भावधानेन कृतं चकार
179.m: for whom Aditi, fire-stick of the gods, through the excellence of austerities, bore in her womb the divine, primeval [embryo], / and who, by taking up a womb, restored Śakra besieged by the hosts of Daityas;

179.s:
padāni yo yogamayāni kṛtvā
cakāra daityān salileśayasthān
kṛtvā ca devāṃs tridaśeśvarāṃs tu
cakre sureśaṃ puruhūtam eva
179.d:
पदानि यो योगमयानि कृत्वा
चकार दैत्यान् सलिलेशयस्थान्
कृत्वा च देवांस् त्रिदशेश्वरांस् तु
चक्रे सुरेशं पुरुहूतम् एव
179.m: who, having made his strides full of yoga, / cast the Daityas into the ocean's depths, / and having made the gods the lords of heaven, / made Puruhūta the lord of the gods;

179.s:
gārhapatyena vidhinā anvāhāryeṇa karmaṇā
agnim āhavanīyaṃ ca vedaṃ dīkṣāṃ samid dhruvam //
179.d:
गार्हपत्येन विधिना अन्वाहार्येण कर्मणा
अग्निम् आहवनीयं च वेदं दीक्षां समिद् ध्रुवम् ॥
179.m: who with the Gārhapatya rite, with the Anvāhārya ritual, / established the Āhavanīya fire, the Veda, initiation, the sacrificial fuel, the ladle,

179.s:
prokṣaṇīyaṃ sruvaṃ caiva āvabhṛthyaṃ tathaiva ca
avākpāṇis tu yaś cakre havyabhāgabhujas tathā //
179.d:
प्रोक्षणीयं स्रुवं चैव आवभृथ्यं तथैव च
अवाक्पाणिस् तु यश् चक्रे हव्यभागभुजस् तथा ॥
179.m: the sprinkling vessel, the dipping spoon, the concluding bath, / and with hands facing downward the eaters of the sacrificial shares;

179.s:
havyādāṃś ca surāṃś cakre kavyādāṃś ca pitṝn atha
bhogārthe yajñavidhinā 'yojayad yajñakarmaṇi //
179.d:
हव्यादांश् च सुरांश् चक्रे कव्यादांश् च पितॄन् अथ
भोगार्थे यज्ञविधिना ऽयोजयद् यज्ञकर्मणि ॥
179.m: and made the gods consumers of oblations, and then the ancestors consumers of ancestral offerings; / for enjoyment, according to the rule of sacrifice, he joined [them] in sacrificial action;

179.s:
pātrāṇi dakṣiṇāṃ dīkṣāṃ carūṃś colūkhalāni ca
yūpaṃ samit sruvaṃ somaṃ pavitrān paridhīn api //
179.d:
पात्राणि दक्षिणां दीक्षां चरूंश् चोलूखलानि च
यूपं समित् स्रुवं सोमं पवित्रान् परिधीन् अपि ॥
179.m: the vessels, the sacrificial fee, the initiation, the rice offerings, and the mortars, / the sacrificial post, the fuel, the dipping spoon, the soma, the purifiers, and the enclosing sticks,

179.s:
yajñiyāni ca dravyāṇi camasāṃś ca tathāparān
sadasyān yajamānāṃś ca medhādīṃś ca kratūttamān //
179.d:
यज्ञियानि च द्रव्याणि चमसांश् च तथापरान्
सदस्यान् यजमानांश् च मेधादींश् च क्रतूत्तमान् ॥
179.m: and the sacrificial articles, and similarly other cups, / the members of the assembly, the sacrificers, and the supreme sacrifices beginning with animal sacrifices—

179.s:
vibabhāja purā yas tu pārameṣṭhyena karmaṇā
yugānurūpaṃ yaḥ kṛtvā lokān anuparākramāt //
179.d:
विबभाज पुरा यस् तु पारमेष्ठ्येन कर्मणा
युगानुरूपं यः कृत्वा लोकान् अनुपराक्रमात् ॥
179.m: he who of old divided them through his supreme ritual action; / who, having arranged the worlds according to each yuga through his subsequent prowess,

179.s:
kṣaṇā nimeṣāḥ kāṣṭhāś ca kalās traikālyam eva ca
muhūrtās tithayo māsā dinaṃ saṃvatsaras tathā //
179.d:
क्षणा निमेषाः काष्ठाश् च कलास् त्रैकाल्यम् एव च
मुहूर्तास् तिथयो मासा दिनं संवत्सरस् तथा ॥
179.m: moments, blinks, kāṣṭhās, kalās, and the three divisions of time, / muhūrtas, lunar days, months, the day, and the year,

179.s:
ṛtavaḥ kālayogāś ca pramāṇaṃ trividhaṃ triṣu
āyuḥkṣetrāṇy upacayo lakṣaṇaṃ rūpasauṣṭhavam //
179.d:
ऋतवः कालयोगाश् च प्रमाणं त्रिविधं त्रिषु
आयुःक्षेत्राण्य् उपचयो लक्षणं रूपसौष्ठवम् ॥
179.m: the seasons, and the conjunctions of time, the threefold standard in the three [worlds], / lifespan, bodies, growth, auspicious marks, and beauty of form,

179.s:
trayo lokās trayo devās traividyaṃ pāvakās trayaḥ
traikālyaṃ trīṇi karmāṇi trayo varṇās trayo guṇāḥ //
179.d:
त्रयो लोकास् त्रयो देवास् त्रैविद्यं पावकास् त्रयः
त्रैकाल्यं त्रीणि कर्माणि त्रयो वर्णास् त्रयो गुणाः ॥
179.m: the three worlds, the three gods, the three Vedas, the three fires, / the three times, the three actions, the three castes, the three qualities—

179.s:
sṛṣṭā lokāḥ purā sarve yenānantena karmaṇā
sarvabhūtagataḥ sraṣṭā sarvabhūtaguṇātmakaḥ //
179.d:
सृष्टा लोकाः पुरा सर्वे येनानन्तेन कर्मणा
सर्वभूतगतः स्रष्टा सर्वभूतगुणात्मकः ॥
179.m: by whom, infinite, all the worlds were formerly created through action; / the creator abiding in all beings, consisting of the qualities of all beings,

179.s:
nṛṇām indriyapūrveṇa yogena ramate ca yaḥ
gatāgatābhyāṃ yogena ya eva vidhir īśvaraḥ //
179.d:
नृणाम् इन्द्रियपूर्वेण योगेन रमते च यः
गतागताभ्यां योगेन य एव विधिर् ईश्वरः ॥
179.m: and who delights through yoga preceded by the sense-organs of men; / who through the yoga of coming and going is indeed the ruling sovereign;

179.s:
yo gatir dharmayuktānām agatiḥ pāpakarmaṇām
cāturvarṇyasya prabhavaś cāturvarṇyasya rakṣitā //
179.d:
यो गतिर् धर्मयुक्तानाम् अगतिः पापकर्मणाम्
चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य प्रभवश् चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता ॥
179.m: who is the path of those endowed with dharma, and no path for evil-doers, / the origin of the four varnas and the protector of the four varnas,

179.s:
cāturvidyasya yo vettā cāturāśramyasaṃśrayaḥ
digantaraṃ nabho bhūmir vāyur vāpi vibhāvasuḥ //
179.d:
चातुर्विद्यस्य यो वेत्ता चातुराश्रम्यसंश्रयः
दिगन्तरं नभो भूमिर् वायुर् वापि विभावसुः ॥
179.m: who knows the fourfold knowledge, the refuge of the four stages of life, / the intermediate quarters, the sky, the earth, the wind, or fire,

179.s:
candrasūryamayaṃ jyotir yugeśaḥ kṣaṇadācaraḥ
yaḥ paraṃ śrūyate jyotir yaḥ paraṃ śrūyate tapaḥ //
179.d:
चन्द्रसूर्यमयं ज्योतिर् युगेशः क्षणदाचरः
यः परं श्रूयते ज्योतिर् यः परं श्रूयते तपः ॥
179.m: the light consisting of the moon and sun, the lord of the yuga, the night-wanderer; / who is heard of as the supreme light, who is heard of as the supreme austerity,

179.s:
yaṃ paraṃ prāhur aparaṃ yaḥ paraḥ paramātmavān
ādityānāṃ tu yo devo yaś ca daityāntako vibhuḥ //
179.d:
यं परं प्राहुर् अपरं यः परः परमात्मवान्
आदित्यानां तु यो देवो यश् च दैत्यान्तको विभुः ॥
179.m: whom they call the highest and the lowest, who is supreme, possessed of the supreme self; / who is the god of the Ādityas, and the all-pervading destroyer of the Daityas,

179.s:
yugānteṣv antako yaś ca yaś ca lokāntakāntakaḥ
setur yo lokasetūnāṃ medhyo yo medhyakarmaṇām //
179.d:
युगान्तेष्व् अन्तको यश् च यश् च लोकान्तकान्तकः
सेतुर् यो लोकसेतूनां मेध्यो यो मेध्यकर्मणाम् ॥
179.m: and who is the destroyer at the ends of yugas, and the destroyer of the destroyer of worlds; / who is the bridge of the bridges of the world, pure among pure deeds,

179.s:
vedyo yo vedaviduṣāṃ prabhur yaḥ prabhavātmanām
somabhūtaś ca saumyānām agnibhūto 'gnivarcasām //
179.d:
वेद्यो यो वेदविदुषां प्रभुर् यः प्रभवात्मनाम्
सोमभूतश् च सौम्यानाम् अग्निभूतो ऽग्निवर्चसाम् ॥
179.m: knowable to the knowers of the Veda, the lord of sovereign beings, / who has become the moon among the gentle, who has become fire among those of fiery splendor,

179.s:
yaḥ śakrāṇām īśabhūtas tapobhūtas tapasvinām
vinayo nayavṛttīnāṃ tejas tejasvinām api //
179.d:
यः शक्राणाम् ईशभूतस् तपोभूतस् तपस्विनाम्
विनयो नयवृत्तीनां तेजस् तेजस्विनाम् अपि ॥
179.m: who has become the ruler among the Indras, who has become austerity among ascetics, / the modesty of those of guided conduct, the splendor of the splendid—

179.s:
vigraho vigrahārhāṇāṃ gatir gatimatām api
ākāśaprabhavo vāyur vāyoḥ prāṇād dhutāśanaḥ //
179.d:
विग्रहो विग्रहार्हाणां गतिर् गतिमताम् अपि
आकाशप्रभवो वायुर् वायोः प्राणाद् धुताशनः ॥
179.m: He is the embodiment of those worthy of embodiment, the goal of those who move. / From space arises wind; from wind, through breath, comes fire;

179.s:
divo hutāśanaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇo 'gnir madhusūdanaḥ
rasāc choṇitasaṃbhūtiḥ śoṇitān māṃsam ucyate //
179.d:
दिवो हुताशनः प्राणः प्राणो ऽग्निर् मधुसूदनः
रसाच् छोणितसंभूतिः शोणितान् मांसम् उच्यते ॥
179.m: from heaven fire is the breath, and the breath is fire, Madhusūdana. / From chyle arises blood; from blood, meat is said to arise;

179.s:
māṃsāt tu medaso janma medaso 'sthi nirucyate
asthno majjā samabhavan majjātaḥ śukrasaṃbhavaḥ //
179.d:
मांसात् तु मेदसो जन्म मेदसो ऽस्थि निरुच्यते
अस्थ्नो मज्जा समभवन् मज्जातः शुक्रसंभवः ॥
179.m: from meat is the birth of fat; from fat, bone is stated [to arise]; / from bone, marrow arose; from marrow comes the origin of semen;

179.s:
śukrād garbhaḥ samabhavad rasamūlena karmaṇā
tatrāpāṃ prathamo bhāgaḥ sa saumyo rāśir ucyate //
179.d:
शुक्राद् गर्भः समभवद् रसमूलेन कर्मणा
तत्रापां प्रथमो भागः स सौम्यो राशिर् उच्यते ॥
179.m: from semen the embryo arose through action rooted in chyle. / There, the first portion of the waters is called the lunar mass;

179.s:
garbhoṣmasaṃbhavo jñeyo dvitīyo rāśir ucyate
śukraṃ somātmakaṃ vidyād ārtavaṃ pāvakātmakam //
179.d:
गर्भोष्मसंभवो ज्ञेयो द्वितीयो राशिर् उच्यते
शुक्रं सोमात्मकं विद्याद् आर्तवं पावकात्मकम् ॥
179.m: the second mass is to be known as arising from the embryo's heat; / one should know semen to be of the nature of Soma, and menstrual blood of the nature of fire.

179.s:
bhāvā rasānugāś caiṣāṃ bīje ca śaśipāvakau
kaphavarge bhavec chukraṃ pittavarge ca śoṇitam //
179.d:
भावा रसानुगाश् चैषां बीजे च शशिपावकौ
कफवर्गे भवेच् छुक्रं पित्तवर्गे च शोणितम् ॥
179.m: And their conditions follow the primary fluids, and in the seed are the moon and fire; / semen belongs to the class of phlegm, and blood to the class of bile.

179.s:
kaphasya hṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ nābhyāṃ pittaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
dehasya madhye hṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ tan manasaḥ smṛtam //
179.d:
कफस्य हृदयं स्थानं नाभ्यां पित्तं प्रतिष्ठितम्
देहस्य मध्ये हृदयं स्थानं तन् मनसः स्मृतम् ॥
179.m: The seat of phlegm is the heart; bile is situated in the navel. / The heart is in the middle of the body: that is remembered as the seat of the mind.

179.s:
nābhikoṣṭhāntaraṃ yat tu tatra devo hutāśanaḥ
manaḥ prajāpatir jñeyaḥ kaphaḥ somo vibhāvyate //
179.d:
नाभिकोष्ठान्तरं यत् तु तत्र देवो हुताशनः
मनः प्रजापतिर् ज्ञेयः कफः सोमो विभाव्यते ॥
179.m: Now, the space between the navel and the cavity: there resides the fire god. / Mind is to be known as the lord of creatures; phlegm is conceived as Soma;

179.s:
pittam agniḥ smṛtaṃ tv evam agnisomātmakaṃ jagat
evaṃ pravartite garbhe vardhite 'rbudasaṃnibhe //
179.d:
पित्तम् अग्निः स्मृतं त्व् एवम् अग्निसोमात्मकं जगत्
एवं प्रवर्तिते गर्भे वर्धिते ऽर्बुदसंनिभे ॥
179.m: bile is remembered as fire; thus the world consists of fire and Soma. / When the embryo is thus set in motion and developed into a mass,

179.s:
vāyuḥ praveśaṃ saṃcakre saṃgataḥ paramātmanaḥ
sa pañcadhā śarīrastho bhidyate vartate punaḥ //
179.d:
वायुः प्रवेशं संचक्रे संगतः परमात्मनः
स पञ्चधा शरीरस्थो भिद्यते वर्तते पुनः ॥
179.m: the wind, joined with the supreme self, entered it. / Existing in the body, it is divided fivefold and functions again:

179.s:
prāṇāpānau samānaś ca udāno vyāna eva ca
prāṇo 'sya paramātmānaṃ vardhayan parivartate //
179.d:
प्राणापानौ समानश् च उदानो व्यान एव च
प्राणो ऽस्य परमात्मानं वर्धयन् परिवर्तते ॥
179.m: prāṇa and apāna, samāna, udāna, and vyāna. / The prāṇa revolves, nourishing his supreme self;

179.s:
apānaḥ paścimaṃ kāyam udāno 'rdhaṃ śarīriṇaḥ
vyānas tu vyāpyate yena samānaḥ saṃnivartate //
179.d:
अपानः पश्चिमं कायम् उदानो ऽर्धं शरीरिणः
व्यानस् तु व्याप्यते येन समानः संनिवर्तते ॥
179.m: the apāna [nourishes] the lower body; the udāna, half of the embodied being; / that by which he is pervaded is the vyāna; the samāna turns inward.

179.s:
bhūtāvāptis tatas tasya jāyetendriyagocarā
pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam //
179.d:
भूतावाप्तिस् ततस् तस्य जायेतेन्द्रियगोचरा
पृथिवी वायुर् आकाशम् आपो ज्योतिश् च पञ्चमम् ॥
179.m: Then his acquisition of the elements, the objects of the senses, arises: / earth, wind, space, waters, and light as the fifth.

179.s:
tasyendriyaniviṣṭāni svaṃ svaṃ bhāgaṃ pracakrire
pārthivaṃ deham āhus tu prāṇātmānaṃ ca mārutam //
179.d:
तस्येन्द्रियनिविष्टानि स्वं स्वं भागं प्रचक्रिरे
पार्थिवं देहम् आहुस् तु प्राणात्मानं च मारुतम् ॥
179.m: Settled in his senses, they performed each its own share: / they declare the body to be made of earth, and wind to be the essence of breath;

179.s:
chidrāṇy ākāśayonīni jalāt srāvaḥ pravartate
jyotiś cakṣūṃṣi tejaś ca ātmā teṣāṃ manaḥ smṛtam //
179.d:
छिद्राण्य् आकाशयोनीनि जलात् स्रावः प्रवर्तते
ज्योतिश् चक्षूंषि तेजश् च आत्मा तेषां मनः स्मृतम् ॥
179.m: the cavities have their origin in space; from water comes secretion; / light forms the eyes and bodily radiance; the mind is remembered as their self.

179.s:
grāmāś ca viṣayāś caiva yasya vīryāt pravartitāḥ
ity etān puruṣaḥ sarvān sṛjaṃl lokān sanātanaḥ //
179.d:
ग्रामाश् च विषयाश् चैव यस्य वीर्यात् प्रवर्तिताः
इत्य् एतान् पुरुषः सर्वान् सृजंल् लोकान् सनातनः ॥
179.m: He through whose potency the senses and their objects were set in motion— / thus creating all these worlds, the eternal puruṣa:

179.s:
naidhane 'smin kathaṃ loke naratvaṃ viṣṇur āgataḥ
eṣa naḥ saṃśayo brahmann eṣa no vismayo mahān //
179.d:
नैधने ऽस्मिन् कथं लोके नरत्वं विष्णुर् आगतः
एष नः संशयो ब्रह्मन्न् एष नो विस्मयो महान् ॥
179.m: how did Viṣṇu come to human state in this mortal world? / This is our doubt, O holy one; this is our great wonder!

179.s:
kathaṃ gatir gatimatām āpanno mānuṣīṃ tanum
āścaryaṃ paramaṃ viṣṇur devair daityaiś ca kathyate //
179.d:
कथं गतिर् गतिमताम् आपन्नो मानुषीं तनुम्
आश्चर्यं परमं विष्णुर् देवैर् दैत्यैश् च कथ्यते ॥
179.m: How did the refuge of those who seek refuge attain a human body? / Viṣṇu is spoken of by the gods and demons as the supreme wonder.

179.s:
viṣṇor utpattim āścaryaṃ kathayasva mahāmune
prakhyātabalavīryasya viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ //
179.d:
विष्णोर् उत्पत्तिम् आश्चर्यं कथयस्व महामुने
प्रख्यातबलवीर्यस्य विष्णोर् अमिततेजसः ॥
179.m: Tell, O great sage, of the wondrous descent of Viṣṇu, / of renowned strength and valor, of Viṣṇu of boundless splendor.

179.s:
karmaṇāścaryabhūtasya viṣṇos tattvam ihocyatām
kathaṃ sa devo devānām ārtihā puruṣottamaḥ //
179.d:
कर्मणाश्चर्यभूतस्य विष्णोस् तत्त्वम् इहोच्यताम्
कथं स देवो देवानाम् आर्तिहा पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
179.m: Let the true nature of Viṣṇu, whose deeds are wondrous, be told here: / how is he the god of gods, the dispeller of distress, Puruṣottama,

179.s:
sarvavyāpī jagannāthaḥ sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ
sargasthityantakṛd devaḥ sarvalokasukhāvahaḥ //
179.d:
सर्वव्यापी जगन्नाथः सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः
सर्गस्थित्यन्तकृद् देवः सर्वलोकसुखावहः ॥
179.m: all-pervading, the lord of the universe, the great lord of all the worlds, / the god who effects primary creation, preservation, and dissolution, the bringer of happiness to all worlds,

179.s:
akṣayaḥ śāśvato 'nantaḥ kṣayavṛddhivivarjitaḥ
nirlepo nirguṇaḥ sūkṣmo nirvikāro nirañjanaḥ //
179.d:
अक्षयः शाश्वतो ऽनन्तः क्षयवृद्धिविवर्जितः
निर्लेपो निर्गुणः सूक्ष्मो निर्विकारो निरञ्जनः ॥
179.m: imperishable, constant, endless, free from decay and growth, / untainted, devoid of qualities, subtle, changeless, immaculate,

179.s:
sarvopādhivinirmuktaḥ sattāmātravyavasthitaḥ
avikārī vibhur nityaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ //
179.d:
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तः सत्तामात्रव्यवस्थितः
अविकारी विभुर् नित्यः परमात्मा सनातनः ॥
179.m: freed from all limiting adjuncts, abiding in pure existence alone, / immutable, all-pervading, eternal, the ancient supreme self,

179.s:
acalo nirmalo vyāpī nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ
viśuddhaṃ śrūyate yasya haritvaṃ ca kṛte yuge //
179.d:
अचलो निर्मलो व्यापी नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः
विशुद्धं श्रूयते यस्य हरित्वं च कृते युगे ॥
179.m: unmoving, stainless, omnipresent, eternally content, without support? / In the Kṛta age, his pure state of Hari is heard of,

179.s:
vaikuṇṭhatvaṃ ca deveṣu kṛṣṇatvaṃ mānuṣeṣu ca
īśvarasya hi tasyemāṃ gahanāṃ karmaṇo gatim //
179.d:
वैकुण्ठत्वं च देवेषु कृष्णत्वं मानुषेषु च
ईश्वरस्य हि तस्येमां गहनां कर्मणो गतिम् ॥
179.m: and his state of Vaikuṇṭha among the gods, and his state of Kṛṣṇa among men. / We desire to hear of this deep course of action

179.s:
samatītāṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca śrotum icchā pravartate
avyakto vyaktaliṅgastho ya eṣa bhagavān prabhuḥ //
179.d:
समतीतां भविष्यं च श्रोतुम् इच्छा प्रवर्तते
अव्यक्तो व्यक्तलिङ्गस्थो य एष भगवान् प्रभुः ॥
179.m: of that Lord—past and future! / He who is the unmanifest, dwelling within manifest marks, this blessed Lord,

179.s:
nārāyaṇo hy anantātmā prabhavo 'vyaya eva ca
eṣa nārāyaṇo bhūtvā harir āsīt sanātanaḥ //
179.d:
नारायणो ह्य् अनन्तात्मा प्रभवो ऽव्यय एव च
एष नारायणो भूत्वा हरिर् आसीत् सनातनः ॥
179.m: Nārāyaṇa, whose self is boundless, the source, and imperishable: / having become Nārāyaṇa, he was the eternal Hari.

179.s:
brahmā śakraś ca rudraś ca dharmaḥ śukro bṛhaspatiḥ
pradhānātmā purā hy eṣa brahmāṇam asṛjat prabhuḥ //
179.d:
ब्रह्मा शक्रश् च रुद्रश् च धर्मः शुक्रो बृहस्पतिः
प्रधानात्मा पुरा ह्य् एष ब्रह्माणम् असृजत् प्रभुः ॥
179.m: He is Brahmā, Śakra, Rudra, Dharma, Śukra, and Bṛhaspati. / Anciently, the Lord, whose essence is the pradhāna, created Brahmā;

179.s:
so 'sṛjat pūrvapuruṣaḥ purā kalpe prajāpatīn
evaṃ sa bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ
kimarthaṃ martyaloke 'smin yāto yadukule hariḥ //
179.d:
सो ऽसृजत् पूर्वपुरुषः पुरा कल्पे प्रजापतीन्
एवं स भगवान् विष्णुः सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः
किमर्थं मर्त्यलोके ऽस्मिन् यातो यदुकुले हरिः ॥
179.m: he, the primeval puruṣa, created the lords of creatures in a former kalpa. / Why, then, did that blessed Viṣṇu, the great lord of all worlds, / Hari, go into the mortal world into the family of Yadu?
